about:
The register of WeedJS's speed work, in two lists.

`hypotheses`: every speed hypothesis tested or planned, plus developer-experience todos (kind `dx`), one entry each: its status, a one-line result, its rank while it is pending, its records (`records`, by id) and links into the plan docs (`refs`).

`records`: every sitting, kernel run, gate and decision, with its date, its time when known, its verdict and its numbers in full. `timeFrom` says where a time comes from: `recorded` is when the record was written down, `commit` the time of a commit it names. The records up to 2026-10-24 were the rows of HYPOTHESIS_LOG.md and the WASM plan's results log; most of September's have no time, because they reached the log in batches.

A ref names a row of a doc, never a line: `EXECUTION_PLAN.md#E-82b` is the one row whose title is `E-82b` or holds it as a whole token (use the id, or the start of the title when the id finds several rows); a file name alone is the whole document.

Read it with `node scripts/hypotheses.mjs` (`find`, `show`, `log`) or as a page, `node scripts/buildHypothesesPage.mjs --open` (built locally, not committed). Add a record with `node scripts/hypotheses.mjs record`. Raw result files under tests/results are not kept: a record carries the numbers that decided it.

statuses.running: Being measured, or built and not yet measured.
statuses.blocked: Waiting on something outside the hypothesis.
statuses.kept: A speed keep: the primary got at least 3 % cheaper and nothing regressed.
statuses.kept-kernel: The kernel won; the product did not move (kept, product-neutral).
statuses.kept-hygiene: A fix or cleanup that stays because nothing got 3 % worse.
statuses.mixed: A split result: read the details.
statuses.screened: A sitting too thin to settle it.
statuses.dropped: Measured under the protocol and not 3 % cheaper (or worse): reverted.
statuses.rejected: Lost in the kernel, or its premise did not hold.
statuses.fail: The sitting did not count (floor, load, regime).
statuses.answered: A question or check that was answered (not a speed claim).
statuses.note: A campaign note: measurements without a verdict of their own.
statuses.passed: A gate that found no regression: a check on a batch, not a speed claim.

Kernel +117.5 % (25/25, Node); Chrome EMIT_MS 1.24 → 0.92 ms; Predator gate, 8 pairs: pre-render 5.054 → 4.666 ms, −4.6 %, worse 2/8 (spatial's +5.1 % flag did not reproduce in a same-build pair). Watched re-gate (2026-10-24, the stamp off): pre-render 5.407 → 5.255 ms, −5.2 %, worse 1/4.

The component columns, screened on the collect at 262 144 sprites: -0.7 to +3.3 % (C), -1.0 to +1.9 % (JS); not taken.
hypotheses.next: Each queue column a cache line after the last in renderQueueLayout; measure on a scene at an aliased capacity.

hypotheses.title: `copyTypeActiveListToBuffer` with `TypedArray.set`, re-sat on clean sides (Q1)

Two Predator sittings were called REGRESSION on spatial, renderer and particle (+3 to +4 %), which never run the copy, and no mechanism was found. Every worker moving the same way is drift or side bias (M13); read against those workers' median, logic was −1 % and 0 %. Under today's rule a kernel win whose scene is not 3 % worse is kept on its kernel.

hypotheses.title: `physics.wasmMemoryMB`: the developer chooses the size of Box2D's memory, per scene
hypotheses.result: Box2D's memory is sized per scene and stays fixed while it runs: the worker's name carries the size, the glue's pre-js creates the memory with initial = maximum, and the module's import accepts 16 MB to 2 GB. Running out shows an error that names the key; the stats and the memory panel publish the peak (sbrk). Survey of 25 runs: largest peak 89.7 MB (BallsHeavyStressScene), Predator 60.2 MB, so the default dropped to 128 MB and every shipped scene fits. Not timed: the .wasm code and data are byte-identical, and the per-step JS gained one export call.

hypotheses.title: A bigAtlas with more frames than MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE draws no sprite, silently: the texture LUT has one row per frame
hypotheses.statusText: found 2026-11-03 in Conurbano-weed (9 020 frames; SwiftShader's limit 8 192); fixed the same day (f47a2e86, R-0820)
hypotheses.result: The texture LUT keeps one frame a row up to 2048 (WebGL 2's promised MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE) and folds past it, K = ceil(N / 2048) frames a row, so neither side passes 2048 up to 1 396 736 frames; the 12 shaders fetch (3*(id % K), id / K). Below 2048 the texture is bit for bit the old one. Lockstep exact scenes 0 pixels differ, also forced folded; WebGPU folded draws (BunnyMark, GpuGalaxy, MeshGallery, BadPiggies, Predator).

hypotheses.title: Decorations: skewX and skewY, a shear of the sprite drawn in its facing
hypotheses.statusText: asked 2026-11-04 (Conurbano-weed: houses from flat pieces, one texture for every heading), done the same day (7ab3153), fixed in its review (N-116, 6ddf857c); kernels tie (R-0822); the scene pair under the floor and Predator neutral on the reference machine (R-0823)
hypotheses.result: skewX / skewY shear a decoration's scaled sprite about its anchor (x += skewX·y, y += skewY·x). Drawn in the facing as a shear sway was: baseRotC = rotC = skewMarkerC (1.5 + 0.49·skewY/(1+|skewY|)), rotS = skewX; the four sprite shaders read a cosine past 1.005 as a shear, skewY back with one division. A sheared decoration does not turn or sway and hangs unturned, so pre-render and the particle worker are unchanged and no pass reads the new columns. Kernels against main: attachedSway +8.7 % (code unchanged), attachedWalls -1.3 %, decorationCollectYSort -0.8 %: ties. hypotheses.next: Step 0: where main's input handlers run against the frame clock's vsync (the E-197 stamp and the frame clock). Then logic reads input once main has dispatched the frame's events (a word main writes, a budgeted wait), or main wakes the workers after its handlers. Owner: E-197's latency in Boids and Predator.

records.title: Keep set product confirm
records.text:
**Claim:** HASH + P2 + P6 + HYGIENE + COLLIDE (no PACT, no LIGHT), plus always-on load counts, is faster than `main` `0695a8d`.

**How:** Gameplay headed 5-run Balls + Predator; kernel Node emitFlat; detailed stats off; load ±5%

**Numbers:** Balls load OK (`BODY_COUNT` 9004 / 9004). Physics 6.911 → 6.554 ms (−5.2%), logic0 0.339 → 0.271 ms (−20.1%). Predator `BODY_COUNT` −0.1% but `ACTIVE_PARTICLES` 76.0 → 82.7 (**+8.8%**, cv ~75–80%): **pair does not exist**. Kernel emitFlat 7079 → 8570 ops/s (+21.1%).

**Why:** Product “faster than main” is false: Predator load missed ±5%. Balls-only would keep. P6 stays a kernel claim. HASH Predator spatial not confirmed on this keep set.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/product-confirm/report.md (not kept)`

records.title: 8 ms campaign floor
records.text: isolation campaigns that judge `STEP_MS` need a baseline median of at least 8 ms before a speed keep, worse, or tie. If that median cannot be reached, the verdict is **FAIL / no signal**. Hygiene may stay if no primary is 3 percent worse. Kernel ops/s does not use this floor. Skip-work rows B and C were already measured at the old 2 ms floor. Those sittings stay as written. See `[HOW_WE_MEASURE.md](./HOW_WE_MEASURE.md)`.

records.title: 3 ms stress floor
records.text: on a stress scene, if the millisecond primary is under 3 ms on either side, the pair is **FAIL**. Three percent of 0.3 ms is timer noise. Raise that scene's own load knob. The delta is not a keep and not a drop. Gameplay (Balls, Predator, `steadyCombatScene`, zenithal, catalog `kind: 'gameplay'`) skips this floor. Kernel `timeIt` uses the same 3 ms sample floor. Constant: `STEP_MS_FLOOR` in `[tests/bench/benchmarkDefaults.mjs](../../tests/bench/benchmarkDefaults.mjs)`. Hot-path hypotheses 1–9 on this branch were measured before the floor existed. Leave those historical verdicts as they are. A new question about the same idea, on today’s code, is a new pair under the current protocol.

records.title: Leftovers joint/parent/fixture
records.text:
**Claim:** Widens pairs/parent/entity to u32 when the flag is 32. Ids 65536+ do not alias.

**How:** Wrap 65536/70000; hunt leftover ≥8 ms.

**Numbers:** Pack 16+16 aliases B=65536→0. Two-column and `EntityIdArray` keep the id.

**Why:** Hygiene. Deco/particle/bullet pools stay 16.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/entity-id-width-best/report.md (not kept)`

records.title: NBR mixed stride
records.text:
**Claim:** Count u16 + ids u32 is ≥3% cheaper than homogeneous u32 ids at play 30k.

**How:** Kernel walk 30k and 300k.

**Numbers:** 30k +0.1% TIE; 300k +13%.

**Why:** Play ties. Compose stays homogeneous. CELL not-measured.

**Evidence:** `kernel-nbr-stride.json`

records.title: FL5 gen per slot
records.text:
**Claim:** Per-slot generation + CAS of the index is legal under contention.

**How:** Contention 4 workers, 80k pops.

**Numbers:** 6320 and 6437 double-handouts.

**Why:** Without DCAS it is ABA. Do not merge.

**Evidence:** `kernel-fl.json`

records.title: Uint32 vs Int32 (same width)
records.text:
**Claim:** `Int32Array` + sentinel −1 is ≥3% more ops/s than `Uint32` on lists, neighbors, or links.

**How:** Isolated kernel 30k and 300k, 3 ms floor, checksum.

**Numbers:** LIST 30k 56227 vs 27818; NBR 3674 vs 2366; links 300k tie.

**Why:** Int32 does not win. Champion `Uint32`. No bunny.

**Evidence:** `kernel-signed.json`

records.title: Sprites painter
records.text:
**Claim:** Sorting the queue by `sortKey` and a single blend lower `pixi_STEP_MS` ≥3% versus the double pass with Z, same queue.

**How:** Catalog 16k under 8 ms. Copy of `PainterSortStressScene` at 300000 (id cap 32). Headless 2×8/10 `--src`, detailed stats off. Load probe with stats on.

**Numbers:** Pixi 15.226 → 26.229 ms (**+72.3%**). Samples 14.698/15.754 vs 25.945/26.512. `VISIBLE_SPRITES` 300000. Both sides ≥ 8 ms.

**Why:** Reverted. The radix of 300000 does not pay for the second draw. The double pass stays.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/sprite-painter/report.md (not kept)`

records.title: Mesh movers only
records.text:
**Claim:** With the quiet revision, fill pose only for the entities on the list. Pixi ≥3% cheaper on a mixed one, and the all-moving does not worsen by 3%.

**How:** Kernel 2048 vs 5%. `MeshFillMixed` 6500 and `MeshFillMoving` 6500. 8/10 `--src` n=1.

**Numbers:** Kernel 15.7 → 382 ops/s. Mixed pixi 14.508 → 16.114 ms (**+11.1%**), `BODY_COUNT` 6500, moved 206 vs 335. All-spin 17.546 → 17.214 ms (−1.9%).

**Why:** The upload is still the whole VBO. `packMovedMeshes` stays false.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/moved-bodies/report.md (not kept)`

records.title: Pose movers only
records.text:
**Claim:** After a seed, copy only the dirty set to the double buffer. Physics ≥3% cheaper if many sleep, and Balls does not worsen by 3%.

**How:** Kernel 48k vs 5%. Balls heavy headless 8/10 `--src` n=1, detailed off.

**Numbers:** Kernel 64.9 → 83.7 ops/s (**+29%**). Physics 11.490 → 12.114 ms (**+5.4%**). `BODY_COUNT` 12004, moved 12000.

**Why:** On Balls everyone moves: the copy does not go down and the bookkeeping adds. `poseMoversOnly` stays false.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/moved-bodies/report.md (not kept)`

records.title: Neighbors dirty cells only
records.text:
**Claim:** Refresh neighbors of the mover and of whoever can see a cell whose membership changed. It lowers the step ≥3% with ~5% awake.

**How:** Kernel FN 0. `MovedBodiesMixedScene` 22k, 1100 teleports. 8/10 `--src` n=1.

**Numbers:** Spatial 11.108 → 13.637 ms (**+22.8%**). `BODY_COUNT` 22000, moved 1100/1100. Baseline ≥ 8.

**Why:** The oracle does not lie and the step does get worse. `dirtyNeighborRefresh` stays false.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/moved-bodies/report.md (not kept)`

records.title: Neighbors if nobody moved
records.text:
**Claim:** If the moved list is empty and the active set did not change, do not run the neighbor search. It lowers `spatial_STEP_MS` ≥3% on a static pile.

**How:** 60k static, vr 170. Headless 8/10 `--src` n=1. Gameplay headed Balls + steadyCombat, 5×25/18, detailed off.

**Numbers:** Stress 39.190 → 3.338 ms (**−91.5%**). Both ≥ 3 ms, baseline ≥ 8, `BODY_COUNT` 60000, moved 0. Balls physics 7.222 → 7.183 ms. Spatial 2.010 → 1.925. Logic0 0.392 → 0.415 ms (**+5.9%**). Logic samples 0.366–0.423 vs 0.361–0.430. `BODY_COUNT` 9004, moved 9000.

**Why:** Keep of the static scene. The default does **not** turn on: on Balls everyone moves and the logic0 median passes 3%. `skipIdleNeighbors` stays false.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/moved-bodies/report.md (not kept)`

records.title: Grid movers only
records.text:
**Claim:** Rewriting the grid with the Box2D list and local cells per entity lowers `spatial_STEP_MS` ≥3% if few move, and does not worsen by 3% if all move.

**How:** Kernel checksum 0/5/100%. Stress 60k static vr 0, and 22k awake vr 170. Headless 8/10 `--src` n=1, detailed off.

**Numbers:** Kernel 5%: 13.8 → 160 ops/s. 100%: 14.2 → 6.9 ops/s. Quiet stress 5.269 → 3.990 ms (−24%), `BODY_COUNT` 60000, moved 0. Baseline **< 8 ms**. Awake 15.274 → 13.922 ms (−8.9%), moved 22000/22000.

**Why:** FAIL / no signal on the quiet one (id cap 16). The −8.9% awake is n=1 and the code was supposed to do the full rebuild. Flag `incrementalMovers` stays false. Threshold 0.35.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/moved-bodies/report.md (not kept)`

records.title: Painter with movement
records.text:
**Claim:** One blend and reinserting only those that change Y does not come out ≥3% more expensive than the double pass, and it sorts. Radix and sort every 3 frames are compared in the same sitting.

**How:** `PainterMove*Scene`, N 300000, 10% cross a row. Headless 2×8/10 `--src`, detailed stats off. `off` first.

**Numbers:** off 30.648 ms (41.625/19.671, cv 51%). radix 38.310 (**+25%**). reinsert 30.051 (**−2%**). decimate 27.982 (**−8.7%**). All ≥ 8 ms.

**Why:** Reinsert stays. Speed tie, the blend is the reason. Decimate draws old order 2 of every 3 frames. Radix is not chosen. Default with Y-sort: `reinsert`.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/sprite-painter/move-report.md (not kept)`

records.title: Double queue `% 2`
records.text:
**Claim:** The buffer index `frame % 2` is ≥3% more ops/s if it is `& 1` or a bit that flips together with the `++`.

**How:** `docHypMod2Microbench.mjs`, 3 ms floor, checksum 4 in 8 steps. No scene.

**Numbers:** `% 2` 1513 Mops/s. `& 1` **+7.1%**. xor **+18.5%**.

**Why:** The writer uses the xor. Pixi and the shared frame use `& 1`. It is not `STEP_MS`: once per frame.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/mod2-index/report.md (not kept)`

records.title: H-VIS previous list
records.text:
**Claim:** Clearing `isItOnScreen` only for the visibles from the previous frame lowers `preRender_STEP_MS` ≥3% on bunny N=1.

**How:** Bunny 250k headed 8/10 `--src`, N=1, `skipCull`. No patch.

**Numbers:** preRender 23.686 ms, COLLECT 18.675, EMIT 5.017, queue 250000.

**Why:** All fit in the camera. The previous list writes the same as the `fill`.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/doc-hyp-hunt/report.md (not kept)`

records.title: H-NBR view lazy
records.text:
**Claim:** Not creating the neighbor view in `bind` does not make SpawnStorm ≥3% more expensive.

**How:** SpawnStorm 2×8/10 `--src`, baseline = H-HAS runs.

**Numbers:** logic0 10.593 → 10.391 (**−1.9%**). Samples 10.105/10.676.

**Why:** Hygiene. The storm tick does not read neighbors.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/doc-hyp-hunt/report.md (not kept)`

records.title: H-HAS flags per class
records.text:
**Claim:** One `_hasComponents` per class does not make `logic0_STEP_MS` ≥3% more expensive on SpawnStorm.

**How:** SpawnStorm headless 2×8/10 `--src`.

**Numbers:** logic0 10.519 → 10.593 (**+0.7%**). `ENTITIES_PROCESSED` 2001. Heap 3600/3641 vs 3642/3429.

**Why:** Hygiene. It is not a memory keep.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/doc-hyp-hunt/report.md (not kept)`

records.title: H-NCACHE neighbor cells
records.text:
**Claim:** Direct offsets or an interior/edge hybrid are ≥3% more ops/s than the hot `Map`.

**How:** `docHypNeighborCellsMicrobench.mjs`, 3 ms floor, checksum equal.

**Numbers:** Direct **−42.2%**. Hybrid **−0.9%**.

**Why:** The `Map` stays.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/doc-hyp-hunt/report.md (not kept)`

records.title: H-ROW / H-OWN spatial
records.text:
**Claim:** One index per row or one owned list lowers `spatialMax` ≥3% when the rebuild or the home-row skip dominate.

**How:** Hunt 30k and 300k, 8/10 `--src`, detailed stats. No patch.

**Numbers:** 30k rebuild 1.518 / step 10.409 (14%). 300k rebuild 13.235 / step 145.427 (9%); neighbor 132.182. Home-row skip 7.5% and 7.1%.

**Why:** There is no patch. The step is the neighbor. An index does not touch it.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/doc-hyp-hunt/report.md (not kept)`

records.title: H-TICKALL without scratch
records.text:
**Claim:** `tickAll` with stride, without compacting indexes, is ≥3% more ops/s.

**How:** `docHypTickAllMicrobench.mjs`, 3 ms floor, checksum equal. No stress.

**Numbers:** W=1 **+158.7%**, W=2 **+146.5%**, W=4 **+122.2%** ops/s.

**Why:** The signature in `src/` is not changed. MinimalTickAll at 60k is 0.622 ms; 8 ms does not fit in the useful cap.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/doc-hyp-hunt/report.md (not kept)`

records.title: H-BUCKET tickInterval
records.text:
**Claim:** With `staggeredUpdates`, visiting only the frame's phase lowers `logic0_STEP_MS` ≥3% versus the countdown, same writes of those that do tick.

**How:** `MinimalTickIntervalScene`. 60k 2×8/10 (floor of the fast side). 160k width 32, physics off, 8/10 n=1. Phase test in node.

**Numbers:** 60k 28.232 → 1.932 ms, visits 60000 → 15000 (fast side < 3 ms). 160k 77.540 → 4.732 (**−93.9%**), visits 160000 → 40000. Both sides ≥ 3 ms, baseline ≥ 8.

**Why:** Speed keep. Default on if there is no `CameraInOutListener` and no forced type. `tickBuckets: false` goes back to the countdown.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/doc-hyp-hunt/report.md (not kept)`

records.title: H-BLOCK logic by blocks
records.text:
**Claim:** With W≥2, contiguous ranges lower the max `logic*_STEP_MS` ≥3% versus the stride, and W=1 does not worsen by 3%.

**How:** MinimalTick headless 8/10 `--src`. W=2 and W=4: baseline from the hunt, then two runs. W=1 one hygiene run.

**Numbers:** W=2 max 15.762 → 14.686 (**−6.8%**; 14.130/15.242). W=4 max 9.416 → 8.203 (**−12.9%**; 8.083/8.322). W=1 27.101 → 26.704 (**−1.5%**).

**Why:** Speed keep on W=2 and W=4. The W baseline is n=1 from the hunt; the two new runs stay below.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/doc-hyp-hunt/report.md (not kept)`

records.title: H-AX skip accel without RigidBody
records.text:
**Claim:** Not writing `ax/ay/aa` on types without RigidBody lowers `logic0_STEP_MS` ≥3% at 60k ticks. It is not Visit pile.

**How:** `MinimalTickScene` headless 2×8/10 `--src`. Baseline first.

**Numbers:** logic0 27.101 → 29.382 ms (**+8.4%**). Samples 25.940/28.262 vs 28.253/30.511. `ENTITIES_PROCESSED` 60000.

**Why:** Reverted. The per-entity branch loses to three stores.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/doc-hyp-hunt/report.md (not kept)`

records.title: Doc+Doubao filter
records.text:
**Claim:** Stats padding, SoA hot/cold, instancing, `fround`, spatial sleep, hierarchical grid, query bitset, and worker WASM are new hyps.

**How:** Read of `src/` and of the log. No A/B.

**Numbers:** Stats already go to 64 B (`16*4`) and are written once per frame. `fround` does not change a store to a `Float32Array`. Cell sleep is H1 dropped. Instanced batch is already 15 floats.

**Why:** They are not reopened. The false sharing that matters is the tick stride, measured as H-BLOCK.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/doc-hyp-hunt/report.md (not kept)`

records.title: PreRender emit before the join
records.text:
**Claim:** If the count did not change, emitting on the cached prefix before the join lowers the max `preRender_STEP_MS` ≥3% on bunny 250k with 4 workers.

**How:** Same sitting, headed 5×25/18 `--src`, N=4. Baseline (join between collect and emit) first. Primary = max STEP.

**Numbers:** Baseline median 11.742 ms (10.283/11.562/11.742/12.236/13.444). Hyp 11.898 ms (**+1.3% TIE**; 11.094/11.391/11.898/12.021/12.087). Queue and `MARK_ACTIVE` 250000. Workers are even: `max(collect+emit)` does not drop below `max(collect)+max(emit)`.

**Why:** Reverted. It is not speed. Predator was not left on the rewrite path.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/prerender-early/ (not kept)`

records.title: Painter-sort: retire GPU two-pass
records.text:
**Claim:** A single Y-sort path (CPU painter + one blend) is correct for Predator/Adobe/shards, and does not worsen the step ≥3% versus reinsert already measured.

**How:** Unit (`renderQueueSortPaths`, PMA, persist type 6). Permanent stress: `painterShardedStressScene.js` (2 workers) + `painterAdobeStressScene.js` (type 6). Hygiene, no speed A/B — the two-pass was already a tie vs reinsert at 300k.

**Numbers:** No new `STEP_MS`. The speed keep is still the reinsert vs two-pass one (30.1 vs 30.6 ms). This row is correction + delete.

**Why:** Deleted `entitiesParticleBatch`, `coverageMesh`, `BATCH_DEPTH.SORT_KEY`. `_uploadSortedSprites` serves ENTITIES and custom layers. Persist does not write over an expanded queue. `renderer.painterSort` **was retired:** `ySorting` turns on reinsert; `radix`/`decimate`/`off` are no longer API.

**Evidence:** `[docs/DEVLOG.md](./DEVLOG.md)`

records.title: Painter-sort: custom layers + sharding
records.text:
**Claim:** It is not a speed hyp — real bug investigation. `createPainterState`/`painterSameSet`/`radixPainterOrder`/`orderPainterSlots` (new, `sortIndexByKey.js`) generalize the main queue painter to a dense set without filtering (`idxE=null`, the shape a custom layer needs) and to a `count` that stays the same while the split between pre-render workers moves down.

**How:** Unit tests (`sortIndexByKey.test.js`, dense case with a changing count and values mixed at the same count). New stress scene `painterShardedStressScene.js` (2 pre-render workers, `skipCull:false`, drift crosses the camera edge). Headless smoke 20000 sprites, frames 200/201/205/209.

**Numbers:** No `STEP_MS` — correction, not speed. Unit tests pass. Visual smoke with no z-order corruption between adjacent frames.

**Why:** Sharding does not reproduce the Predator bug by itself. Persist + Adobe (type 6) is a real write-index bug; `_type0PersistHit` now aborts if there is type 6. The GPU two-pass was retired: one painter, ENTITIES = sprite layer, `'off'` = reinsert. Predator no longer pins `'off'`.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/painter-shard-coverage/report.md (not kept)`

records.title: useZBuffer, one pass
records.text:
**Claim:** `renderer.useZBuffer` (default false) skips the painter and writes the Y key into Z. In Predator the step drops ≥3% with the same fight. A single cut at 1/255.

**How:** Predator headed 8/10 `--src` n=1, detailed stats on. CPU first, then the flag, and it is reverted. Captures 8/3 aside.

**Numbers:** Step 10.650 → 5.830 ms. `SORT_MS` 2.209 → 0. Upload 5.383 → 2.373. Present 0.442 → 0.798. Visible sprites 36880 → 37126. Bodies 16638 → 16757. Particles 112 → 231.

**Why:** No keep: the particles do not match. The knob stays, default off. The renderer's `ySorting` is renamed to `ySortingInCPU`.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/use-zbuffer/report.md (not kept)`

records.title: Two instance buffers
records.text:
**Claim:** Uploading the VBO to a buffer the GPU is not reading lowers `SPRITES_MS` of the frames with a queue ≥3% on Bunny, and the Pixi step does not worsen ≥3%.

**How:** Bunny 250k headed 8/10 `--src` n=1, detailed stats on, on top of the dense upload. Baseline first. `MARK_ACTIVE` 250000.

**Numbers:** Upload 9.921 → 9.326 ms (−6.0%, 84 and 88 samples). Step 13.337 → 13.530 (+1.4%). `VISIBLE_SPRITES` 250000.

**Why:** Keep. It is not a Pixi fork: two `Buffer` and the geometry alternates.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/sprites-ms-hyps/report.md (not kept)`

records.title: lightGlow sprite versus add
records.text:
**Claim:** In Predator, sprite mode lowers `SPRITES_MS` ≥3% versus the ADD batch, same fight.

**How:** Smoke headed 8/10 `--src` n=1, sprite first.

**Numbers:** Sprites 5.168 vs 6.660. Step 10.382 vs 11.171. `ACTIVE_PARTICLES` 168 vs 215. Moved 3342 vs 6891.

**Why:** No keep. The knob stays. Default `add`. The glow queue is not built.

**Evidence:** same report

records.title: Dense upload without Y-sort or lights
records.text:
**Claim:** If there is no painter and lighting is off, do not build `idxE` or search for type 3. `SPRITES_MS` of the frames with a queue drops ≥3% and the Pixi step does not worsen ≥3%.

**How:** Bunny 250k headed 8/10 `--src` n=1, detailed stats on. Baseline first. `MARK_ACTIVE` 250000/250000.

**Numbers:** Upload 11.134 → 10.611 ms (−4.7%, 86 and 91 samples). Step 14.851 → 15.173 (+2.2%).

**Why:** Keep for the pack. The step is not a win.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/sprites-ms-hyps/report.md (not kept)`

records.title: Sort by Y bands
records.text:
**Claim:** Each pre-render sorts a Y band and the one that publishes concatenates. Pixi does not sort. It lowers `pixi_STEP_MS` ≥3% and the pre-render max does not rise ≥3%.

**How:** Kernel 300k, bands with no overlap, checksum = single sort. Same headed PainterMove run (21.924 / 5.165 / 10.727). No grid, no particles.

**Numbers:** Band 150k 1.069 ms, concat 0.300 ms. Pixi without sort 16.759 ms (−23.6%). Pre-render 12.097 ms (+12.8%). k=4: band 1.004, concat 0.266, pre-render 11.997 (+11.8%).

**Why:** NO-GO. Concatenating is cheap. The band sort exceeds the pre-render +3%.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/prerender-sort-gonogo/yband-report.md (not kept)`

records.title: Sort in pre-render
records.text:
**Claim:** Each span is sorted with `orderPainterSlots` and the one that publishes does a k-way. Pixi lowers `STEP_MS` ≥3% and the pre-render max does not rise ≥3%.

**How:** Kernel 300k, k=2 and k=4, checksum = single sort. `PainterMoveReinsertScene` headed 8/10 `--src` n=1, detailed stats on. No SAB.

**Numbers:** Pixi 21.924 ms, `SORT_MS` 5.165 (23.6%). Pre-render 10.727, `SORT_MS` 0. Queue 300000. Merge k=2 8.06 ms, k=4 12.71 ms. Span reinsert 1.22 / 1.05 ms.

**Why:** NO-GO. The merge alone already passes the pre-render +3% (10.7 + 8.1). `painterIndex` is not written.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/prerender-sort-gonogo/report.md (not kept)`

records.title: Pixi Buffer.update without copy
records.text:
**Claim:** `Buffer.update` copies the `Float32Array` before uploading it.

**How:** Read of Pixi 8.20.1 `GlBufferSystem.updateBuffer` and `GpuBufferSystem.updateBuffer`. No patch, no scene.

**Numbers:** WebGL `bufferSubData` on `buffer.data`. WebGPU `writeBuffer` on `data.buffer`. `fastCopy` only on create.

**Why:** There is no fork.

**Evidence:** same report

records.title: sortKey ordinal
records.text:
**Claim:** Precomputing `floatBitsToOrd` once lowers reinsert ≥3% ops/s and `pixi_STEP_MS` ≥3% on PainterMove.

**How:** Kernel checksum equal, n=300000, 10% moved. Separate stress, on top of the quantized key, 2×8/10 `--src`.

**Numbers:** Kernel 170.6 → 181.6 ops/s (**+6.4%**). Pixi 24.355 → 24.618/29.693 (median 27.156, **+11.5%**). Both ≥8 ms. Glow: radix at 256 is 0.33 of reinsert's ops/s (~0.01 ms per pass).

**Why:** Reverted. The array does not stay. There is no glow painter.

**Evidence:** same report

records.title: Y tie-break by id
records.text:
**Claim:** `(id % 127 + 1) / 256` keeps the same-pixel tie stable when the queue is repacked, and does not make pixi ≥3% more expensive.

**How:** Unit: a queue that grows to the left reverses the order. Stress against the quantized median, 2×8/10 plus one confirmation.

**Numbers:** Pixi 24.355 → 50.850/50.423 (median 50.637, **+108%**). Confirm 63.497. Pre-render 0.005 ms (backpressure skip, **<3 ms**).

**Why:** Reverted. The same-pixel tie stays.

**Evidence:** same report

records.title: Integer-pixel Y key
records.text:
**Claim:** `Math.round(pose.y) * 128` on type 0 and 6 keeps reinsert quiet against a jitter <0.5 px, and does not make `pixi_STEP_MS` ≥3% more expensive on PainterMove.

**How:** Kernel n=300000, 10% ±0.2 px. `PainterMoveReinsertScene` headless 2×8/10 `--src`, detailed off. Baseline first.

**Numbers:** Kernel 205 → 1985 ops/s. Quantized moves 0 slots; raw moves 30000. Pixi 23.593/24.040 → 23.212/25.497 (median 23.817 → 24.355, **+2.3%**). Both ≥8 ms. Pre-render median 5.191 → 3.280, baseline **<8 ms**.

**Why:** Bugfix. It is not a speed keep. N is not raised: pixi already passes 16 ms.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/ysort-quantize/report.md (not kept)`

records.title: Predator `lighting.resolution=0.25`
records.text:
**Claim:** Against resolution 1, the GPU step falls ≥3 % at both zooms.

**How:** Screening n=1 `hour=0` `shadowLights=48`. Primary `GPU_STEP_MS`.

**Numbers:** 7.821→4.459 (−43 %) and 13.406→5.526 (−59 %). Present 7.654→3.694 and 13.308→4.849. `GPU_LIGHTS` 0→0.57 (at res 1 the mesh went to present). Bodies ±0.1 %. Pixi far +9.7 %.

**Why:** Predator 1→0.25. Engine is not touched. Softer look. No confirm.

**Evidence:** same report

records.title: `gpuShadowPath=batch`
records.text:
**Claim:** One cookie draw and one caster draw, same filtered list as `copy`, lowers Pixi ≥3 % at both zooms without spiking `GPU_SHADOWS_MS`.

**How:** Predator screening `--src` 3 s/5 s n=1 `hour=0`, zoom 1.5 and 0.4, `shadowLights=48`.

**Numbers:** Pixi 10.566→10.503 (−0.6 %) and 11.661→12.928 (**+10.9 %**). Passes 41→2 and 33→1.3. GPU shadows 0.18→0.15 and 0.10→0.12. Bodies ±0.8 %.

**Why:** Drop as default. The buffer stamp eats the savings. Knob `batch` stays.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/render-hyps/campaign-lights-shadows.md (not kept)`

records.title: CPU shadows (`main`) vs GPU (branch)
records.text:
**Claim:** In Predator, the CPU shadow queue is more expensive than drawing the sun and the lights in the shader.

**How:** `--src`. Predator headed 2×3 s/5 s. `main` `f8cb00a` first, worktree, then this branch.

**Numbers:** Pre-render 20.4/20.2 and 18.3/18.3 vs 11.1/11.1 and 11.3/11.3. `SHADOW_Q_MS` ~7 vs 0.02. Pixi 10.5/10.8 vs 12.1/12.5. Bodies ~18000.

**Why:** Stays. Pre-render drops ~8 ms. Pixi rises ~1.5 and does not eat the savings. There is no kernel: the path is workers.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/render-hyps/cpu-vs-gpu.md (not kept)`

records.title: Z clip on the zIndex bands in use
records.text:
**Claim:** The z-buffer sorts the same foot as the painter, also with an anchor, without walking the queue. The Predator renderer does not read as more expensive: the key sweep and the band give the same median.

**How:** Node (span 65536 vs one band). Headed pixel painter vs `useZBuffer`. Predator `--src` 5×25/18, detailed stats off. Old span, sweep, band.

**Numbers:** Float32 smears 1 px and 5 px on the old span. On screen those two come to match the painter. Renderer 9.992 / 10.563 / 10.558. Bodies 16630 vs 16611. Physics and logic also rise in the third sitting.

**Why:** Order hygiene. It is not a speed keep. `anchorX` without rotation stays a key tie.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/gpu-ysort/report.md (not kept)`

records.title: Shadows under 2 px
records.text:
**Claim:** A screen-height filter lowers `SHADOWS_MS` ≥3 % without emptying the casters.

**How:** Screening n=1, `copy`, `lightingRes=0.25`.

records.title: Cookies every frame with interval 2

records.text:

**Why:** It stays. The bench did not pan by eye. If it still slides when the camera moves, the next hyp is snap to the coarse pixel, not another caster path.

records.title: `shadowUpdateInterval=2` (hold `shadowRT`)

records.title: Lights in a texture, shadows on both backends
records.text:

records.title: useZBuffer on Bunny

records.title: Caster copy without `subarray` per row
records.text:

records.title: Stamp dirty with moved bodies
records.text:
**Claim:** Sun/stamp cache per `entityIndex` (generation+pose, without `poseSkip`) lowers the pole ≥3 % when the sharded pack did not pay.

**How:** Same sitting, pack again on the publisher, vs HEAD `25fb0c0`.

**Numbers:** N=2 pole 6.617→9.098 (**+37.5 %**) and 15.193→21.033 (**+38.4 %**). Lights/cookies 12.0→5.5 and 10.2→4.7. N=1 pole 7.060→8.914 and 15.246→20.966. Bodies ±0.6 %.

records.title: Stamp on each shard (z-buffer, N=2)
records.text:
**Claim:** Sun+stamp pack per pre-render and compact 512 on the join lowers the pole ≥3 % in Predator night, zoom 1.5 and 0.4.

**How:** Headed `--src` 3 s/5 s n=1 vs HEAD `25fb0c0`. `hour=0`, N=2 keep, N=1 control.

**Numbers:** N=2 pole 7.059→10.703 (**+51.6 %**) and 14.333→15.600 (**+8.8 %**). Casters 4657/4516 and 13195/13425. Lights 12→43 and 35→45 (influence). Bodies ±1.1 %. An A/B with `GPU_CASTERS=0` does not count (`_dummyCount` shared).

**Why:** Drop of the sharded pack: the publisher again weaves the joined SoA. One shadow per Adobe entity stays and the range = influence if `visualRange` is 0. `_emitWriteCount` stays.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/render-hyps/shard-stamp/report.md (not kept)`

records.title: WebGPU `collectGpuStats` + readback
records.text:
**Claim:** `debug.collectGpuStats` (default off) turns on timestamp-query. `finishFrame` resolves a single sample; until the unmap there are no timestamps and no other submit. Bitonic sums all the compute passes.

**How:** Hygiene. Gate headed Predator + F5 with the flag on. `test:node` `gpuFrameTimer.test.js`.

**Numbers:** Gate: `GPU_TIMER=1`, `GPU_STEP_MS` 13.1, `GPU_SORT_MS` 12.6 (8 s/8 s). Sitting 5×25/18: snapshot `GPU_STEP` 7.653 / `GPU_SORT` 6.440.

**Why:** Hygiene. The normal game does not pay for resolve. The bench does not change the default; this campaign passes `--collect-gpu-stats`. `GPU_LIGHTS` / `GPU_PRESENT` stay 0 (Dawn often does not write the end). It is not a speed claim. 2026-10-01: the 2026-09-25 contract (do not abort stamps with MAP_READ pending) rewrote the query set and hung the GPU process in Predator; from this date WebGPU measures one frame and waits for the unmap. Zoom in Predator likewise hung the process: the next sample went back to timestamping the shadows. Since then the shadows carry no timestamp and there are 45 frames of wait after each unmap. 2026-10-01 night: the fast zoom hung the same way with the debug UI closed, because the scene flag still arms the timer. WebGPU no longer arms timestamp queries. The GPU clock was removed: timestamps and onSubmittedWorkDone hang the Chrome process and no error arrives. The GPU row stays on Passes, Casters, and ShadowLights.

**Evidence:** `src/render/gpuFrameTimer.js`

records.title: Windows by id with no wait
records.text:
**Claim:** Each preRender sorts its block, writes AoS into a fixed window, and does not wait for the sibling. Pixi mixes by key. The max falls ≥3 % vs the join in Predator far, N=2, and Pixi does not rise ≥3 %.

**How:** Headed screening 3 s/7 s `--src` `hour=0&zoom=0.4&preRenderWorkers=2`, detail on. Reverted to the join.

**Numbers:** preRender 216.4 and 41.3 (the second hung). Pixi 2.737 with visible entities 9559 and casters 0. It is not the same frame as the join (23 ms, live casters).

**Why:** The clone of the private SoA of the whole queue eats the first frame and one worker does not continue. It is not left in. The sortKey bands were not built separately: the cost was in the preRender, not in the merge.

**Evidence:** same report

records.title: PreRender N=2/4 join, far
records.text:
**Claim:** With today's join, 2 and 4 workers each lower the max `preRender_STEP_MS` ≥3 %, and Pixi does not rise ≥3 %, in Predator far.

**How:** Same sitting as the deletion. Headed 3 s/7 s `--src`, detail on. N=1 then N=2 then N=4.

**Numbers:** N=1 22.755 / Pixi 4.808. N=2 max 23.152 (+1.7 %), Pixi 5.390 (+12 %). N=4 max 20.951 (−7.9 %), Pixi 6.093 (+27 %). BODY ~17200.

**Why:** It does not scale. Worker 0 keeps sorting the whole queue. It is not the default.

**Evidence:** same report

records.title: CPU-only ySort
records.text:
**Claim:** Removing bitonic, useZBuffer, packKeys, and packDirect does not make preRender or Pixi ≥3 % more expensive in Predator far, N=1.

**How:** Headed screening 3 s/7 s `--src` `hour=0&zoom=0.4`, detail on, same sitting. Confirm 5×25/18 detail off of the working tree already without GPU sort.

**Numbers:** Screening preRender 21.197→22.755 (+7.4 %, n=1), Pixi 4.955→4.808 (−3.0 %), emit 3.917→3.818, BODY 17102/17229. Confirm preRender median 11.672 (12.525/12.633/11.502/10.850/11.672), Pixi 2.740, BODY 16577.

**Why:** Hygiene. The +7 % is one sample with detail on; the emit did not move. The GPU sort code does not come back. Confirm with detail off ~12 ms, not ~22.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/prerender-far/report.md (not kept)`

records.title: Bitonic H1 vs combo, far camera
records.text:
**Claim:** With ~33 k sprites, H1 or the combo lowers Pixi ≥3 % without inflating pre-render ≥3 %.

**How:** Headed screening n=1 3 s/7 s `--src` `hour=0&zoom=0.4`, `collectGpuStats` on.

**Numbers:** Load OK: BODY 17166/17049/17120, moved ±1.5 %, particles ~5 k ±5 %. Pixi 7.912→7.215→6.622. `GPU_SORT` already 0.49 ms in the snapshot (not 6.4). H1 pre **+20 %**. Combo emit **+109 %**, pre 11.4→20.0.

**Why:** No default combo. Far, the sort is already cheap; direct pack at 33 k breaks the emit. n=1, no confirm.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/bitonic-ysort/gpu-far.md (not kept)`

records.title: Bitonic H1/H2/H3 + combo (GPU numbers)
records.text:
**Claim:** One encoder / pack keys / direct pack, each against a new snapshot, and the three together, with real `GPU_STEP_MS` and `GPU_SORT_MS`.

**How:** Predator headed 5×25/18 `--src` `hour=0&zoom=1.5`, detail on, `collectGpuStats` on. Snapshot `gpu-baseline-*`. No vs `baseline-r*` (GPU-blind).

**Numbers:** H1 `GPU_SORT` 6.440→0.097 (−98.5 %), `GPU_STEP` 7.653→1.105. H2 sort 5.432 (−15.7 %). H3 sort 5.229 (−18.8 %). Combo sort 0.093 / step 1.046 (same as H1). BODY ±1.3 %. Particles do not close.

records.title: ySort bitonic + read Z
records.text:
**Claim:** `ySort: 'bitonic'` on WebGPU does not worsen `pixi_STEP_MS` or `GPU_STEP_MS` ≥3 % against `'cpu'` in Predator, and does not inflate pre-render ≥3 %.

**How:** Headed overlay (previous sitting). WebGPU timer `timestamp-query` + `GPU_SORT_MS`. PainterMove WebGPU 8 s/10 s n=1. Predator screening n=1 8 s/10 s zoom 1.5 and 0.4 + WebGL. Confirm 5×25/18 WebGPU `hour=0` `zoom=1.5` cpu / Z / bitonic, detail off.

**Numbers:** Overlay bitonic = painter. PainterMove pixi 1.350 / 2.421 / 1.798 (all three **< 3 ms**). Pre-render 75.824 / 49.600 / 53.903 (−28.9 % vs cpu). Confirm pixi 2.922 → 3.942 (**+34.9 %**), pre-render 5.823 → 6.967 (**+19.6 %**). BODY 16666 / 16737 / 16958 (cv <1 %, ±1.8 %). Screening particles 106 / 230 / 3032. `GPU_STEP_MS` WebGPU 0 (`GPU_TIMER=1`); WebGL 4.739.

**Why:** No keep. Overlay stays fine. Pack 300 k does not inflate; pixi stress FAIL by floor. Predator: BODY closes, particles do not; pixi and pre-render worsen ≥3 %. GPU WebGPU with no number **in that sitting**. The readback was fixed later (row below). It is not reverted. Default `ySort: false`. `'cpu'` and `useZBuffer` stay.

**Evidence:** `tests/results/bitonic-ysort/report.md (not kept)`

records.title: Shared pack
records.text: joining the sprite pack in `packSpriteLayer` does not move Predator's bottleneck. Headed, 5 runs, warmup 25 s, measure 18 s, detailed stats off, `--src`. Baseline `c418c4e7` (emit already committed, without the pack) and then the working tree. Primary `max(preRender, renderer)`: 11.854 ms → 11.675 ms (−1.5 %). Renderer 8.045 → 8.174 ms (+1.6 %). `GPU_CASTERS` 14056 → 14031 and `GPU_SHADOW_LIGHTS` 40.8 → 40.8, both within 5 %. Pre-render `VISIBLE_ENTITIES` 16631 → 16606. `BODY_COUNT` 16626 → 16606. `ACTIVE_PARTICLES` has cv 86 % and 75 %, so that load does not close and there is no speed keep. Hygiene: the bottleneck does not get 3 % worse. Numbers in `tests/results/pack-sprite-layer/`.

records.title: Three-path spatial cull on Predator
records.text: another sitting, different from the naive-grid paragraph above. The new cull uses the physics Grid for entities with a collider, `DecorationsSpatial` for decorations, and `createSpriteSpatial` for sprites without a collider, against the linear screen cull in `e281d51d`. Headed, 2 runs, warmup 10 s, measure 10 s, detailed stats off, `--src`. A hygiene hypothesis in the regime with the fight inside the view, not a small-camera speed claim. Primary `max(preRender, renderer)`: 12.043 ms → 16.967 ms (+40.9 %). Pre-render 12.043 → 16.967 ms. Renderer 8.664 → 5.321 ms; that Pixi drop is not sold as a win because it draws less. Pre-render `VISIBLE_ENTITIES` 16613 → 16686 (+0.4 %, low cv). `GPU_CASTERS` 14281 → 10808 (−24.3 %). `GPU_SHADOW_LIGHTS` 41.6 → 31.4 (−24.6 %). `BODY_COUNT` 16611 → 16687 (+0.5 %). `ACTIVE_PARTICLES` has cv 47 % and 79 %, so that load does not close and physics/logic are not used as evidence of the cull. The pair does not exist: casters are missing (and shadow lights). Numbers in `tests/results/spatial-cull/`.

records.title: Renderable grid on Predator
records.text: with a single pre-render, the grid replaces the per-sprite screen test. Headed, 5 × 25 s / 18 s, detailed stats off, `--src`. Baseline `e281d51d` (linear cull) and then the tree with the grid. Predator with the fight in the view is not the regime in which the grid can say "faster". Because it stays on by default, the pair is hygiene: do not lose casters and do not let `max(preRender, renderer)` rise 3 %. It does not close. Pre-render 11.823 ms → 15.932 ms (+34.8 %). Pixi 8.003 → 4.025 ms, because it draws less. The maximum goes from 11.823 to 15.932. `VISIBLE_ENTITIES` 16588 → 15540 (−6.3 %). `GPU_CASTERS` 15520 → 10616 (−31.6 %). `GPU_SHADOW_LIGHTS` 45.3 → 33.1. `BODY_COUNT` 16581 → 16564. The pair does not exist: sprites are missing. Numbers in `tests/results/render-grid/`.

records.title: Contiguous Y bands with 2 pre-renders
records.text: with `numberOfPreRenderWorkers=2`, `sortSprites=preRender`, and `packGpuSprites=preRender` (query; Predator's default stays at 1 worker and sort pixi, so without that the band path does not run). Headed, 2 runs, warmup 10 s, measure 10 s, detailed stats off, `--src`. Baseline: tree without Y-bands (stash of those files; old N>1 path with a joined painter). Current: contiguous bands; the new path was confirmed because each pre-render walks the camera's visible set (`VISIBLE_ENTITIES` ~16689 on both workers) instead of the baseline's shard by id (~8315 / ~8338). Primary `max(max(preRender0, preRender1), renderer)`: 17.801 ms → 17.001 ms (−4.5 %). Pre-render max 17.801 → 17.001 (baseline samples 18.228 / 17.374; current 15.687 / 18.324). Renderer 3.312 → 3.521. `GPU_CASTERS` 14960 → 14740 (−1.5 %). `GPU_SHADOW_LIGHTS` 43.5 → 42.8 (−1.6 %). Comparable visible totals (baseline sum ≈ 16654 vs current 16689) and `BODY_COUNT` 16651 → 16687 (+0.2 %), all within 5 %, low cv. `ACTIVE_PARTICLES` cv 51 % / 41 %: physics/logic are not used. This is not the small-camera grid regime. Verdict: speed **kept** (the maximum at least 3 % cheaper, visual load and body load OK; the shadows are not split). Before measuring current, a typo `DecorationsComponent` → `DecorationComponent` in `_bandMembershipPixel` that crashes the worker was fixed. Numbers in `tests/results/y-bands/`.

records.title: Three Predator configs, same sitting
records.text: headed, 2 × 10 s / 10 s, detailed stats off, `--src`. Baseline from the scene file: 1 worker, sort `pixi`, pack `pixi`. Then 2 workers with sort and pack in Pixi. Then 2 workers with sort and pack in pre-render, which turns on the Y bands written that day (each worker walks the whole visible set and filters by Y; it does not query cells). Primary `max(preRender, renderer)`, and with two pre-renders the worse of the two. 1 worker: pre-render 10.519 ms, Pixi 9.101 ms, maximum 10.519. 2 workers Pixi: 12.034 and 12.033 ms, Pixi 11.716 ms, maximum 12.034 (+14 % against the baseline). Bands: 19.154 and 19.112 ms, Pixi 3.285 ms, maximum 19.154 (+82 %). Total visible entities 16618, 16665, and 16719. Bodies 16615, 16658, and 16718. Casters 12473 (cv 14 %, shadow lights 36.4 with one run at 32.8), 15297, and 13868. Between Pixi-2 and bands the casters fall 9 % along with the shadow lights (44.4 → 40.2); casters per light stay ~344. The plan's hypothesis (each worker queries only its band) is not this sitting. The variant that was written does not beat the baseline. Numbers in `tests/results/predator-configs/`.

records.title: Shader light pool in Pixi
records.text: `computeVisibleLights` stopped shrinking `_visibleLightsAll` every frame (that threw the objects away and the next frame created them again) and sorts only the used span. Same Predator, same protocol, against the `766bf53d` baseline. Primary `max(preRender, renderer)`: 11.484 ms → 11.799 ms (+2.7 %). Pre-render samples 11.097 and 12.502 (cv 8.4 %). Renderer 6.630 → 6.113. It is not a speed keep and it does not cross 3 % worse. `VISIBLE_ENTITIES` 16629 → 16674 (+0.3 %). `GPU_CASTERS` 16248 → 14965 (−7.9 %) and `GPU_SHADOW_LIGHTS` 47.3 → 43.5 (−8.0 %) do not close the 5 %: one run saw 40.9 lights and 14112 casters, the other 46.1 and 15818. Casters per light stay ~344. Physics cv 36 %. The change does not pack shadows; the sitting is noisy, not a hole in the sprites. It stays. Numbers in `tests/results/predator-single-prerender/after-pixi-lights.json`.

records.title: Fixed light lists and sort/pack without rewriting the other knob
records.text: the visible-light lists and the stamp lists are built once at the SAB size and the frame writes into those slots. A `sortSprites` and a `packGpuSprites` that do not go together throw, instead of changing the other knob. Same Predator, same protocol, against the `766bf53d` baseline (11.484 ms). Primary `max(preRender, renderer)`: 11.484 ms → 11.204 ms (−2.4 %). Pre-render samples 10.979 and 11.429. Renderer 6.630 → 6.562. records.title: Phases 6+7+8 together on Predator zoom 0.4
records.text:
`src/render/renderGrid.js` was built (multi-cell AABB, extent = max(boundsHalf, visualRange), camera with floor/ceil, overflow if the freelist runs out, no aliases). Grid cull in pre-render with `preRender.renderGrid` (engine and scene default off; Predator only with `?renderGrid=1`). Decorations are indexed at spawn; the decoration collect follows the particle worker's visible list. Y bands (phase 7) query only the band's cell rows when N>1 and sort/pack go to pre-render. The circle stamp filter (phase 8) was measured and turned off: it lowered casters and lights. Protocol: headed, 2×10 s/10 s, detailed stats off, `--src`. Baseline of this sitting (same tree, linear cull, 1 worker, sort/pack pixi): pre-render 12.082 ms, renderer 8.421 ms, maximum 12.082; `VISIBLE_ENTITIES` 16596; `GPU_CASTERS` 13520; `GPU_SHADOW_LIGHTS` 39.4; `BODY_COUNT` ~16590. Numbers in `tests/results/rendergrid-full/`.

1. **Grid N=1 + circle stamp + sort/pack pixi** (`renderGrid=1`): pre-render 19.278, renderer 5.393, maximum 19.278 (+59 %). Visible 16611 (ok). Casters 11416 (−15.6 %). Lights 33.3 (−15.6 %). The pair does not exist (sprites/shadows lost) and the bottleneck gets worse. The stamp filter was turned off afterwards.
2. **Grid N=1 cull alone (linear stamp), decoration collect by grid**: pre-render 20.248, renderer 5.589, maximum 20.248. Visible 16590. Casters 11636 (−14 %). Lights 34.0 (−14 %). The pair does not exist; slower.
3. **Grid N=1 entities only (decorations by the particle list), small freelist**: pre-render 11.871 (−1.7 %), renderer 5.813, maximum 11.871. Visible 16565. Casters 10726 (−20.7 %). Lights 31.4 (−20.5 %). The step fell because Pixi draws less; the pair does not exist.
4. **Same as (3) with freelist ×48 and full overflow (orphan-membership fix)**: pre-render 11.751 (−2.7 %), renderer 6.586, maximum 11.751. Visible 16612 (ok). Casters 11657 (−13.8 %). Lights 34.0 (−13.8 %). Visual load still does not close; there is no keep (it needs −3 % with load within 5 %).
5. **Grid + cell bands N=2 + sort/pack pre-render** (`renderGrid=1&preRenderWorkers=2&sortSprites=preRender&packGpuSprites=preRender`): pre-render max 18.823, renderer 3.046, maximum 18.823 (+55 %). Sum of visible per worker ~18461 (≈ half per band). Casters 13883 and lights 40.4 close to this sitting's baseline. Visual load acceptable, but the bottleneck is much worse than 12.082.

Verdict of the sitting: **no** 6+7+8 variant beats the Predator zoom 0.4 baseline without losing sprites or without raising the maximum. After that sitting the grid, the Y bands, and every pre-render with more than one worker are deleted. A single pre-render remains. `sortSprites` and `packGpuSprites` stay on `pixi` or `preRender`. Predator's default is sort and pack in Pixi, linear cull.

records.title: visPoly + combat remeasured vs `main`
records.text:
`VISIBLE_ENTITIES` 1 on visPoly **is not a small load and not a black canvas**. The scene has an albedo sprite (`VisPolyAlbedo`) plus 360 raycasted lights and 700 occluders; the ~9 ms is the polygon pre-render, not the linear cull of one sprite. Pack/sort stay pinned to `pixi` (the same scene on both sides; the scoreboard only swaps `src/`). Sub-timers `COLLECT_MS` / `SORT_MS` / `SHADOW_Q_MS` / `VISIBILITY_MS` stay at 0 with detailed stats off, as the protocol requires. Headed remeasure 5×10 s/10 s, detailed stats off, `--only visPoly --headed-only visPoly`: preRender 8.651→9.444 ms (**+9.2 %**, cv 3.0 % / 2.1 %), BODY 1060, VIS=1 both, pixi −0.9 %. It confirmed the WORSE: it was not noise on the +3.5 %. Keep-set cause: `_sortPrefix` was an O(n²) insertion sort over the ~360 lights (main uses native `.sort()`; this branch's takeClosest had already gone back to the native sort). The stamp list was also sorted even when `sunN` was 0 (visPoly has no `ShadowCaster`; `GPU_CASTERS` 0). Minimal fix compatible with the keep-set: `_sortPrefix` becomes native `Array.sort` (a prefix copy so pooled slots are not broken) and the stamp sort is skipped when there are no sun casters. Remeasure after the fix: preRender 8.820→8.669 ms (**−1.7 %**, **TIE**), VIS=1, BODY 1060, pixi +1.2 %. steadyCombat remeasured with the same knobs: particle 0.246→0.241 (−2.0 %), spatialMax 0.079→0.081 (**+2.4 %, ~2 µs**), logic0 0.212→0.209 (−1.4 %), BODY 204, particles ~4033/4037. **TIE.** The previous +4 µs WORSE was timer noise; combat AI is not chased. Product gate vs main (physics / logic0 / particle / spatial-max / pixi, none ≥3 % worse and some ≥3 % cheaper): **TIE**, not "faster". Headed box2d from the previous sitting stays TIE −1.6 %. Green catalog: **no** (Uint16 / `MAX_LAYERS` / skipped-pack ceilings: they are not raised). Keep-set merge: **a human call** — hygiene + stamp-grid + pack reuse, with no claim of a green scoreboard. Numbers: `tests/results/scoreboard/visPoly/verdict.json`, `steadyCombat/verdict.json`, backups `_loop-backups/visPoly-verdict-remeasure-plus9.json` and `visPoly-verdict-after-nativesort.json`.

records.title: R2 emit type 0
records.text: the plan asked to pick it by hot line. In the after-H9 trace the `emitSpriteQueue` lines are spread out (the hottest is 8 % of self time, `srScaleX[idx]`); there is no line that justifies a hypothesis. **Not-measured.** In the after-campaign trace `emitSpriteQueue` is 26.6 % of pre-render's self time (first on the thread) and it is still spread out: `srScaleX[idx]` 8.1 %, `srAlpha[idx]` 7.7 %, `frameAccum[idx]` 6.5 %, `srAnchorX[idx]` 5.8 %, `srAnchorY[idx]` 4.4 %, `collectorIndex[i]` 4.1 %. An idea that does come out of this trace, not measured: emit in entity-index order so those reads are sequential. It changes the queue's row order, so the painter's tie-break would have to be by entity id and not by row, or the checksum will not match.

records.title: L2 contacts: each logic worker validates only its own pairs on the stay
records.text: trace after-campaign (with L1, L3, S4, S3, X1): `_processBox2dCollisionCallbacks` is still 19.1 % of logic's busy time. The 3 logic workers validated **every** pair every frame (two generation `Atomics.load`s + `Transform.active`) but each one fires callbacks only for pairs with `minE % workers === index`: two thirds of the work was so that `isCollidingWith` would answer correctly. Foreign pairs now go to a second table (same columns, a negative value in the `Map`) and are validated when `frameCollisions.has(key)` asks for them, plus a sweep every 30 frames that drops the old ones so the table does not grow. `frameCollisions` becomes a view with `has()` (the only use in the engine and in the demos). Kernel `contactsMicrobench.mjs` (worker 0 of 3, fixture pairs): variant **+80.5 %** in contact and **+72.6 %** dense, with the observable checksum identical (stays fired + how many pairs `has()` answers); the previous checksum used `.size`, which with L2 would count old foreign pairs that had not been swept, and it was changed before measuring. Gate 4 against patched `src/` **+73.3 %** dense, same checksum. Parity `contactPairParity.test.js` passes unchanged: callbacks and `has()` of every pair, every frame, against the Set + two Map reference, with respawns and actives that change, workers 0 and 1 of 3. Predator ABAB 8 counterbalanced pairs (baseline with L1, L3, S4, S3, X1), owner logic: **4.427 → 3.870 ms (−11.7 %, 0/8 pairs worse)**; spatial −1.5 %, physics −6.8 %, renderer −1.7 %, particle −6.8 %, pre-render −2.9 %, none regress. Load: `BODY_COUNT` −0.1 %, `GPU_CASTERS` +0.2 %. On pair 1 an audio kernel of ~9 s ran in parallel; logic gave −3.5 % on that pair, inside the range of the rest. **Kept (product).** Numbers in `tests/results/predator-abab/L2/summary.json`.

records.title: L1 contacts: a dense pair table instead of a `Set` + two `Map`s
records.text: trace after-H9: the contact stay was ~34 % of logic's busy time (`_gensMatch` 29.8 %, hot line = the two `Map.get`s). A `Map` from key to slot and `Uint32Array` columns (min, max, gen of min, gen of max), deleted by swap; the stay walks columns (no `Set` iteration, no unpack, one hash per begin/end, none on the stay except `beginSet`). This is not "Stay without sqrt" (2026-09-21, kernel +553 % / scene +20 %): that kernel measured only the scan; this one runs drain + begin/end + stay on the real `LogicWorker` with Predator's contact pairs. Kernel `contactsMicrobench.mjs`: bench variant **+84 %** (7800 pairs) and **+179 %** (dense); against patched `src/` (gate 4) **+215.9 %** dense. Parity `contactPairParity.test.js` (Set + two Map reference, 120 frames, 2 workers of 3). Predator ABAB 8 pairs, owner logic: **6.610 → 4.116 ms (−36.7 %, 0/8 pairs worse)**; spatial −1.1 %, physics −6.4 %, pre-render −5.9 %; renderer +5.8 % and particle +3.6 % with 5/8 pairs worse (noise, they do not block). Load: `BODY_COUNT` −0.6 %, `GPU_CASTERS` −1.3 %. `contactGensPack.test.js` now pins the two `Uint32Array` columns (still no BigInt and no Float64). **Kept (product).** Numbers in `tests/results/predator-abab/L1/summary.json`.

records.title: Bug: contacts with mismatched gens in (max, min) order
records.text: `_applyContactBegin` stored `genA`/`genB` in the order of the Box2D event and the stay compared them against `(minE, maxE)`. If the event arrived (greater, lesser) and the two bodies had different generations (one respawned), the pair was purged while it was still in contact: no `onCollisionStay`, no `onCollisionExit`, `isCollidingWith` false. Fix: they are stored in (min, max) order on begin and compared the same way on end. Test `tests/node/contactGenOrder.test.js`. **Kept (correction).**

records.title: Kernels against a revision: rounds and a verdict by ranges
records.text: at the close of the campaign, `runKernelsVsRev.mjs --vs HEAD --changed` marked `gpuQueuePack` **WORSE (−5.0 %)**, and again **−11.9 %** on a repeat, with the same code on both sides (`gpuQueueLayout.js` unchanged, no imports, identical checksum). Five processes in a row of the same tree gave 1875 to 2128 ops/s: one process per side is not enough for the 3 %. It is now 5 rounds per side with the order alternating, the median, and the verdict also requires that KEEP win (or lose) at least 90 % of the 25 round-against-round comparisons. With that, the same case gives 56 %, a tie. The gate 4s of this campaign were run with a single pass: L1 +215.9 %, L2 +73.3 %, L3 +51.5 %, S4 +22.6 %, S3 +12.9 %, and X1 +38.9 % are above that spread; L4 (+8.5 %) is not, but it was dropped because of Predator.

records.title: Second batch, not measured
records.text: **R3** (emit in entity order) is the same memory-order idea as X5, which did not pay in the browser because of the cross-core effect, and it needs a pre-render kernel with the real worker that does not exist yet. **H11** (repeat under the current protocol) needs that same kernel. **PH1** (`publishPose` without the per-body generation `Atomics.load`): `publishPose` lives in the Emscripten post-js (`weedjsPost.js`) and cannot be imported; it needs a physics-worker harness, and the change touches the generation protocol between logic and physics. **P2** (sway without `Math.sin`): Predator's frequencies are continuous (`1 + rng() * 2` per decoration), so a sine per distinct frequency does not apply; a polynomial sine changes the values in the last digit and is a visual-quality decision, not a measurement. **Not-measured.**

records.title: X6 Pixi: painter radix with one 4-byte histogram and constant passes skipped
records.text: `radixSortIndicesBySortKey` (9 % of Pixi, 98 % from `radixPainterOrder`) did 4 histogram passes and 4 scatter passes, each with indirect key reads. Now: the 4 histograms in one read, and a pass whose byte is the same in every key is skipped (in a stable LSD radix that pass is the identity); sprite keys `round(y) * 128` have a constant low byte. New kernel `painterRadixMicrobench.mjs` (catalog row `painterRadix`; foot-Y keys from the fixture): variant **+75 %** sprites only, **+45 %** with 20 % fractional keys; gate 4 **+48.4 %** (5/5 rounds), identical checksum. Test `radixPainterSort.test.js` against a reference LSD radix (negatives, `-0`, all equal, few values, z bands, subsets, 0–2 slots). Predator ABAB, owner renderer: **4.083 → 3.933 ms (−2.9 %, 2/8 worse)**, just under 3 %; no worker regresses. **Kept (kernel, product-neutral).**

records.title: X5 pack: `packInstancedRows` reading in slot order
records.text: invert the painter list once and walk the queue in order, writing each row at its position. Along the way the kernel `gpuQueuePackMicrobench.mjs` turned out to measure wrong: with the cases in the same process, the shipped function had seen sprites and casters before the clock started and ran almost twice as fast as seeing only one kind of call, which is how the engine uses it (Pixi packs sprites, pre-render packs casters). With each case in its own `worker_thread` (clean JIT), base sprites 1074 ops/s, casters 1315. That reproduced D1 in Node: the function compiled by OSR deopts on `ctx.particleCount = particles` ("Insufficient type feedback for generic named access") until it recompiles. D1a (move that store to a wrapper with no loop) changes nothing: −1.7 % sprites, +5.2 % casters. X5 with the choice at the caller (not a fallback inside the loop: that cost −46 % on casters, the same symptom as X2): kernel **+145 %** sprites; control with the X5 loop in painter order **+50 %** (half the gain is the loop without screen/snap/filter branches, the rest is the order). Gate 4 **+138.1 %**, identical checksum; byte-for-byte parity test on 10 cases. With the queue in cell order (as pre-render builds it) the kernel is still at +73 %. Predator ABAB, owner renderer: **REGRESSION** — renderer +2.5 % (5/8), pre-render **+5.4 % (8/8 worse)**. A trace with X5 shows `packRowsInSlotOrder` at 35.9 % of Pixi, almost what `packInstancedRows` had (38 %): the path runs and it is not faster in the browser. Likely explanation: pre-render writes the queue on another core a moment before, and the cost is bringing those cache lines over, not the read order; in the kernel the data is hot on the same core. **Dropped.** The code went back. The kernel stays with one case per `worker_thread` and `--queue-order cells`.

records.title: S6 spatial: a list of owned entities instead of walking cells
records.text: `findNeighborsForOwnedEntities` walked every cell of its rows, read each `gridCounts`, and deduped with `entityProcessedMarker` (14–15 % of the function in the trace). `rebuildOwnedRows` already computes each entity's position: there it builds the dense list of those whose home row is on this worker (row from `Math.fround(posY)`, the same way the search rereads it), and the search walks that list. The per-entity marker and the ownership check are deleted. It also fixes a latent bug: an entity whose home cell was full (`maxEntitiesPerCell`) was never processed and kept stale neighbors. Kernel: variant +4.9 %, gate 4 **tie** (−0.0 %). Test `spatialOwnedList.test.js`: per-frame checksum identical to the cell walk (reconstructed with the inverse diff) over 45 frames with Predator's config, and with a cap of 4 per cell S6 processes all 4000 entities and the old walk does not. Predator ABAB, owner spatial: **4.182 → 3.463 ms (−17.3 %, 0/8 worse)**; renderer +2.8 % (6/8, under 3 %), the rest does not move. The kernel does not see it because it runs the three spatial workers in sequence on one thread; in the scene they run in parallel over the same grid. **Kept (product, and a correction).**

records.title: Q1 logic: `copyTypeActiveListToBuffer` with `TypedArray.set`
records.text: element-by-element copy loop (2.4 % of logic) → `buffer.set(subarray)`, clipped to the space that remains (the old loop silently dropped what did not fit; `set` would throw). Private function of the module: it cannot be injected as a variant, so it was measured directly at gate 4. The kernel `querySystemMicrobench.mjs` used 2048 actives in non-shared lists; it moved to 16384 (Predator) in a `SharedArrayBuffer` and gained a checksum. Gate 4 **+20.9 %** (5/5 rounds), with lists in a SAB **+21.2 %**. New edge test (more matches than space) passes on the old code and the new. Predator ABAB, owner logic, **two sittings: REGRESSION both** — first logic +2.7 % (5/8), spatial +3.8 %, renderer +3.8 %, particle +4.0 % (6/8 each); second logic +3.5 % (6/8), particle +3.2 % (6/8), pre-render +3.6 % (6/8). The A/A control rules out a harness bias. I did not find the mechanism (spatial, renderer, and particle do not run this copy) and the kernel does not reproduce it. **Dropped.** The code went back; the kernel improvements and the test stay.

records.title: G1 logic: neighbors read straight from `Grid._neighborData`
records.text: trace after-L2: `getNeighbor` 8–9 % + `neighborCount` 7 % + `_neighborView` 2 % of logic. `getNeighbor(i)` now reads `Grid._neighborData[offset + 1 + i]` (no per-entity view and no call), and `neighborCount` reads `Grid._neighborData` without the static getter. It was the half of L4 that was never measured alone. Kernel `gameObjectAccessMicrobench.mjs` with a new `neighbors` case (Predator layout: `maxNeighbors` 1024, lists up to 120, a type test per neighbor, like `findACivilianToShoot`): variant **+36.7 %** `tick` and **+31.1 %** `neighbors`; gate 4 **+28.4 %** (5/5 rounds), identical checksum. Test `gameObjectNeighbors.test.js` (against the old view, widths 16 and 32, one id 70000). Contract: `getNeighbor(i)` is valid for `i < neighborCount`; past that it reads the next row. Predator ABAB, owner logic: 8 pairs −5.7 % but only 5/8 better; extended to 16 pairs: **−0.1 % (8/16 worse)**. No worker regresses. **Kept (kernel, product-neutral).**

records.title: Predator A/A control
records.text: before continuing after Q1, a sitting of 8 pairs with exactly the same code on both sides. **NEUTRAL**, no bias toward B: logic −6.0 % with 3/8 worse, renderer −3.8 % with 2/8, pre-render −3.0 % with 3/8. With identical code the paired median of logic moves 6 %, and the 6/8 pair rule is what filters it. Numbers in `tests/results/predator-abab/AA-control/summary.json`.

records.title: New method: kernels that do not write `src/`, worktrees, Predator ABAB
records.text: the `*-hyps/` campaigns, the one-sitting A/Bs, and `poolFlowHyps.test.js` were deleted (all of them copied snapshots over `src/`). Kernels call the shipped function or the real worker in Node (`workerHarness.mjs`); variants live in the bench (`methodVariant.mjs` compiles the shipped method with an exact diff). A/B against another revision = a worktree in `../weed-ab/`. Product gate: `runPredatorAbab.mjs`, A B A B, 8 pairs of 10 s/10 s, every worker, a regression only if the paired median is ≥ +3 % **and** ≥ 75 % of the pairs get worse. Full rules in `HOW_WE_MEASURE.md` ("Hypotheses from the trace: the gates"). The new trace (`--trace-cpu`, parser with ms, hot lines, and callers) is in `tests/results/v8-deopt/after-h9/parsed/hot-lines.md`.

records.title: Kernels `--changed` against HEAD
records.text: liquidfun TIE (−1.2 %), liquidfunCouple TIE (+1.9 %), preRenderWorker TIE (−2.3 %). `publishPose` comes out **NEW**: HEAD has no `weedjsBindPoseBench`, so the baseline does not start. The comparison that counts is the gate 4 above, not that row.

records.title: P1 pthread pool 2 against 4
records.text: `wasm-function[102]` is the mailbox wait, so dropping the pool from 4 to 2 (`build_for_weed.bat 2`, LTO full) was the cheap test. Node WASM tests, 51/51. Predator ABAB, A = the saved 4-thread wasm, B = the 2-thread wasm: physics **8.671 → 10.875 ms (+26.2 %, 8/8 worse)**. Renderer −10.4 % and pre-render −9.9 % (0/8 worse): fewer cores burned, but the solver falls behind. **REGRESSION.** The 4-thread wasm went back into `src/box2d/`. The spinner in `solver.c` was not touched: it is not the 61 % of the trace, and removing a thread already showed those pthreads do real work.

records.title: P3 sleeping cells opt-in
records.text: `updateCellSleepingStates` is 12 % of particle, and particle is at ~2 ms. The ceiling is a few tenths of a millisecond, not the bottleneck (pre-render ~8 ms). The overlay and `Grid.isCellSleeping` read it. **The default is not changed.** Not-measured as a speed keep.

records.title: Sway with a grid of 100 frequencies
records.text: the sine that costs is one per blade (`swayBaseAngle * freq + i * 0.1`). The later `Math.cos`/`Math.sin` almost never runs: the grass amplitude is ≤ 0.08. Quantizing the frequency alone is not enough, because the phase `i * 0.1` is still distinct. Kernel in the bench (tolerance 1e-3 against `Math.sin`, checksum of the pass): n=20000, base 1571 ops/s; LUT 1024 +15.6 % (not implemented); 32 frequencies +161.3 %; 100 frequencies +161.1 %. Tie between 32 and 100, 100 stays. `sin(i*0.1)` and `cos(i*0.1)` are built once; per frame there are 100 sines and the loop is a product. Config `particle.swayFrequencyBuckets` default 0: the other scenes stay on `Math.sin`. Predator turns it on and the spawn writes the grid `1 + bucket * (2/99)`. Gate 4 against the previous worker: **1624 → 2194 ops/s (+35.1 %, 100 % of rounds)**, within 1e-3 of the sine. Test `swayBuckets.test.js`. Predator ABAB 8 pairs, owner particle: **2.027 → 1.813 ms (−10.0 %, 1/8 worse)**. Logic −2.4 %, spatial 0 %, renderer −0.6 %, pre-render −0.1 %. Physics +3.6 % with 5/8 worse (6/8 is required for a regression). Load: `BODY_COUNT` −0.0 %, `GPU_CASTERS` −0.8 %. **Kept (product).** Numbers in `tests/results/predator-abab/SWAY/summary.json`.

records.title: P2 sway without `Math.sin`
records.text: Predator spawns 20000 blades of grass with `swayFrequency: 1 + rng() * 2`. A sample of 20000 floats like that has **19979** distinct `float32` values. The sine-of-a-sum identity does not apply. **Not-measured** (not worth it). The sine was not touched.

records.title: E1 4-frame cache in `findACivilianToShoot`
records.text: it is demo, not an engine API. 8 pairs: logic −4.9 % but only 5/8 better. Extended to 16, like G1: **logic −0.1 % (8/16 worse)**. Particle +3.2 % with 10/16 worse, does not block. **NEUTRAL.** The cache changes who the soldier shoots for a few frames and it does not pay. The file went back to git. Not kept.

records.title: PH1 `publishPose` without the generation `Atomics.load` when nothing respawned
records.text: a shared `Int32` (`bodyGenEpoch`) rises in `bumpBodyGeneration`. If it matches the value already seen and the previous frame skipped no body, the publish does not do the per-body load. If it skips (new generation, body not recreated yet), it does not latch the epoch: the next frame stays on the slow path. In-memory kernel +135.9 %. Gate 4 against the `weedjsPost.js` from before the loop: **3234 → 7992 ops/s (+147.1 %, 100 % of rounds)**, identical checksum. Test `publishPoseEpoch.test.js`. Predator ABAB 8 pairs, owner physics: **8.741 → 8.751 ms (−0.8 %, 4/8 worse, cv 6/13 %)**. Logic −0.6 %, spatial −2.7 %, renderer +0.8 %, particle −4.9 % (2/8, does not block), pre-render −1.5 %. Load: `BODY_COUNT` +0.1 %, `GPU_CASTERS` −0.6 %. **Kept (kernel, product-neutral).** Predator physics does not move: the step is still inside the wasm. The closing trace (`after-t2`) still shows the `Atomics.load` at 41 % of `publishPose`: Predator respawns all the time, the epoch does not stay latched, and the fast path is not the one the scene runs. Numbers in `tests/results/predator-abab/PH1/summary.json`.

records.title: H11 hoist of `ShadowCaster` in `_writeQueueShadow`
records.text: the in-memory variant won +6.9 % (25/25 round pairs) with the same checksum, but gate 4 against the patched `src/` gave **1118 → 1162 ops/s (−0.5 %, 44 % of rounds) TIE**. The gain was recompiling the method, not the hoist. The code went back. **Rejected** at gate 4. There was no Predator. **Re-landed in `4a7fa4c1` and reverted again 2026-10-21 (`bae431b6`, review E-45):** it came back inlined into `emitSpriteQueue` with no row. With the plain `_writeQueueShadow` call restored, against HEAD: emit kernel **+8.6 %** (70/81, checksums equal); Predator, 4 ABAB pairs, owner pre-render **−2.5 %, better in 4/4**. The inline loses.

records.title: R3 emit in entity order
records.text: new kernel `preRenderWorkerMicrobench.mjs` (the real `PreRenderWorker`, collector in cell order, checksum per entity). A variant that sorts the collector by index before the shipped loop: identical checksum, **−68.8 %** ops/s (1153 → 360, 5 rounds). The sort eats the sequential read. **Rejected-in-kernel.** There was no Predator. Same lesson as X5: memory order is not kept from the kernel, and here the kernel did not even win.

records.title: Trace after-keeps and what was measured after
records.text: CPU capture in `tests/results/v8-deopt/after-keeps/` (Predator headed, detailed stats off). The after-l2 was stale: G1, S6, and X6 were already in the tree. The weight order did not change enough to reorder the plan. Logic ~270 ms/s: contacts 15 %, `findACivilianToShoot` 12 %, `get` 8 %, `neighborCount` 8 %, `getNeighbor` 6 %. Spatial ~290 ms/s: `findNeighbors` 41 %, `_publishFilteredNeighbors` 29 %, `rebuildOwnedRows` 20 %. Pre-render ~517 ms/s: `emitSpriteQueue` 23 %, `_displayPose` 11 %, `packInstancedRows` 10 %, `_writeQueueShadow` 3.7 %. Pixi: `packInstancedRows` 39 %, radix 6.6 %. Physics: `wasm-function[102]` 61 % of the pthread threads, `publishPose` 365 ms on the JS thread and 45 % of that function is the generation `Atomics.load`. Deopts: the V8 log had IC lines and **zero** `code-deopt` lines. D1 and D2 still do not reproduce. Map of the shipped binary (no `name` section, LTO) in `tests/results/wasm-map/after-keeps.md`: Chrome's index includes the 18 imports, so `wasm-function[102]` is binaryen's `$84`. The body is the Emscripten mailbox wait (`_emscripten_get_now` + `cmpxchg`), not the spinner in `solver.c`. That spinner is `$74` (chrome 92) and it is not in the top of the trace.

records.title: Scoreboard against `fc229a21`
records.text: 38 rows, `tests/results/scoreboard/report.md`. `queryAabb` KEPT, logic 16.6 ms → 0.16 ms (−99 %). `box2d` TIE (physics −1.2 %). `liquidfunQuery` WORSE, physics 12.295 → 12.933 ms (+5.2 %, cv 8 % on the new side). That row's module was not edited; the physics host was. The wake is not reverted: the Predator ABAB of that change was NEUTRAL and the keep is the QueryAABB row. Balls lockstep fails the same way on `fc229a21` (spawn ~2100 of 9004 at 120 s), so the scoreboard was run with `--skip-lockstep`. The closing trace does not reorder Predator's threads.

records.title: Close against `fc229a21`
records.text:
`pnpm test:node` 806/806. Balls lockstep fails the same way as in the snapshot: spawn timeout, 2204 of 9004 at 120 s. The scoreboard was run with `--skip-lockstep` and `--skip-node`. Predator ABAB 8 pairs, A = `fc229a21`, B = this tree: **NEUTRAL**. Spatial **7.271 → 6.503 ms (−11.4 %, 0/8)**. Pre-render +2.8 % (6/8), renderer +1.7 % (5/8), particle −0.8 %. Logic **+8.1 % (6/8, cv 10 %)** and physics **+10.8 % (5/8, cv 12 %)** do not cross the runner's regression rule (they do not block). Load: `BODY_COUNT` −0.0 %, `GPU_CASTERS` +0.0 %. `tests/results/predator-abab/close-vs-fc229a21/summary.json`.

Scoreboard 38/38, `tests/results/scoreboard/report.md`: **11 rows FAIL/WORSE**. Scene or kernel keeps: `queryAabb` logic −98.7 %, `liquidfunQuery` physics −5.9 %, `visPoly` pre-render −3.7 %, `bullets` particle −5.9 %, `decalBlit` pixi −3.2 %, and kernels `audioSlots` +8.0 %, `shadowStamp` +7.2 %, `gpuQueuePack` +8.3 %, `painterRadix` +6.8 %, `preRenderWorker` +5.9 %. `box2d` TIE (physics +1.5 %). `liquidfunCouple` WORSE (physics +3.8 %). `spatial` on the stationary stress falls 2.735 → 1.901 ms (−30.5 %) but the baseline is under the 3 ms floor, so the row is FAIL. `box2dRayJs` publishes logic 0.000 ms on `fc229a21` and 16.513 ms now: the scoreboard pair has no baseline, and the verdict for that stress is its own ABAB (49.935 → 16.567 ms). Predator trace after the ray keep: `tests/results/max-campaign/wave5/`.

records.title: Max campaign, snapshot
records.text: rev `fc229a21`. Predator A/A 8 pairs, NEUTRAL. Side A median: preRender 7.150 ms, physics 6.836 ms, spatial 6.497 ms, renderer 4.132 ms, logic 3.974 ms, particle 1.665 ms. Physics in the trace: three pthreads at 100 %, `wasm-function[102]` 60.8 % (mailbox wait). The pool is not lowered: the threads are busy, not idle, and an earlier sitting with 2 threads already made the step more expensive. `wasm-function[285]` is 11.6 % and has no name in this binary's map; the C was not touched. Numbers in `tests/results/predator-abab/max-baseline/` and `tests/results/max-campaign/`.

records.title: Trace wave after the ray keep
records.text:
trace `tests/results/max-campaign/wave5/` against `close/cpu-summary.json`. Spatial is still in `findNeighborsForOwnedEntities` (53.7 %, and the `entityPosData` load is 23 % of that function). Pre-render: `emitSpriteQueue` 21.5 %, `_displayPose` 10.5 %, `collectVisibleEntities` 8.2 %. Pixi: `packInstancedRows` 38.9 %. Physics: `wasm-function[102]` 64.9 % (mailbox, already closed), `wasm-function[285]` 10.5 % (the SAT already lost on Balls). Logic: contacts 14.5 %; `findACivilianToShoot` and `person.js` are demo and do not enter.

Three hypotheses from that trace, Predator headed, stats off:

1. Cache the squared range in the candidate loop when the half-extent repeats. Owner spatial, 4 pairs: **6.077 → 6.760 ms (+9.1 %, 4/4)**. Renderer +9.5 % (3/4), pre-render +3.8 % (3/4). **REGRESSION.** The extra branch on the hot line does not pay: the half-extents change. The file went back to git.
2. With interpolation off, `_displayPose` does not load the previous pose. 4 pairs looked like a keep (−5.4 %, 3/4) but physics and logic, which do not run that function, also fell ~10 %. Extended to 8: pre-render **7.768 → 7.510 ms (−2.0 %, 4/8)**. **NEUTRAL.** The file went back to git.
3. Remove the `|| 0` from `boundsHalfW/H` in `collectVisibleEntities` (17 % of that function in the trace). 4 pairs, owner pre-render: **7.406 → 7.999 ms (+4.8 %, 4/4)**. Renderer +8.0 % (4/4). `GPU_CASTERS` +0.2 %. **REGRESSION.** The file went back to git.

None of them stayed. The wave is not repeated.

records.title: One wait for 3072 `castRayClosest`
records.text: the busy Box2D stress leaves logic at ~50 ms because each ray is its own SAB round trip. Hypothesis: the 3072 rays go into a single `PENDING` and the physics worker calls `castRayClosestBits` in one pass, without waiting between rays. `RayVsBox2dBoxBusyScene` headless, 8 pairs, owner logic: **49.935 → 16.567 ms (−66.8 %, 0/8)**. Physics **6.345 → 4.542 ms (−28.4 %, 0/8)**. `BODY_COUNT` 2800 = 2800. Pre-render +5.2 % is 0.73 ms, under the floor. **Kept (product).** `Box2d.castRayClosestBatch`. `tests/results/predator-abab/ray-batch/summary.json`.

records.title: QueryAABB wake on the LiquidFun query
records.text: the same stress, headless, 4 pairs. A without `pumpQueryWake`, B with the wake always armed. Physics **11.405 → 11.746 ms (+4.0 %, 3/4)**, logic **+15.1 % (4/4)**, `BODY_COUNT` 4 = 4. The wake is what makes it more expensive. The fix (arm `waitAsync` only after serving a QueryAABB, so that stress does not go back to 16 ms) against the always-armed wake: physics **12.929 → 12.438 ms (−2.9 %, 2/4)**, logic −1.7 % (2/4). It does not reach 3 %. Particle +8.2 % is 0.045 ms, under the 3 ms floor, and does not count. **Dropped.** Both files went back to git. `tests/results/predator-abab/lf-query-wake/` and `lf-query-lazy/`.

records.title: Polygon SAT, cut the second axis
records.text: `wasm-function[285]` is `b2CollideTask` (task table, no symbol; the body carries `B2_CONTACT_RECYCLE_COS_ANGLE` 0.98 and `1.5 * B2_LINEAR_SLOP`). Hypothesis: in `b2CollidePolygons` the second `b2FindMaxSeparation` is unnecessary if axis A already cleared the speculative band. Rebuild LTO full, 4 threads, Node WASM tests 71/71. records.title: renderOnly particles
records.text: `ParticleEmitter` accepts `renderOnly: true` (default off). A shared `Int32` counts how many there are. If it is 0, integrate and emit do not read the column. If it is > 0, those particles age on the CPU and do not integrate motion or enter the sprite emit; the look stays on the compute layer that already packs them. Test `particleFlatGravity.test.js`. Integrate stress, one run, default: particle 2.460 → 2.276 ms, preRender 4.021 → 4.135 ms (+2.8 %, under 3 %). This is not a new GPU integrator: if the shader does not move the pose, the sprite is not drawn.

The previous sitting does not count: the machine was busy (Balls reached 35 ms). This sitting, the same build with and without the filter, detailed stats off.
