records.title: Math-allocation audit, scoreboard vs `5ef9775e`
records.text:
`pnpm bench:scoreboard --vs 5ef9775e` aborts in lockstep. Balls never reaches 9004 active transforms inside 120 s: this tree stopped at 3004 and then 2404, and the pre-audit `src/` in the worktree stopped at 2104. Same harness, same `setTimeout` spawn. Lockstep was skipped and the 38 catalog rows were run (`--skip-lockstep`, detailed stats off). That sitting’s product line said nine rows were FAIL or WORSE. Three of those are under the 3 ms floor (spatial, queryAabb, meshFillMoving), which is not a regression. The six WORSE rows were re-run the same day, same anchor, same flags, `--only ray,rayVsBox2d,liquidfunQuery,tilemap,decalPremultiply,painterRadix`. `ray.js`, `tileMap.js`, `pinGpuTexture.js`, and `sortIndexByKey.js` are unchanged since `5ef9775e`.

The rerun: ray kernel 1,511,214 → 1,517,427 ops/s (+0.4 %). ray scene logic0 was 4.405 → 4.652 ms (+5.6 %) on that pair, then a scene-only pair was 4.658 → 4.561 ms (−2.1 %), **TIE**. `RAYCAST_COUNT` was 3072 on both trees and `RAYCAST_MS` was 4.090 → 4.036 ms. rayVsBox2d **TIE** (kernel +1.5 %, logic0 −0.8 %). liquidfunQuery physics 12.576/13.252 → 12.281/11.245 ms (−8.9 %), the opposite sign of the first sitting’s +6.3 % on overlapping samples. tilemap **TIE** (kernel +2.9 %, logic0 −1.5 %; the −37.2 % did not reproduce). decalPremultiply kernel +6.3 % and painterRadix kernel −2.7 %, both the other side of a 4 % first-sitting swing, source unchanged. **No code change.** None of the six is a stable regression. The first board’s Balls physics tie (8.209 → 8.127 ms) and visPoly keep (9.035 → 7.396 ms) stand. `productVerdict` no longer counts a step-floor FAIL as “do not claim a better WeedJS”. The row itself stays FAIL, as the protocol requires.

Kernel-only WORSE: decalPremultiply −4.7 %, publishPose −9.3 %. visPoly preRender −16.5 % and swayBuckets kernel +14.7 % are keeps. This commit is not faster than `5ef9775e`.

records.title: Math-allocation audit, visibility hygiene
records.text: H-04 hoists the constant end direction in `angularSweep.js`. H-06 uses the first-order ε expansion for the pre/post samples. H-05 uses angle addition in `emitArcVertices` (at most 4 steps). The polygon gate, stated before the edit, is 1e-4 world units against a fixture snapped from the old sweep; the test passes. H-08 drops `%` from `normalizeAngleSigned`: bit-identical on `(−π, π)`, at most 1 ulp on `[−3π, 3π]`. No scene. The Predator trace names none of these functions. **Kept (hygiene).** H-09 (squared distance before the occluder cull) was **not shipped**: it is the same extra branch that lost 4/4 on 2026-10-06, and there is no vehicle.

records.text: numeric sort of packed keys instead of a comparator on the spawn permutation. Kernel, 5/5 rounds: n=8 +110.11 %, n=64 +117.75 %, n=256 **+147.06 %**, n=1024 +106.10 %. records.text: cache the sway-frequency bucket instead of recomputing `bucketFromSwayFrequency` per decoration. Kernel at N=65 535, k=3: **−18.0 %**, cv 1.0 %, parity exact. records.title: Math-allocation audit, H-03 hypot
records.text: six runtime sites use `Math.sqrt(x*x+y*y)` instead of `Math.hypot`. Kernel, five counterbalanced rounds, accumulator live: `Math.hypot` about 30 M ops/s, `Math.sqrt` about 470 M ops/s, **~16×**, at every magnitude from 1e-3 to 1e7. Only about 64 % of in-range pairs are bit-identical; the rest differ by a few ulps, which is inside float32. `adobeAnimCompiler.js` still calls `Math.hypot`. Not in the Predator trace. **Kept (hygiene).** No sitting.

records.title: Math-allocation audit, H-02 gather copy
records.text: `gatherInstancedRows` copies each sprite row in a loop instead of `dst.set(src.subarray(...))`. Kernel at the real depth, 45 568 rows: subarray 6.6 M rows/s, looped 8.8 M rows/s, **1.32×**. The 2.94× figure (4.136 → 12.149 ops/s) is a small working set and is not the claim. A `PerformanceObserver` over 45 568 rows × 40 rounds counted **0 GC events on both sides**, so the allocation story is dead. Scene, spritePack, spacing 6, 4K, 6 pairs, detailed stats on because the probe reads `RENDER_QUEUE_SIZE`: preRender 7.225 → 7.409 ms, paired −4.8 %, worse 3/6, cv 8/13 %. Attributed `SPRITE_PACK_MS` 1.480 → 1.416 ms, paired −5.8 %, worse 1/6, cv 7/6 %, **under the 3 ms floor**. Gate verdict NEUTRAL. Output bit-identical (`gatherInstancedRowsParity.test.js`). **Kept** on the real-depth kernel. Not a product speed keep. Full write-up: `[MATH_ALLOC_AUDIT_IMPLEMENTATION_LOG.md](./reports/MATH_ALLOC_AUDIT_IMPLEMENTATION_LOG.md)`.

records.title: Audio slot scan, per-bus list and quietest cache
records.text:
a full bus was walking every slot up to the high-water mark, including other buses. Each bus now keeps the slots it holds, plus the quietest voice and the second quietest, in a tail of the channel SAB. A shot that is not louder than the cached minimum drops after one read. A louder shot claims that slot and promotes the second. A miss walks that bus's list only. The worklet's free sites update the list. `PLAYS_PER_TICK` was raised from 800 to **1200** and frozen. Headed, `--src`, detailed stats off, one window each side, warmup 10 s, measure 10 s: logic0 **8.806 → 0.278 ms (−96.8 %)**. Baseline is above 8 ms. The fast side is under 8 ms, which the campaign rule allows when the baseline cleared it and the step got cheaper. `BODY_COUNT` 0 / 0. Kernel `audioSlotMicrobench.mjs` storm case, 5 alternating rounds, checksum matched (drop count and the voices left on each bus): **20,916 → 261,576 ops/s (+1150 %)**, 5/5. The no-channel occupancy cases in that same run went through a bench wrapper and are not the shipped path (occ50 −10 %, occ90 −8 % there). `soundManager.test.js`, the mixer tests, and `soundSlotClaim.test.js` pass. **Kept.** Predator was not the pair: this function was 4.3 % of logic there.

Main thread busy is 19 ms/s. `getActiveSlotCount` is the top function, **20.1 ms in the 10 s window** (10.6 % of that light thread, 97 % of it the `for` over `maxSlots`). Kernel `audioMetricsMicrobench.mjs`, 2048 slots / 128 playing, checksum 128: **42,732 ops/s** (23 µs/call) and `readPlayingVoices` **49,921 ops/s**. At 60 Hz the scan is about 1.4 ms of main per second. There is no worker `STEP_MS` for that call. **Screened.** No counter was added.

The audio worklet does not appear in the trace (no `process`, `mixVoice`, or `audioMixerProcessor` samples). Kernel `audioMixerMicrobench.mjs`, checksum of one quantum: 32 voices 37,289 ops/s, 128 voices **9,527 ops/s**, 512 voices 2,322 ops/s, 128 voices inside a 2048-slot table **9,271 ops/s** (−2.7 % vs the 128-slot mix, under 3 %). The empty-slot walk is not the mix. **Dropped.** The panel stayed closed during the trace. `audioPanelMicrobench.mjs`, checksum 200 rows: update at 0 voices 5,380 ops/s, at 200 voices 5,887 ops/s. Not a worker step. Three Box2D threads sit in `wasm-function[102]` at 1000 ms/s while physics `STEP_MS` is 0.076 ms. They were left alone.

records.title: 100k tweens, one logic worker
records.text: `TweenStressScene`, `maxTweens` 100000, three logic workers, physics off, one sprite. records.title: Ease dispatch, switch vs else-if vs object
records.text: `applyParticleEase` stays a switch. The kernel `tests/bench/easeDispatchMicrobench.mjs` times that shipped function against the same curve bodies written as an else-if chain and as a plain object of functions keyed by the numeric ease id. A direct call to the one curve, with no id test, is the ceiling on the single-ease rows. `src/` was not edited. Seed `0xe35e0001`, 4096 inputs, three fresh isolates per cell, `timeIt` held the 3 ms sample floor. Checksums match the shipped function on every cell (lerp `1543583917`, quad-in `1054200789`, bounce `1369305495`, mixed `69436109`). Median ops/s: lerp switch 107.5 M (9.3 ns), else-if 101.9 M (−5.2%), object 307.7 M, direct 1004 M. Quad-in switch 113.3 M (8.8 ns), else-if 108.0 M (−4.8%), object 314.7 M, direct 944 M. Bounce switch 56.5 M (17.7 ns), else-if 54.8 M (−3.1%), object 147.4 M, direct 279 M. Mixed ids, uniform over 0..13: switch 57.2 M (17.5 ns), else-if 53.8 M (−6.0%), object 53.2 M (−7.0%). The else-if chain is about 1 ns slower. The object is about 3× the switch when the id does not change, and the direct call is about 3× the object again, so the lookup is not free. When the id changes every call the object loses the three rounds by about 1 ns. This loop is tiny, so a small function can inline here; `Tween.tick` and particle integrate are large and were not re-timed. **Screened.** No scene. Report: `tests/results/ease-dispatch/kernel.json`.

Working tree versus HEAD `src/` in `../weed-ab/HEAD-5c986922`. Checksums match except free-span (the new merge joins the neighbor the old scan left behind) and chain mass (disk mass versus 0). Medians: one-shot audio quantum 162,214 → 203,438 ops/s (+25.4%, 25/25); play on a live bus 3,641,064 → 2,232,915 (−38.7%, 0/25); sized chain scratch check 346,340,337 → 259,542,513 (−25.1%, 0/25); free span 160,294,943 → 126,540,232 (−21.1%, 0/25, different checksum); texture word union 3,458,173 → 3,034,855 (−12.2%, 0/25); `locateView` 16,150,132 → 37,513,599 (+132%, 25/25); chain ray plus pick 34,583 → 38,675 (+11.8%, 25/25); `setPlane` 557,507 → 601,549 (+7.9%, 22/25); `getMetrics` 51,152 → 51,387 (+0.5%, 16/25); `setAngle` 184,479,154 → 188,361,755 (+2.1%, 18/25); channel handle 69,299,749 → 69,949,962 (+0.9%, 14/25); chain `syncMass` 43,501,903 → 66,232,842 (+52%, 25/25, different checksum); `updateTexture` union 1,798,103 → 2,229,406 (+24%, 21/25). Kernel keeps are the one-shot quantum, `locateView`, and the chain query. The play path, the scratch check, the free, and the texture word union are kernel losses. `setPlane` and the picture upload are above 3% on the median and short of 23 of 25 rounds. records.title: Contact pair key, E-10 and E-27
records.text: E-10 rejected in kernel, no `src/` change. The kernel's own premise probe swept all **715,838,805** `pack16` keys and found **0 boxed**, range `[-2,147,450,879, 2,147,483,646]`, 25 % negative, because JS `<<` is 32-bit signed. Timing 42.15 M against 42.05 M ops/s (−0.23 %), checksums equal. A 2026-10-20 review note (M10) says the V8 premise was backwards: pointer compression makes Smis 31-bit, the sweep ran in Node (no compression), and in Chrome every key with minE at or above 16384 is a HeapNumber once it enters `_pairSlot` or `frameCollisions`. The Node result stands for Node; the Chrome cost is E-54. E-27 asked whether `entityIdWidth: 32` costs anything (falsifier: within 3 % of the 16-bit path), using the same kernel unmodified, 64 k entities: `PAIR0` pack16 plus `Set` 7,007,659 ops/s, `PAIR1` float-multiply plus `Set` 3,422,003 (0.49×), `PAIR3` packCantor plus `Set` (ships at 32-bit) 4,061,285 (0.58×). **The falsifier fails:** the 32-bit option is about 1.73× slower on pack-then-`Set.has` and 2.40× on packing alone. Cantor against the other 32-bit encoding is −1.8 %, so the entire gap is the key becoming a double. `PAIR_COUNT` (logic stats slot 16, stride 16 → 17) was added as the missing denominator; no scene. Reports: `[reports/E-10-pair-key-smi.md](./reports/E-10-pair-key-smi.md)`, `[reports/E-27-entity-id-width-32.md](./reports/E-27-entity-id-width-32.md)`.

Kernel `angularSweepMicrobench.mjs` times the shipped polar write on 80 segments at **36,190 ops/s** (checksum 426461800); that case is not the same work as `cases.sweep`. **Kept.** Reports: `tests/results/compound-vispoly/baseline.json`, `polar.json`, `kernel-polar.json`. records.title: Clear shapes past a batch of 32
records.text: `destroy_loose_shapes` read 32 shape ids and treated a second full read as "nothing left," so a body with 64 or more shapes kept every shape after the first 32. The clear now stops only when the body's shape count does not fall. Node test `clearing 96 shapes leaves none` in `tests/node/rbColliderComposition.wasm.test.js`. Kernel `tests/bench/clearShapesMicrobench.mjs`, five alternating rounds, old wasm from `ba6c091d` against the rebuilt module, clear clock excludes the fill and the body recreate, step sample held the 3 ms floor. Leftovers on the old module: 64 shapes leave 32, 96 leave 64. After the fix both leave 0. 32 and 63 already left 0. A clear of 96 shapes (the new call destroys 96, the old call destroyed 32) is **552 354 → 256 163 ops/s**, slower in 5 of 5 rounds. That is the work that used to be skipped. Per shape destroyed the new call is faster (17.7 M → 24.6 M shapes/s). A clear of 32, the same destroy count on both sides, is **548 169 → 757 465 ops/s**, faster in 4 of 5, short of the 90 % round rule. A step of 200 shapes, which does not call clear, is **3.103 M → 2.898 M ops/s (−6.6 %)**, slower in 4 of 5. The same-work clear of 32 did not get slower, so the step dip is the relink, not this loop. **Kept (hygiene).** Not a speed claim. Report: `tests/results/clear-shapes/pair.json`.

records.title: One slot helper for the six sync query SABs, R3
records.text: hygiene, kept. `RayVsBox2dBoxIdleScene`, 4 pairs against HEAD: physics −0.21 % (B worse 2/4), logic −0.14 % (2/4), load 2000/2000. Tie.

records.title: Sync query wake for every kind, E-56
records.text: kept on the batch regime. Physics answered sync queries only inside `doStep`; only QueryAABB woke it between steps. `RayVsBox2dBoxIdleScene` (one 3072-ray batch per tick), headless, `--src`, stats off, A = `e7393e27`, 4 counterbalanced pairs, `BODY_COUNT` matched: **logic0 16.6 → 2.9–3.4 ms (−82 %, 4/4)**; physics `STEP_MS + QUERY_WAKE_MS` −1.4 % (2/4, under the 3 ms floor). Single casts are screening only (baselines under the floors): 8 per tick logic −78 % (3/4), physics busy +4.9 %; 1536 per tick logic −71 % with the load not matched (the old code served 1024 per burst). Ending every burst on a 0.1 ms spin was tried first: −70 % physics busy at 8 casts, +31 % to +50 % logic at 384 casts; the step's bursts keep the old tail (E-57). `STEP_MS` alone is not the physics primary here: a batch answered by the wake left `STEP_MS` −88 % with no saving.

records.title: Save encode, E-49
records.text: kept on the kernel (`62537602`); the browser time-to-save on Predator, the stated primary, was not run. No format change. The writer caches each field name's UTF-8 bytes (`nameBytes`, a Map capped at 4096 names, cleared when full) instead of calling `TextEncoder` per entity per field, and the snapshot builds each component class's field plan once per save instead of per entity. Kernel `saveEncodeMicrobench.mjs` (new), 4000 mixed entities, 49 alternating rounds against `89c94e18`: snapshot **109.7 → 42.5 ms** per save (49/49), encode **235.0 → 40.9 ms** (49/49), so **345 → 83 ms** of main-thread stall per save. The output is byte for byte the same: `saveEncodeGolden.test.js` pins length 51908 and its sha256, which HEAD also produces, plus a 5000-name round-trip past the cache cap. No worker `STEP_MS` moves, because the world is paused during the snapshot. The restore side (`applyEntitySaveRestore`) is still open as E-49b.

records.title: Ease front under the inline limit, E-59
records.text: kept (`7e56612e`; tools `e79834c1`). `applyParticleEase` was 717 bytes of bytecode, over TurboFan's 460-byte inline limit, so `--trace-turbo-inlining` showed it refused in `updateParticlePhysicsBuffers` and `Tween.tick`. The new front is 245 bytes with literal case labels for LERP and the six polynomial curves, and EXPO, BACK and BOUNCE moved to `applyRareEase` (451 bytes), which V8 still inlines with mixed ids. Kernel `particleIntegrateMicrobench`, three new cases (2048 particles with alpha and scale tweened), 9 alternating rounds against `e3524a0b`, checksums equal on every case: LERP 10,024 → 12,802 steps/s (+27.7 %, 81/81), QUAD_OUT 10,124 → 13,021 (+28.6 %, 81/81), 14 ids mixed 9,654 → 12,451 (+29.0 %, 81/81), rotation tween 10,175 → 12,370 (+21.6 %, 81/81), untweened a tie. Minor GCs per 1000 steps fell from 8 / 16 / 15 to 0 / 1 / 0. `tweenPoolMicrobench` (65,535 LERP tweens) 535 → 708 ticks/s (+32.4 %, 72/81 cross-round wins). Scene, 4 ABAB pairs, headless, `--src`: `ParticleIntegrateStressScene ?tween=1` particle **4.62 → 4.12 ms (−10.3 %, 4/4)**, the verdict; every other worker ties or improves. `TweenStressScene` logic0 2.36 → 1.95 ms (−15.9 %, 4/4), screening only because the baseline is under the 3 ms floor and 65,535 tweens is already the 16-bit entity maximum. Predator hygiene, 4 pairs: particle +3.4 % (2/4, under its floor), logic −9.7 % and −2.9 %, physics +4.8 % (3/4) on a worker the change does not touch (an A/A sitting with the same harness gave physics +2.85 %, 3/4). The planned primary scene was wrong: `ParticleIntegrateStressScene` spawned untweened particles and never ran the ease, so it got `?tween=1` (off by default). A parity test holds every id against the old single switch bit for bit. **Kept.**

records.title: Compound outline per-entity revision, E-58
records.text: dropped, no product win after G1. A per-entity `entityRevision` (Uint32 per entity, appended after the pool revision, bumped by `replaceForEntityFlat` and `_freeFixtureChain`, never reset) keyed the three `ensureCompoundSolid` call sites. Tests showed one remesh leaving the other bodies' cached outlines alone and the suite was green. `CompoundVisPolyStressScene`, `remeshEvery=1`, 4 ABAB pairs against `66b82a5a`. 36-triangle islands: pre-render 6.54 ms, **−0.8 % (1/4), tie**; renderer −5.8 % (0/4) on a 1.7 ms baseline under the floor. 128-triangle islands (`ringSegments=64`, new knob `df614bbf`): pre-render 10.94 ms, **+0.8 % (2/4), tie**; renderer +3.4 % (3/4) at 2.0 ms, under the floor. 256 triangles saturates pre-render (19 ms, 116 % load) on the visibility sweep, so it cannot judge this. G1 already made a rebuild 12–18× cheaper and pre-render only outlines bodies inside a light's reach. The patch was not kept. Reopen only with a scene where rebuilds show in a profile (many large lit islands, one cut per frame, primary at least 3 ms).

records.title: Polar bin direction table, E-42
records.text: kept (`c8db38ea`). `stampPolarBin` and `sweepDistAt` called `Math.cos/sin` of a constant bin angle, and the clip output computed them a third time. One table of 1025 entries covers both kinds of angle (index m is `-π + m·½·(2π/512)`, a bin centre at m = 2b+1, a group centre at m = b0+b1), built with the loops' own expression, so a lookup is the same double. Kernel, 9 rounds against `f404b2d2`, checksums equal: raster (`polar`) **+252.2 %**, full-circle merge +74.7 % (512 bins) and +107.9 % (128 vertices), general merge +5.6 % (79/81), sweep tie. `CompoundVisPolyStressScene`, 4 pairs: **pre-render 4.03 → 2.32 ms (−42.3 %, 4/4)**. With E-41 the scene went 6.47 → 2.32 ms. A golden test pins 12 merged polygons to hashes of the code before E-41, which they still match. That scene's pre-render is now under the 3 ms floor, so E-43 and E-44 need another scene. **Kept.**

records.title: Audio `play()` bus walk, E-46
records.text: regression confirmed and fixed (`4f7e3ff6`; knob `a8b7c482`). Since `8af92002`, `_reclaimDeadVoices` ran before the `count >= maxV` early drop, so every play walked its bus's whole voice list. At 1200 plays per tick logic0 was 2.25 ms, under the floor, so `AudioStormScene` got `?plays=N`. At 2400, 4 ABAB pairs against `8af92002^`: **logic0 0.44 → 4.29 ms, about 10× (4/4)**. The fix counts releases in channel header word 6 (the mixer's `releaseVoice` when its CAS wins, and the host's `stop`, `stopAll` and `stopSlot`); each bus keeps the value it last walked at (tail word 6) and skips the walk while it has not moved. B1's ownership rule is unchanged. `AudioStorm plays=2400`, 4 pairs against HEAD: **logic0 4.33 → 0.57 ms (−86.6 %, 4/4)**. Tests: the real mixer bumps once per release, and a host stop frees room on a full bus (that test fails with the bumps removed). The last 0.13 ms against `8af92002^` is B1's ownership checks. **E-46b, measured and not kept:** the `claim` closure hoisted into a static method (`_claimListed`, 9 arguments) tied in `audioSlotMicrobench` (storm +1.9 %, 63/81; three-thread occupancy −1.9 %) and was reverted. **Kept.**

records.title: Small review items, E-50
records.text: two kept on kernels, four screened with no change. **`collectSolidSegments` order, kept** (`64d0caa9`; kernel cases `6b7ad641`): the facing test runs before the range test, and a back-facing edge is range-tested only until something hit. Kernel, 9 rounds, checksums equal: island +4.9 % (80/81), large outline +22.6 % (81/81). Compound scene `ringSegments=64`: pre-render −2.5 % (4/4), a tie in the good direction. **Body-dirty list duplicates, kept** (`a18d3918`; kernel case `b4370d95`): a deferred mark is listed only when the slot's pending flags go from 0. Kernel, 9 rounds: a 4096-spawn window with 3 marks each **+21.6 % (81/81)**, the empty flush ties. `SpawnStormScene` logic0, the owner, ties (+0.07 %, 8 pairs). Physics read +4.5 % (6/8) and again worse on the fix side in a side-swapped 8-pair sitting, but physics `STEP_MS` tracks `BODY_MOVED_COUNT` (r = 0.84 over 32 runs) and the fix-side runs moved 5.8 % more bodies, outside the 5 % load band. At matched load the fix side is +0.06 ms (0.8 %) with a 0.094 ms standard error: no difference. **Screened, no change:** `_snapshotVertGen` (two whole-pool copies per MESH layer per frame take 13.9 µs at 65,536 entities in Node), the frameClock header seqlock (three atomic loads where one would do, once per worker per frame), light-splat attenuation (saves a `sqrt` per fragment, GPU fill only, which the CPU `STEP_MS` benches cannot time), and the littleCity jitter (two `rng()` per person-frame). Body-create allocations are open as E-50b (needs a Node kernel with the Box2D WASM and SpawnStorm physics as the primary).

records.title: Light sort adaptive insertion to merge, E-08 reopened
records.text: kept (`c53f163b`; kernel `7319ff1c`). The first E-08 fix still allocated (`tmp.slice(0, n)` made a new array on most frames), and `b69c880e` had replaced it with an insertion sort. New kernel `sortPrefixMicrobench` on the real worker, 360 lights: insertion takes 54 µs on random order, 3.4 µs in grid-cell order and 1.35 µs sorted, and the visible-light list comes from `queryActiveEntities` in entity order, random in y for moving lights. A fixed switch at 64 to a merge sort won random (+355 %) and lost cell order (−54 %). Kept adaptive: past 64 items the insertion sort gets a budget of 16 moves per item, and a list that spends it finishes in a stable bottom-up merge sort (runs of 32) through a scratch grown once. Kernel, 9 rounds, checksums equal: 360 random **+187 %**, 128 random +17.5 %, cell order −12 %, sorted −17 % (0.3–0.5 µs), 46 and 20 lights tie. `VisPolyStressScene` (360 lights): pre-render +1.4 %, a tie. The test runs on a real worker (stable-sort parity for random, ties, sorted and reversed input, and scratch reuse). **Kept.**

records.title: Particle lights past the cap, E-52
records.text: fixed (`7aecfd0e`; kernel `c18ac7fa`). `packParticleLights` took lit particles in active-list order until `particleLights.max`, so a bright impact spark could drop out behind dim beam particles. When the main loop fills the cap with candidates left, the rest go through their own copy of the per-light work, and each candidate brighter than the dimmest packed light (screen radius times alpha, through a min-heap) replaces it. The main loop is unchanged, so the under-cap path is the same code. Kernel, 9 rounds: under the cap a tie (+0.9 %). The laser shape (600 dim lights and 8 sparks over a 256 cap) costs **3.9 → 14.5 µs**, mostly per-candidate work for the rest of the list. A 1.5× replace threshold saved only 2 µs and lost exact selection, so it was dropped. Terrain demo with the laser held: renderer 0.71 ms, under the floor, so no verdict; it read +7 %, with spatial and pre-render (untouched) +4–5 % on the same side. Tests: sparks after 300 dim lights are kept; a filtered or off-screen bright light is not. **Kept** as a correctness fix with a measured kernel cost.

records.title: Turned-camera cull for sprites, E-51
records.text: kept for sprites (`f6063781`; knob `c0ad244c`). With a turned camera the cull kept the axis-aligned box around the view, about 2.2× the screen area at 45° on 16:9. `collectVisibleEntities` now runs a copy of its loop that turns each sprite into view space and tests it against the view plus the same margin; rotation 0 runs the loop it always did. Rotation-0 hygiene, `camRot=0&spacing=12`, 4 pairs: pre-render −0.08 % (3.38 ms baseline), renderer +1.2 %, both ties. `SpritePackStressScene ?camRot=0.785&spacing=14`, 4 ABAB pairs: queued sprites **30,589 → 15,997**, **pre-render 4.41 → 2.72 ms (−38.3 %, 4/4)**, renderer −31 % (4/4, 0.68 ms baseline, under the floor). `turnedCameraCull.test.js` checks on a real worker that the kept set is exactly what `viewWorldToScreen` puts in the view, at four rotations and zooms. The other culls (particles, decorations, glow, Adobe pieces) still use the box and are open as E-51b.

records.title: Full-circle merge in the polar clip, E-41
records.text: superseded by E-43 (`43b5bc2c`), which merges the placeholder faster; the path is removed. Was kept (`634baaab`; kernel case `87528d3c`). Compound bodies `continue` before `occCount++`, so a light that sees only compound occluders got `buildFullCircle` (32 edges) and `clipVisibilityToPolar` ran `sweepDistAt` for every bin against it, 16,384 `raySegT` per light to learn "R" (`sweepDistAt` was 34.2 % of pre-render busy time in `CompoundVisPolyStressScene`; node timing 103 µs against 26 µs per light). The merge is not skipped, since that would move the outer edge from the 32-gon's chords to the circle (up to 0.5 % of R). It tests three edges per bin instead of 32: a ray from the centre of a convex polygon only meets the edge whose span holds it, or a neighbour at a corner, so the minimum is the same bit for bit. The placeholder is recognised by its vertices, in its own copy of the loop; anything else takes the full scan. Kernel `angularSweepMicrobench`, new `polarFullCircle` cases, 9 rounds against `7ba494d1`: **+224.9 % at 512 bins, +116.1 % at 128 vertices** (81/81, checksums equal); the general merge, nearest and sweep tie. Scene `CompoundVisPolyStressScene`, 4 ABAB pairs: **pre-render 6.47 → 4.07 ms (−37.2 %, 4/4)**, every other worker ties. `polarFullCircle.test.js` holds it to the full scan on 60 random lights across 8 vertex caps. **Kept.**

records.title: Lazy polar bin clear, E-44
records.text: screened, under the bar. Every raycasted light fills 512 floats; ~50–100 ns each, so the visPoly row's 360 lights spend ~18–36 µs a frame against a ~5 ms pre-render (under 1 %). A lazy clear on the first stamp would be exact but cannot reach 3 %. Not done.

records.title: Pixi circle fan table, E-60
records.text: kept (`7c301240`; knob `1d91efac`). `_renderOccluderSelfLit` called `cos/sin` of the same 16 fan angles for every lit circle occluder and every light. A constructor table built with the loop's own expression gives the same doubles (16/16). `VisPolyStressScene?occluderShape=circle` (700 round occluders, 360 lights), 4 ABAB pairs: **renderer 6.49 → 5.61 ms (−13.2 %, 4/4)**, pre-render −2.2 %.

records.title: Polar merge by arc scatter, E-43
records.text: kept (`43b5bc2c`; knob `2f6880df`; no input copy `fcdec953`). `clipVisibilityToPolar` tested every sweep edge against every output ray. Each edge now tests only the rays inside the arc it subtends from the light (with raySegT's 1e-4 slack, padded 1e-6 rad); an edge near a half turn is tested by every ray. A minimum is order-free and skipped rays would get Infinity, so the polygon is bit-identical (`polarMergeScatter.test.js`, against a copy of the old scan). Kernel, 7 rounds, checksums equal: **merge +1451 %**, placeholder circle +72.7 % / +18.1 % (512 / 128), so E-41's path is removed. `CompoundVisPolyStressScene?boxes=60`, 4 ABAB pairs: **pre-render 11.61 → 3.46 ms (−69.8 %, 4/4)**; default scene −11.5 % (under the floor). Dropping the input copy afterwards: kernel ties, checksums equal. Scene `boxes=60`, 4 pairs: pre-render +1.96 % (2/4), a tie; no worker 3 % worse.

records.title: Chained outline raster, E-61
records.text: kept (`0b8b07f2`). A CPU profile after E-43 put `writePolarSegment` at 27 % of pre-render busy, 90 % of it two `atan2` per edge. Pre-render walks each outline in a chain order (built on first use after a rebuild; `seg` keeps its order for Pixi) and reuses the angle of the end it just rastered when the next edge starts there; bit-identical (±0, the −π fold and the zero-length case argued in the code; `polarRasterChain.test.js`). A first version that kept the cache inside `writePolarSegment` crossed the 460-byte inline limit and lost 7–14 % in the kernel; the stamping now has one call site and inlines. Kernel, 7 rounds: island collect +16.4 % (49/49), large +6.8 % (44/49). Compound scene, 4 pairs: **`ringSegments=64` pre-render 5.03 → 3.97 ms (−20.8 %, 4/4)**; `boxes=60` −7.2 % (3/4).

records.title: Merge arcs without atan2, E-62
records.text: kept (`483f1da7`). E-43's `mergeSweep` spent 63 % of its time on two `atan2` per sweep edge, used only to choose candidate rays. The cross product of the slack-extended ends now picks the short way and `pseudoAngle` (`y/(|x|+|y|)` by quadrant, slope 1/2 to 1 per radian, so the 1e-6 pad still covers 1e-6 rad) orders ends and rays. Output still comes only from `raySegT`: bit-identical. Kernel, 7 rounds, checksums equal: merge +13.5 %, placeholder circle +6.2 % / +10.5 %. Compound scene `boxes=100`, CPU profiles of 7.6 s with the same total busy time: `mergeSweep` inclusive time **346 → 233 ms (−33 %)**, about 0.25 ms a frame. Its `STEP_MS`, 6 ABAB pairs: −0.5 % (4/6), a tie; the scene's run-to-run load spread (±10 %) hides ~6 %. At `boxes=60` (−7.5 %, 5/6) two tree runs fell under the 3 ms floor, so that row fails. Kept on the kernel; the scene is not worse. (The commit message's −60 % is `mergeSweep`'s self time alone, without its inlined callees.)

records.title: Merge binary searches "not inlined", E-64
records.text: screened, premise wrong, reverted. A Chrome profile listed `firstRayAfter` / `firstRayAtOrAfter` as frames, read as un-inlined calls boxing a double. One call site each tied in Chrome (merge inclusive 233 → 230 ms) and lost 5.4 % in the Node kernel. V8's CPU profiler names inlined code by its source function, so a frame in the profile is not evidence of a call: ask `--trace-turbo-inlining`.

records.title: Branchless rotation-0 particle cull, E-65
records.text: screened, not taken. Kernel, 65k random particles: −16 % at 82 % visible, +8 % with all visible. Emitter particles are spatially clustered by index, so the branch usually predicts; the gain depends on the scene.

records.title: Turned-camera cull for particles, E-51b
records.text: kept (`de5096a4`; knob `652b91b3`). ParticleIntegrateStressScene `camRot=0.785`: the box around the turned view held almost every particle and the render queue sat at its 55,000 cap. The turned path tests each particle in view space. A branchy first version cost the particle worker +11 % (4/4) through misprediction (the box branch was always taken, the turned one splits ~73/27); branchless it ties. 4 ABAB pairs: queue → ~36,000, **pre-render 4.84 → 3.42 ms (−29.4 %, 4/4)**, renderer −24.9 % (4/4). Rotation 0 ties.

records.title: FSM time boxed per onUpdate, E-68
records.text: screened. One heap number per FSM tick (0.8 MB/s per logic worker in Predator, ~20 µs a frame). Needs a public signature change.

records.title: Contact begin Set, E-54
records.text: kept (`1a1c4c37`). The old premise (0 % of Predator's keys box) used 16,583 ids; Predator now has 42,633 slots and its soldiers, trees and rocks are above 16384. The stay loop's per-pair key + Set probe was 4.2 MB/s in one logic worker; a per-slot stamp replaces it (parity test against the Set reference). Predator: **logic −382 µs at matched load (se 132 µs)**, about −9.5 %.

records.title: Pre-render boxing in Chrome, E-66
records.text: kept (`fbaaad81`, `878bc55a`, `7b980c2f`). Sampling heap profile of Predator: pre-render allocated 30.1 MB/s (Node: nothing on the same paths). Light comparators returning `a − b` (3.5 MB/s) now return a sign; the per-entity pose scratch object (17.6 MB/s, x and y most likely tagged fields through shared map transitions) is a Float64Array; the returned sort key (8.9 MB/s) is stored into its slot. Pre-render allocation → 0.27 MB/s. Predator: **pre-render −8.7 % (4/4)** for the pose scratch; the comparators −3.7 % (3/4); the sort key a tie over 10 pairs.

records.title: Component getter by integer slot, E-69
records.text: dropped. Replacing `_componentCache[name]` (megamorphic keyed load in the one shared getter) with a closure-captured slot into an array: kernel −12.7 % holey, tie when pre-filled; Predator 8 pairs logic −137 µs (se 70) at matched load, but the getter's own CPU-profile time **749 → 1,079 ms**. Restored. See L4 (2026-09-30), the same area: kernel wins do not carry to Predator's ~15 classes.

records.title: Scoreboard platform vs `main`
records.text:
**Claim:** Catalog runner can compare every engine feature with load gates.

**How:** Scoreboard full; 40 rows

**Numbers:** ray:TIE, rayVsBox2d:TIE, decals:FAIL, emit:FAIL, integrate:FAIL, spatial:FAIL, box2d:TIE, liquidfun:TIE, liquidfunCouple:TIE, liquidfunQuery:KEPT, queryAabb:FAIL, nav:FAIL, visPoly:KEPT, tilemap:TIE, tilemapGid:FAIL, contactDrain:FAIL, box2dRayJs:KEPT, queryPublish:FAIL, preRender:FAIL, compute:FAIL, decorations:TIE, bullets:TIE, spawn:KEPT, steadyCombat:WORSE, decalBlit:KEPT, sceneryCam:FAIL, meshFillMoving:FAIL, meshFillPan:FAIL, meshFillLook:FAIL, audioStorm:FAIL, audioSlots:TIE, gameObjectAccess:KEPT, shadowStamp:TIE, gpuQueuePack:KEPT, decalPremultiply:TIE, painterRadix:WORSE, publishPose:TIE, preRenderWorker:WORSE, swayBuckets:WORSE, textureUpload:WORSE. No. 6 row(s) FAIL/WORSE. Do not claim a better WeedJS. 12 row(s) are a protocol ceiling (not claimed). 3 row(s) are under the 3 ms floor (not a regression).

**Why:** Platform shipped. Do not claim best WeedJS unless every catalog row is KEPT or TIE and none WORSE/FAIL.

**Evidence:** [`tests/results/scoreboard/report.md`](../tests/results/scoreboard/report.md)

records.title: Render-queue columns typed from the constructor, E-71 + E-72
records.text: kept (`a49482f4`, `4289cbc5`). A field declared `null` and later given a typed array has field type Any in V8 (`--trace-generalization`: `h{Any}`); declared as an empty array of the right class it keeps `h{Class(…)}`. N-32's 8 `null` column declarations cost the emit kernel 15 %; the other 16 columns had been `null` all along. Emit kernel 1,458 → 1,717 (E-71, +17.7 %) → 2,004 ops/s (E-72, +17.8 %), 49/49 each, checksums equal. Predator headless 8 pairs, pre-render at matched load +53 µs (se 154) and +12 µs (se 186): emit is under 1 ms of 6.7 ms there. A/A of the E-72 sitting: worker medians −4.6 to +7.2 % with identical code. Audit for the other workers: E-73.

records.title: Typed start for the other workers' fields, E-73
records.text: screened, no change. Spatial's 15 fields +0.6 % (35/49), pre-render's collector columns +0.7 % (25/49): ties. The pose columns' upper bound is +9.6 % (58/81) on a collect with poses published, but `_latchPose` resets them to `null` every frame as the "no pose" sign, so the change is a new sentinel at ~15 readers for ~0.1 ms of pre-render: parked. The cost appears where per-entity code tests the array's truthiness (emit's guards, `_displayPose`), not where a loop only indexes a hoisted local.

records.title: Self-lit follows visibility, N-19
records.text: fixed (`ed5a7b89`), a bug fix measured for cost. One owner store per improved polar bin. Read from a module-level `let`, the owner cost the compound collect kernel 8–11 % (island 104k → 93k passes/s, 0/49), with the stamping chain still inlined (`--trace-turbo-inlining`). As a parameter down `collectSolidSegments` → `rasterPolarSpan` → `stampPolarBin`: −7.7 %. Setting the `_polarActive` module flag once per span (from the bins' return values) instead of in every improved bin: −5.1 % island, −0.5 % large. Lesson: in a hot inlined loop, a module variable read or written per iteration is a context-slot access TurboFan does not keep in a register. Compound scene `ringSegments=64`, 6 pairs: pre-render +1.7 % (4/6), renderer −4.5 % (5/6 better, plausibly fewer self-lit fills).

records.title: Water tunnelling into the planet, N-18
records.text: closed, probe artifact (`59d9cd6d`). The probe bound 64 body slots for 310 terrain islands; 246 islands had no shapes. With a slot per island, 0 particles get in at any drop with the planet's skin 0. The earlier "skin does not matter" reading came from the same broken world; on the fixed one a 1 px skin lets 3–13 particles 15–42 px in, so the planet's skin 0 is the right setting.

records.title: Sweep event directions, E-63
records.text: kept (`fd15ae95`). The sweep took `Math.cos/sin` of every event angle that `atan2` had just made from a vertex; the direction is now stored with the event. Not bit for bit, so a frozen pre-change sweep and H-06's 1e-4 gate: 3000 mixed scenes, max move 1.2e-10, same counts. Kernel +16.6 % (49/49); VisPolyStressScene pre-render −9.0 % (5/6), CompoundVisPoly `boxes=100` −3.9 % (5/6); the renderer's +5–8 % lean is inside an A/A spread of −9.5 to +35.8 %. **E-74** (`rayPolyDist` divides only for crossed edges): +2.3 % (33/49), dropped.

records.title: Spatial neighbour gather in cell order, E-70 + E-75
records.text: dropped, all slower in the spatial kernel (checksums equal): per-worker per-frame cell copy −10 % (3.3 reads per copied cell), shared slot-parallel positions −5.2 % (4.7 MB in order beats nothing; `entityPosData` is 264 KB and cached), branchless candidate append −4.3 %. The "25 % on the gather" in a Chrome profile was latency charged to a load, not a layout problem.

records.title: Short burst tail for a few sync casts, E-57
records.text: dropped. Short spin until a burst has served 16 requests: 8 casts per tick physics step+wake −38 % (6/6), logic0 +40 % (5/6); 384-cast stream logic0 +3.1 % (4/6). The tail only moves the wait between physics and logic. Serving pending queries between physics sub-steps is the shape left to try.

records.title: Planet water pull as one host setting, N-17
records.text: kept (`da9dfe76`, `ddb7efc9`), a bug fix measured for cost. `LiquidFun.setRadialGravity` replaces a ring command per particle per logic tick; the host adds accel × dt to each particle's velocity before each step. Planet scene, 3769 particles poured by 120 `q` taps, 12 one-second samples after 4 s of settling, 3 ABAB pairs, headless. To keep the water the same on both sides the tree ran the pull at G/2, HEAD's effective pull (LiquidFun drains `applyForce` in the first of 2 sub-steps; median water height 31.6–33.6 px on HEAD, 33.8–34.0 on the tree). Physics +3.8 / −5.7 / −6.2 % (2/3 better); logic, both workers, 0.87 → 0.10 ms (under the floor, screening only). HEAD dropped ring commands in every run, the tree in none. With the full G as shipped: water 25 px high, physics 13.9 ms in one run (HEAD 12.4–13.3), the denser water's cost. Scratch probe, not a committed tool.

records.title: Boid facing through setRotationCS, N-41
records.text: kept (`c750a095`), hygiene. `this.setRotationCS(c, s)` in place of a direct `enqueueSetRotCS`. records.title: No-pool Box2D runtime against the 4-pthread pool, E-53
records.text: answered, no cost, tie. The pool is JS-only glue, so the same tree and the same `box2dWasm.wasm` ran both ways, with `c9ba6f6f`'s glue diff reverse-applied for the pool side. Balls, 4 Box2D workers, 8 ABAB pairs, A = no pool (HEAD), B = pool: physics **5.90 vs 5.93 ms (+1.4 % for the pool, 5/8)**. Load identical (9,004 bodies, 9,000 awake). The 5–8 % gap against E-04b was the two days of commits between them. Nothing changed; the glue went back. A re-run of the worker sweep on 2026-10-20 (Balls, headless, `--src`, stats off, 2 rounds) gave physics 10.68/13.76, 8.10/8.03, 6.89/6.39, 6.22/5.98 ms at 1/2/3/4 workers, load 9004/9000, so `4` is still best.

records.title: WASM Q4, the cost of one JS → WASM call, E-76
records.text: measured, premise. `tests/bench/wasmCallCostMicrobench.mjs` with the test module `wasm/test/callCost.c`: near-empty exports by argument shape, alternating in one process with their own loop literals (a shared literal made one call site polymorphic, 13–16 ns), against an inlined JS function doing the same adds. Median ns per call, Node 22 / Chrome 155: JS 1.7 / 1.42, `nop0` 0.47 / 0.41 (elided), `sum4i` 3.1 / 3.9, `sum8i` 3.6 / 4.8, `sum4d` 3.4 / 4.4, `sum8d` 4.8 / 5.3, `load1` 3.3 / 4.2. About 4 ns a call: free per frame, batch or light; about 66 µs a frame per entity at 16.5 k, and per particle at 65 k about 6 % of the particle stress worker. W17's per-command export call is not where its cost is.

records.title: WASM Q3, memory floors, and a calibration of the floor method, E-76
records.text: measured (Node 22, AC), premise. `tests/bench/wasmFloorPremise.mjs`. Each shipped loop is set against a patched copy that keeps its loads and stores and drops its float maths (E-18's method). W22, `_updateDecorationSwayBuckets` on a real worker with 20 000 decorations: **1.74–1.77×** its floor's time in snapshot order, 2.51× shuffled. W23, `stampLightRange` on the Predator fixture: the grid walk is only 6.6–6.9 % of the call (selection, nearest tracking and the append are the rest), and 2.20× / 1.48× its two floors. W5, `findNeighborsForOwnedEntities` on a real worker, 16 500 entities, every list rebuilt, the floor replaying the logged decisions so the rows are identical: **1.026–1.035×**. Calibration on `_publishFilteredNeighbors`, the one loop with a shipped WASM twin: floor 1.015–1.033×, while the module runs the same rows **2.10–2.17×** faster (1.43× in `spatialPublishWasmMicrobench`). A floor ratio near 1 therefore does not say WASM cannot win a gather loop. JS's cost on these loops sits around the loads, not in the arithmetic, and the plan's floor screen is withdrawn for them. W5 goes first in Phase 3 (about 18 % of Predator spatial at the publish's 1.4×), W22 stays open, W23 stays borderline, and W10 is screened on its 2.0 % ceiling.

records.title: Spatial dedup marker as Int32Array, REVIEW_PLAN N-63
records.text: fixed, correctness, speed neutral. From stamp frame 4096 the int32 stamp's top bit is set, and the `Uint32Array` marker never matched it, so for 68 s of every 136 s at 60 fps candidates in several cells were appended and published once per cell (Predator mix: 231 453 duplicates in 13 736 of 16 500 rows). Benches never ran long enough to see it. `processedMarker` is now an `Int32Array`. Spatial frame kernel (`spatialWorkerMicrobench` setup, 3 workers, frames below 4096), alternating processes, 4 per side: 252.6–256.2 against 247.4–254.5 frames/s, identical checksums.

records.title: WASM W5, the spatial candidate gather in C, E-78 / E-76
records.text: **kept (product).** Predator gate (Chrome, headed, source, 6 pairs, owner spatial, `--vs` the commit before the wiring): spatial **5.203 → 4.205 ms, −18.6 % paired, worse 0/6**, cv 3/3 %; physics −3.4 %, renderer −0.3 %, pre-render −1.3 %, logic +4.3 % (4/6, under the 75 % bar; logic reads identical rows, load within 0.05 %); load keys within 0.3 %. The first verdict, FAIL (load), came from a 245 % cv on `FLOWFIELDS_COMPUTED`: median 0 on both sides, one flow field in one baseline run. The nav keys got a gate floor (`452f53c6`) and the recorded pairs re-decided. Wired as `SpatialWorker._findNeighborsWasmGather` behind `wasm.spatialGather` (default on), with the grid in the spatial memory; `tests/node/spatialGatherWasm.test.js` checks both paths frame by frame. Report `reports/E-78-spatial-gather-wasm.md`. The kernel sitting: `wasm/spatialGather.c` does the cell walk, dedup and range test (in double, the JS arithmetic; the worker's circle patterns in their order) for a batch of the entities whose lists rebuild this frame. `spatialGatherWasmMicrobench` runs it as a bench variant on real workers in WASM mode, in a memory laid out as the product would: the publish regions, the grid cells (written there by `rebuildOwnedRows` in both variants), and per worker a marker, truncation flags and a rebuild list, plus the patterns. Rows and counters are equal on every one of 45 frames. Node 22, AC, `runKernelVariants` (alternating processes, 5 rounds), 3 workers, 16 500 entities: Predator's spatial settings with drift, base 267.0–269.4 and WASM 338.2–342.8 frames/s, **+28.0 %, 25/25**; every list rebuilt, +25.5 %, 25/25. Q3's floor said 1.03 for this loop; the WASM gain is not in the arithmetic. Chrome confirms or not in the Predator gate after the wiring.

records.title: WASM plan: W5 wired and kept (E-78)
records.text: The memory map adds the grid cells and, per spatial worker, a marker, truncation flags and a rebuild list, plus the pattern table. `Grid.initialize` views the grid at its offset. `SpatialWorker._findNeighborsWasmGather` is chosen in `update()` when `wasm.spatialGather` is on (the default); `findNeighborsForOwnedEntities` still runs at 32-bit ids and with the switch off. `tests/node/spatialGatherWasm.test.js` runs both paths in two threads, 40 frames: identical rows and counters. Kernel on the shipped paths: +26.9 % (25/25). Bundles: both modules embedded and loading in all 8. **Predator gate (Chrome), 6 pairs: spatial 5.203 → 4.205 ms, −18.6 %, worse 0/6; KEPT (product).** It first read FAIL (load) on a 245 % cv of `FLOWFIELDS_COMPUTED`: median 0 on both sides, one flow field in one baseline run. The nav keys now have a gate floor (`452f53c6`) and the sitting re-decided. Logic +4.3 % (4/6) is under the 75 % bar. Report: [`reports/E-78-spatial-gather-wasm.md`](./reports/E-78-spatial-gather-wasm.md). Two modules ship now, so Phase 6's L1 applies: the coexistence test must cover the gather.

records.title: Source modules against the bundle
records.text: measured, no change (explained the same day by E-77 above). The same tree, headless, `--src` against `dist/` rebuilt from it, 4 pairs alternating, 6 s warm-up, 8 s window, detailed stats off. Predator, bundle against source per worker (`STEP_MS − WAIT_MS`): preRender 7.42 ms −12.0 % (0/4 slower), physics 7.81 −6.5 % (1/4), spatial 6.32 −3.8 % (1/4), renderer 4.51 −3.3 % (1/4), logic1 4.08 −5.9 % (1/4, load +4.5 %); logic0 4.44 −15.9 % does not count (its `ENTITIES_PROCESSED` moved −8.3 %). bunnyMark (screening, logic under the 3 ms floor): logic0 2.78 ms +3.9 % (3/4 slower), preRender +16.8 % (2/4, noise), renderer −7.2 % (0/4). Every scene row in this log is source mode; games from npm run the bundle, which is not slower. The bundle writes `const { … } = WEED` as `var` (captured, mutable) where source mode has module consts; bunnyMark's logic hint points there and needs a heavier logic load to judge. Running it found that Predator and six other demos could not load from the bundle at all (N-57).

records.title: seededRandom state wraps to 32 bits
records.text: fixed, correctness, speed neutral. The mulberry32 state was a closure double that never wrapped; it passed 2^53 at call 4 917 760 of a stream, and from there the sequence was no longer mulberry32 (and would in the end stop changing). Now an `Int32Array(1)` that wraps like the reference; the first 4 917 760 outputs of every stream are unchanged. MinimalTick logic (one `rng()` per entity per tick): source +2.5 % (0/3), bundle −1.3 % (2/3).

records.title: Imports read as module consts, E-77
records.text: kept. `spatialWorker`, `preRenderWorker`, `particleWorker` and `colliderUtils` re-declare the imports their hot methods read (`import { Grid as GridImport } …; const Grid = GridImport;`). Why the bundle beat source: a native import is a cell TurboFan reads at run time, with a TDZ check; webpack's getter is inlined and folded, and so is the class's typed array behind it (`rebuildOwnedRows` 5 564 B of TurboFan code in the bundle against 6 940 B in source, `collectVisibleEntities` 6 496 against 8 256). A module const folds in both forms. Source, MinimalTick, 3 rounds: spatial −16.2 % (3/3), pre-render −22.7 % (3/3); Predator headed, 6 rounds: particle 1.380 ms −27.6 % (6/6), pre-render −6.1 % (4/6), spatial −3.5 % (4/6), logic per 1000 entities +3.4 / +1.0 % (2/6, loads 2482–2950, no import changed in logic). Bundle, Predator headed, 6 rounds: particle 1.289 ms −17.9 % (6/6): its large integrate functions inlined nothing when their helpers came through getters and inline `returnToPool`'s chain now; the other workers within noise (pre-render +6.0 %, 1/6, while its hot functions compile to the same 6 496 B and MinimalTick bundle pre-render was −5.2 %). Bundle +4.2 KB (2 966 778 → 2 971 012). Copying an import into a local at function entry instead: spatial −2 to −6 %, not reproduced. All imports in Pixi, logic and `abstractWorker` as well: nothing more measurable there (their imports are read per frame). Self-contained workers (no `worker_common` chunk, full scope hoisting): bundle +64 %, rejected for size. Not visible in Node (V8 12.4): the spatial kernel tied across all four forms. Guard: `tests/node/importAliases.test.js` (no alias inside the 19-module import cycle, none of an `export let`). Rules in HOW_WE_MEASURE, "Imports in hot code".

records.title: WASM migration Phase 0 and Q1, E-76
records.text: measured (profiles), no change. Every share on record predated E-77, so four headed CPU profiles ran on `5477a582` (source, detailed stats off, 10 s warm-up, 10 s window, about 45 s each; `tests/results/wasm-q1/`). The profiler inflates `STEP_MS`, so only shares were read. Predator: spatial `findNeighborsForOwnedEntities` 61.8 % self (85.8 % inclusive), the WASM publish 17.5 %, `rebuildOwnedRows` 12.5 %; pre-render `emitSpriteQueue` 28.7 % inclusive, `collectVisibleEntities` 32.1 % inclusive (7.2 % self), shadow-caster stamp 25.9 % inclusive; Pixi `packInstancedRows` 33.9 %, painter order 11.8 %; particle `_updateDecorationSwayBuckets` 45.1 %, particle integrate 0.7 %; logic contacts 11.3 %; `publishPose` ~8 % of the physics JS thread. VisPolyStressScene pre-render: the per-light sweep 49.2 %, the neighbour gather 26 % plus `_displayPose` 13.7 %. CompoundVisPoly `ringSegments=64` pre-render: `collectSolidSegments` 84.9 % inclusive, and one line of it, the per-edge `normalizeAngleSigned(Math.atan2(…))`, about 38 % of the worker (V8 runs `Math.atan2` as its native fdlibm port, which WASM can at best match). ParticleIntegrate `tween=1` particle: integrate 75.3 %, list build 22.6 %. What it changed in the plan: W12/W13 lead Phase 3 (ceiling ~17 % + ~7 % in the stress scene), then W2a (~11 %) and W1 (~10 % after the `atan2` is set aside); two candidates the plan had not listed, decoration sway (W22) and the shadow-caster stamp (W23); five parks below. Plan and per-candidate facts: `WASM_HYPOTHESES.md`, "Phase 0 inventory".

records.title: WASM spatial publish kernel against the shipped JS, E-76 T4
records.text: measured (kernel), no change. Until now `spatialPublishWasmMicrobench` timed the WASM against a JS copy of the publish loop. On the T4 harness it times `SpatialWorker._publishFilteredNeighbors` on a real worker in JS mode (the path taken without a publish memory) against `publish_batch` on the product memory. Rows are compared before timing, and the sides alternate in one process for 9 rounds. Node 22 (V8 12.4), WASM checked to be TurboFan (`--allow-natives-syntax`), laptop **on battery**. Uniform case (the 2026-10-06 data: 4 096 entities, 48 random candidates each, batch 2 048), three processes: the shipped JS ran at 2 315–3 068 ops/s and the WASM at 4 015–5 611, **+73.5 %, +82.9 %, +87.4 %**, each 81/81 cross comparisons. The old bench, alternated with it, read +69 %, +123 % and +138 %, its JS copy at about 2 000 ops/s (the copy builds five typed-array views per call). Predator case (the candidate rows the real gather builds for one worker's 4 677 owned entities, 264 851 neighbours published): JS 379, WASM 630 ops/s, **+66.4 %** (81/81). So the +118 % on record was measured against the copy; against the shipped JS the kernel edge is smaller. The scene keep of 2026-10-06 (Predator spatial −14.6 %) stands on its own pair. **On AC power, the same evening**, three processes per case: uniform JS 4 065–4 087 and WASM 7 533–7 628 ops/s, **+85.0, +86.6, +87.3 %**; Predator JS 670–704 and WASM 959–993, **+41.1, +45.1, +43.2 %**, all 81/81. Battery had halved the clock and inflated the Predator edge (+66.4 % from one process).

records.title: WASM Q5, the float32 publish against the double JS path, E-76
records.text: measured (Node), correctness. The shipped module computes `dx² + dy² < er²` in float32. The JS path (`_publishFilteredNeighbors`, taken at 32-bit ids or with `wasm.spatialPublish: false`) computes it in double from the same float32 inputs. Both predicates were evaluated exactly for every candidate the real gather produced over 45 frames of the Predator mix (`spatialWorkerMicrobench` setup, 3 workers): 34 918 287 pairs, **0 disagreements**. Of 3 000 000 pairs placed one float32 step from the edge, 26 957 disagree (0.9 %; 22 497 inside only in double, 4 460 only in float32), all within 3.1·10⁻⁷ of the edge relative to er², about 2.6 float32 steps. On a 2 000-entity edge frame the shipped rows differ from the JS rows for 86 entities. Two double kernels (scratch builds with the pinned flags; the JS arithmetic in C, float32 inputs widened, every operation in double) publish rows identical to the JS path on both frames. Cost, Node 22 (V8 12.4), TurboFan checked, AC power, 3 processes of 9 alternating rounds. On the Predator rows, scalar double read **−1.9, +0.5 and +0.8 %** against the shipped f32x4 module (tie), `f64x2` −3.6 to −5.1 %, the JS path −28.8 to −31.0 %. On the edge frame (sequential candidates, half of them inside, so the arithmetic dominates), scalar double read −21.6 %, `f64x2` −22.3 % and JS −44.7 %. The paths disagree only at the edge and never in a real frame on record. The double kernel costs nothing measurable where the gather's loads dominate, which is the product's case. Next: W8a, the C in double as a correctness change, through the Predator gate.

records.title: WASM W8a, the spatial publish in double, E-76
records.text: kept (correctness). `wasm/spatialPublish.c` does the JS path's arithmetic (float32 inputs widened, every operation in double, scalar), so the WASM and the JS path publish the same neighbour set; in float32 they differed within ~3·10⁻⁷ of the range edge (Q5). Module 571 bytes (876 before). Kernel, Node 22, AC, against the shipped JS (`spatialPublishWasmMicrobench`): Predator rows +43.1, +45.4, +46.3 % (the float32 module read +41.1 to +45.1 % the same evening); uniform +56.7 to +60.0 % (float32 +85.0 to +87.3 %: the predicate dominates that synthetic case). The same Predator rows in Chrome 155 (`chromeKernel.mjs`, 3 runs): double +2.0, +2.0, +3.2 % faster than float32 (72, 60, 78 of 81). Predator gate (`runPredatorAbab --name W8a`, 6 pairs, owner spatial, headed, source): NEUTRAL. Spatial 5.084 → 5.227 ms, +5.0 % paired but worse in only 4 of 6 pairs, under the 75 % consistency bar. Logic −3.8 %, renderer −2.0 %, physics +0.2 %, pre-render +0.4 %; `BODY_COUNT`, `VISIBLE_ENTITIES`, `GPU_CASTERS` all within 0.0 %. The kernel is no slower in Chrome on the scene's own distribution, and the published rows are the same, so nothing downstream changed. Read the spatial +5.0 % as the gate's noise; if a later Predator sitting that touches spatial shows it again, measure this again.

records.title: WASM Q2, fdlibm trig in WASM against Math.*, E-76
records.text: measured, premise. `tests/bench/trigPremise/` builds musl's FreeBSD-derived `atan`, `sin`, `cos` and `asin` into one freestanding module (9 917 bytes), with `atan2` written as V8's ieee754 has it (musl's 2⁶⁴ shortcut cost 1 ulp for 2⁶⁰ < |y/x| < 2⁶⁴). It compares bit for bit on about 10⁸ inputs per function: random bit patterns, the game range ±8π, ±10⁶, [−1, 1], edges near multiples of π/4, and float32 differences for `atan2`. **Node 22 (V8 12.4):** `atan2` 0 of 80.5 M, `atan` 0 of 102 M, `asin` 0 of 102 M; `sin` and `cos` differ by 1 ulp in 0.9–1.5 % of inputs, so V8's are not fdlibm. **Chrome 155 (V8 15.5, Windows):** no function matches. `atan2` differs by 1 ulp in 16.5 % of float32-difference inputs (W1's case) and returns +0 where fdlibm gives −0 for an underflowing negative ratio; `atan` 3.8 % (game range), `asin` 6.0 % ([−1, 1]), `sin`/`cos` about 3 %. After float32 rounding, `sin`/`cos` agree on all 102 M inputs each. WASM float arithmetic is deterministic, so the variable side is Chrome's `Math.*` (other platforms not checked). Rerun: `node tests/bench/trigPremise/node.mjs`; `node tests/bench/chromeKernel.mjs --module /tests/bench/trigPremise/chrome.mjs --args '{"scale":1}'` (about 50 s).

The worklet is in no `STEP_MS` and absent from every trace; 128 voices take about 0.1 ms of a 2.67 ms quantum (`audioMixerMicrobench` 9 527 ops/s, which times `_mixDirect`, not the product's `_mixBuses`). The claim was predictability (no GC or tier-up stalls), not speed. Reopen if glitches are heard.

records.title: WASM W15, `publishPose` in C
records.text: screened, ceiling. Q1 Predator: `publishPose` took 558 ms of the physics JS thread in the window, about 8 % of it; at 1.3× that is 1.8 %. PH1 (2026-10-01) already showed the limit: kernel +147.1 %, Predator physics −0.8 % (4/8 worse), because Predator respawns all the time and the epoch fast path never latches. A C copy also cannot write the pose SABs from Box2D's memory. Reopen only if the memory decision (E-76 Phase 4) puts the pose buffers in Box2D's heap, and then as a copy removal, not a language claim.

records.text: screened, ceiling. Q1 Predator: navigation is 5.9 % inclusive of the particle worker (`computeFlowfield` 3.7 %), so 1.0 % at 1.2×. In NavStress the search runs against an 8 ms deadline (E-38), so a faster search computes more flow fields per frame and `STEP_MS` cannot fall. records.title: WASM W9, `packInstancedRows` in Pixi
records.text: screened, ceiling. Q1 Predator: 33.9 % of Pixi. E-18 measured that arithmetic is 26 % of the call (painter pack 0.497 ms, gather-only 0.367, identity 0.287) and the rest is the gather through the painter list; X5 showed that cost is cache lines pre-render wrote on another core. Plain WASM at 1.2× on the arithmetic saves 33.9 % × 26 % × 0.17 ≈ 1.5 % of Pixi; 3 % needs that arithmetic 1.42× faster than TurboFan, which nothing on record supports. Reopen if a WASM vertex upload path makes the copy in `_commitPackedBatch` go away (a different claim).

records.title: WASM W3, the cull loop of `collectVisibleEntities`
records.text: screened, ceiling. Q1 Predator: the loop is 7.2 % self of pre-render; at the 1.2× that a ~9-column gather with trivial arithmetic could plausibly gain in plain WASM, that is 1.2 % of the worker. The rest of its 32.1 % inclusive is `collectRenderable` → `_writeRenderable`, which reads JS objects per entity and stays JS. Reopen if a cull-dominated scene shows the loop's self time at 18 % or more of pre-render, and then run Q3 first. The whole render-queue build (collect plus emit, 61 % of Predator pre-render) stays open as W4, blocked on the memory decision.

records.title: WASM plan: L1 (two shipped modules)
records.text: `wasmCoexistence.test.js` now runs both shipped modules (the publish and the gather) and the two test modules in four workers on one memory laid out by the map with the gather's regions, a binned grid and the pattern table. Each worker gathers then publishes its own entities. The gather's dedup stamp advances on every pass, as the frame counter does, so the solo reference runs each worker's 200 passes in the same order, and its per-job write check is on the first pass. Byte for byte equal. A sabotaged copy, worker 2's gather pointed at worker 3's marker slice, fails ("logic0 gather_batch wrote outside its region").

records.title: WASM plan: W5 kernel sitting (E-78)
records.text: `wasm/spatialGather.c` (787 bytes; a candidate, built and checked but not shipped) does the gather of `findNeighborsForOwnedEntities` for a batch of rebuild entities. It uses the JS arithmetic in double, the same NaN-safe index clamps, and the worker's circle patterns in their order, so truncation at `maxNeighbors` happens where JS's does. `spatialGatherWasmMicrobench` runs it as a bench variant on real workers in WASM mode: JS keeps every per-entity decision (stagger, skin reuse), one `gather_batch` call per worker does every rebuild, JS does the bookkeeping, then the shipped WASM publish runs. The memory carries the grid (`rebuildOwnedRows` writes it there in both variants), and per worker a marker, truncation flags and a rebuild list, plus the patterns. Rows and counters match on every one of 45 frames. Alternating processes, 5 rounds (Node 22, AC), the frame of 3 workers over 16 500 entities: Predator settings with drift, 267.1 → 341.9 frames/s, **+28.0 %, 25/25**; every list rebuilt, 31.6 → 39.7, +25.5 %, 25/25. Kernel → scene gate: the frame is the worker's whole step, so about −22 % of spatial, far past 3 %. Next: wiring (Phase 5) and the Predator gate in Chrome.

records.title: WASM plan: N-63 (found preparing W5)
records.text: The C gather has to reproduce the JS dedup marker. The JS marker turned out to fail from stamp frame 4096: an int32 stamp read back from a `Uint32Array` never matched it, so candidates in several cells were published once per cell, for half of every 8 191-frame cycle. Fixed in JS (`processedMarker` is an `Int32Array`), with a test; REVIEW_PLAN N-63. The C compares the 32 bits as they are.

records.title: WASM plan: Q3
records.text: `tests/bench/wasmFloorPremise.mjs`, one case per process. **sway** (W22, real worker, 20 000 decorations): the shipped loop takes 1.74–1.77× the time of the same loop with its float maths replaced by XOR of the loaded words, and 2.51× with the snapshot shuffled. **stamp** (W23, Predator fixture, 3 shadows per entity): the grid walk is 6.6–6.9 % of `stampLightRange`, and 2.20× its load-only floor and 1.48× its store-all floor; selection, nearest tracking and the append are the other 93 %. **gather** (W5, real worker, 16 500 entities, every candidate list rebuilt): a patched copy keeps every load, replays the logged range decisions and publishes the same rows; the shipped method takes 1.026–1.035× its time. **publish** is the calibration: the same floor for `_publishFilteredNeighbors` reads 1.015–1.033, while the shipped WASM module runs the same rows 2.10–2.17× faster in this setup (1.43× in `spatialPublishWasmMicrobench`, which calls the method directly). So a floor ratio near 1 does not mean a loop is memory-bound for WASM: on these loops JS's cost is around the loads, not in the arithmetic. The plan's "within ~1.2× of the floor → screened" rule is withdrawn for gather loops. Outcome: **W5 open and first** (about 18 % of Predator spatial at the publish's 1.4×); **W22 open**; **W23 open, borderline**; **W10 screened (ceiling)**, 2.0 % of Predator Pixi with no painter stress scene on record.

records.title: WASM plan: Q4
records.text: `tests/bench/wasmCallCostMicrobench.mjs`, with the test module `wasm/test/callCost.c`, times one call per argument shape, all sides alternating in one process, 9 rounds. Each side has its own loop literal: the first draft shared one between the JS baseline and `sum4d`, which made that call site polymorphic and read 13–16 ns. Medians of 3 runs, ns per call, JS baseline (four adds, inlined) first. **Node 22:** JS 1.7; `nop0` 0.47 (elided); `sum4i` 3.1, `sum8i` 3.6, `sum4d` 3.4, `sum8d` 4.8, `load1` 3.3. **Chrome 155** (`chromeKernel.mjs`): JS 1.42; `nop0` 0.41; `sum4i` 3.9, `sum8i` 4.8, `sum4d` 4.4, `sum8d` 5.3, `load1` 4.2. So a call from optimized JS costs about 4 ns, 2.5–4 ns more than an inlined JS call. Per frame, per batch or per light it is free (360 lights, about 1.4 µs). Per entity it is about 66 µs a frame at 16.5 k entities, and per particle about 0.26 ms at 65 k, about 6 % of the particle stress scene's worker: batch it. **W17** loses its premise: the export call per command is about 4 ns, so a command drain only pays if the handler's JS work itself is a large share, which needs the SpawnStorm trace first.

records.title: WASM plan: Q2
records.text: No: compiled fdlibm cannot match `Math.*` bit for bit in Chrome. `tests/bench/trigPremise/` builds musl's FreeBSD-derived `atan`, `sin`, `cos` and `asin` into one freestanding module, with `atan2` written as V8's ieee754 has it. musl moved the |y/x| > 2⁶⁰ shortcut to 2⁶⁴, which cost 1 ulp there. `sin`/`cos` need a stack, so the module is outside the T6 rules. The comparison is about 10⁸ inputs per function (random bit patterns, the game range ±8π, ±10⁶, [−1, 1], edges within 2 ulps of multiples of π/4) and, for `atan2`, the differences of float32 values that W1 passes. In **Node 22 (V8 12.4)**, `atan2`, `atan` and `asin` are bit-identical (0 of 80.5 M, 102 M, 102 M); `sin` and `cos` differ by 1 ulp in 0.9–1.5 % of inputs, so V8's are not fdlibm. In **Chrome 155 (V8 15.5, this Windows laptop)** none match. `atan2` differs by 1 ulp in 16.5 % of W1-style inputs, and returns +0 where fdlibm gives −0 for an underflowing negative ratio; `atan` differs in 3.8 % of the game range, `asin` in 6.0 % of [−1, 1], `sin`/`cos` in about 3 %. WASM arithmetic is deterministic, so the difference is Chrome's `Math.*`, which may also differ by platform (only this machine was checked). After rounding to float32, `sin` and `cos` agree everywhere: 0 of 102 M each, in Chrome. Consequences: **W12**'s rotation columns are float32, so fdlibm `sin`/`cos` in WASM can keep them bit-identical in practice (its parity test checks). **W1/W2a** use the angles in double, so their bit-identical gates cannot hold against Chrome. Either their gates move to tolerances, or the WASM result becomes the reference (unlike Chrome's `Math.*`, it is the same everywhere), or the angles stay in JS. That choice is the owner's, at those sittings. The repo's bit-identical golden tests run in Node, whose `atan2` is fdlibm; they do not show what Chrome computes.

It passes, and fails against the old float32 module. records.title: WASM plan: T8
records.text: `tests/node/wasmCoexistence.test.js` runs in `npm run test:node`. It puts the spatial module and two test modules in one memory laid out by the map: `coexistScale`, an `f32x4` map, and `coexistHistogram`, which zeroes its bins and then scatters increments into them. Both are built by `buildWasm.mjs` from `wasm/test/` into `tests/fixtures/wasm/` (`"test": true` in the manifest, never bundled) under the same T6 rules. Every byte starts as a canary. First, one thread runs each of the 12 jobs alone, and each may change only its own region: its worker's entities' rows, its scale output, its bins. Then four `worker_threads` (the spatial0, spatial1, logic0 and particle roles) load all three modules through the product loader and run every job 200 times at the same time; the memory must end byte for byte as the solo run left it. Two sabotaged copies fail as they should. One moves a scale output 64 bytes past its region ("logic0 scale_f32 wrote outside its region"); the other changes one worker's scale factor in the concurrent run only ("the concurrent run differs from the solo run"). The module half of REVIEW_PLAN N-62 is fixed.

records.title: WASM plan: T7
records.text: There is one switch per module in the scene config: `wasm: { spatialPublish }`, from `WASM_DEFAULTS` (default true; typed in `weed.d.ts`; noted in `docs/guide/SPATIAL_HASHING.md`). When it is false, `createSceneSharedBuffers` builds no publish memory, so the spatial worker runs its plain-SAB JavaScript publish, the path 32-bit ids take. The bench page reads `?wasmOff=<name>[,…]` (`runIntegratedWorkerBenchmark --query wasmOff=spatialPublish`) and writes `metadata.wasm` (the switches) and `metadata.wasmRan` (what ran) into every result. MinimalTick in source mode, 3 s + 2 s: default `wasmRan.spatialPublish` true, spatial 2.044 ms; `wasmOff=spatialPublish` false, 2.095 ms (a check that both paths run, not a measurement). `tests/node/wasmSwitch.test.js` builds the scene buffers both ways.

records.title: WASM plan: T5
records.text: `src/util/wasmKernel.js` is the shared loader. `loadWasmKernel(name, url, memory, exports)` compiles each module once per worker and refuses any import other than `env.memory`, naming it; the `Proxy` stubs are gone. It also refuses a missing export. It reads data URLs (the bundle), `file:` URLs in Node (`process.getBuiltinModule`, so real workers can bind modules in kernels and tests) and fetches anything else. `spatialPublishClient.js` keeps its literal `new URL('./spatialPublish.wasm', import.meta.url)` and loads through it. `smokeBundleEmbed.mjs` now requires every `wasm/modules.json` module to be embedded as its committed bytes, raw or in a gzipped worker payload. It passed on all 8 artifacts of a fresh build and correctly found no emcc bytes; it fails on a stale `dist/`, which is the point. `smokeBundleBrowser.mjs` counts "wasm unavailable" (the worker's load-failure log) as fatal; all 8 bundles OK. In source mode, MinimalTick ran with no load error. `tests/node/wasmKernel.test.js` covers file and data URLs, compile-once, the emcc fixture refused for its WASI imports, a missing export, and the real spatial worker binding the module in Node through the loader (worker 1 on the second list slice).

records.title: WASM plan: T9
records.text: `src/util/wasmMemoryMap.js` declares every region of a kernel memory with its owner and size. `layoutRegions` places them in order, each on a 64-byte line; `spatialPublishRegions` is the spatial memory: a 64-byte guard at address 0, then pos, range, rows, cand, and one list slice per spatial worker (`listStride`, passed in `gridMetadata`). Two changes to the shipped layout follow. The 128 KB header that held emcc's stack and statics is now that 64-byte guard, because kernels own no memory since T3. And regions that started on 16-, 4- and 2-byte boundaries, with the workers' lists back to back, now each start on their own line. The guard still matters: the emcc fixture's start function writes at 1024 and 1028, now inside the pose region, so the T3 parity test instantiates it before filling the frame. That test also builds its own map-laid memory of at least 2 pages, because the fixture's import asks for 2. `tests/node/wasmMemoryMap.test.js` checks the layout properties.

records.title: WASM plan: T2 with T6
records.text: `scripts/buildWasm.mjs` builds every module of `wasm/modules.json` (clang `--target=wasm32 -std=c11 -O3 -msimd128 -matomics -mbulk-memory -nostdlib -ffreestanding -ffp-contract=off -Wall -Werror`; wasm-ld `--no-entry --import-memory --shared-memory --max-memory=<manifest>`; wasm-opt `-O3 -g --strip-producers --strip-target-features`, so only the name section stays) and `--check` rebuilds into `tests/results/wasm-build/` and compares bytes. The T6 rules live in `scripts/wasmKernelRules.mjs` (a binary-section reader, no toolchain needed) and run after every build: one import, `env.memory`, shared, with the manifest's maximum; only the listed function exports; no start function, globals, data, tables or own memory; a name section. `tests/node/wasmKernelRules.test.js` plants each violation in a hand-assembled module. On the shipped emcc binary the check reports the N-62 list (five extra imports, a start function, a global, a table, four extra exports, no names), so `--check` fails until T3. A freestanding build of the same source is 883 bytes and deterministic (two builds, same bytes).
