records.title: Box2D's memory sized per scene, DX-MEM
records.text: **kept (hygiene); not timed.** `physics.wasmMemoryMB` (default 128 MB, was 512 fixed) needs the Box2D link with `ALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH` + `IMPORTED_MEMORY` so the import takes a range; the memory itself never grows. That flag left the `.wasm` code and data sections byte-identical (only the import's limits changed) and added growth checks to 22 glue heap reads, none per step. The per-step JS gained one export call (`sbrk(0)` for `MEMORY_PEAK_KB`) and one compare. Nothing for an ABAB to resolve, so none was run (BM-9). Peaks per scene: [`reports/DX-MEM-box2d-memory.md`](./reports/DX-MEM-box2d-memory.md).

records.title: A/A of Predator on exact windows, the session's noise reference
records.text: The session's noise reference, and the first sitting on exact windows (`34bc7229`, `630526e7`: every frame of the window counted, primary `STEP_MS − WAIT_MS`). `runPredatorAbab --name aa-2026-10-24 --vs 6d9c7258 --hyp-rev 6d9c7258`, Predator, headed, source, detailed stats off, 4 pairs, both sides in worktrees of one commit. **NEUTRAL**: logic 4.771 → 4.626 ms (−1.1 %), spatial 5.549 → 5.472 (+0.9 %), physics 8.206 → 7.857 (−2.1 %), renderer 4.307 → 4.109 (+0.1 %), pre-render 5.837 → 5.508 (−2.3 %), each worse in 2 of 4 pairs; presented 60.0 both sides; load within 0.5 %. The paired deltas move together across workers within a run: pairs 1 and 2 read side B +4 to +11 % on every worker, pairs 3 and 4 −6 to −15 %. So the run-to-run swing is the machine's, shared by all workers, and per-worker detection limits at 4 pairs are wide (2.5 × paired sd / √4): logic 9.7 %, spatial 12.2 %, physics 14.5 %, renderer 14.1 %, pre-render 14.8 %. Read a Predator owner against the workers the change cannot reach in the same runs (HOW_WE_MEASURE's drift rule), not against these limits alone.

records.title: BunnyMark's pre-render after the persist series: the collect is 70 %, E-128 and E-98
records.text: A CPU profile of `bunnyMarkScene` (250 000 sprites, all on screen) after the persist series (E-115 to E-117): `runIntegratedWorkerBenchmark --headed --trace-cpu --src --no-collect-detailed-stats`, summarised from 10 s. Pre-render (239 ms/s busy, GC 0): `collectVisibleEntities` **69.9 % self**, its hot lines the row writes inlined there since E-98e/f (`rY[n] = keyY` 10 %, `cPx[n] = pose[0]` 9 %, `cRotS` 8 %, `rIndex` 8 %, `cPy` 7 %, `rType` 7 % of that self time); the persist kernel (`persist_frame`, W4c) 26.1 %; nothing else over 1 %. Pixi (196 ms/s): `_packPoseOnly` 68 %, `updateBuffer` 13 %. **E-128 answered:** the cull-and-collect loop is far past W3's reopen trigger (18 %), so W3 folds into W4b, the collect in C, whose rows and poses need Transform in the kernel's memory: Phase 4, with the collect as its first mover (the plan named spatial first, but W6 screened at 1.4 %). **E-98 closed:** the question in its title is answered, pre-render's full emit at 250 000 sprites takes 21.1 → 5.17 ms per new queue (E-98a–g, then E-115 to E-117), under a frame; what is left of the worker is the collect, W4b.

records.title: Pixi's sprite pack in C on one build, with the rows copied before the upload, E-123 (W9d)
records.text:
**kept (product).** W9d, Pixi's plain sprite pack through `gpuPack.wasm`, rebased onto the emit, stamp and sway regions behind `wasm.pixiPack` (`6d9c7258`) and timed on one build: `runPredatorAbab --vs <rev> --query-a wasmOff=pixiPack --owner renderer`, side A the JavaScript pack, side B the kernel, one worktree for both (no side bias), exact windows, headed, source, detailed stats off, 4 pairs.

**Owner scene first:** `renderQueueStressScene` (48 000 plain sprites, 18 880 in view) puts the renderer at 1.438 → 1.183 ms (−17.7 %, 4/4), under the 3 ms floor, so it is not judged there; the scene has no load knob yet. Predator's renderer (4–5 ms, Pixi packs its sprites) is the owner instead.

**First Predator sitting** (the batch's rows were the shared rows themselves, so the Pixi buffer uploaded from the WebAssembly.Memory): renderer 4.126 → 3.937 ms, **−5.1 %, worse 0/4**, but every worker the change cannot reach slower on the kernel side in every pair: physics +9.5 % (4/4), spatial +6.3 % (4/4), pre-render +6.1 % (3/4), logic +4.7 % (3/4); verdict REGRESSION. The same shape as W9d's 2026-10-23 sitting (logic +5.9 %, 7/8), now with no second directory to blame. The one thing besides the kernel that set W9d apart from the default path was the upload: `_commitPackedBatch` copies pre-render's rows into a private array first.

**Second sitting, with that copy** (`365c4b60`: the kernel packs into the shared rows, the batch copies them into its own array, the buffer uploads that): renderer 4.864 → 3.980 ms, **−10.6 %, worse 1/4**, cv 12/10 %; logic +2.7 % (2/4), spatial −6.1 %, physics −9.5 %, pre-render −3.9 %; presented 60.0 both; load within 0.1 %. Verdict KEPT (product). The runs swung with the machine (pairs 1 and 4 read every worker 4–20 % cheaper on side B, as in the session's A/A), so read against the workers the change cannot reach in the same run: renderer −6.5, −3.9, −11.4, −4.4 % (median **−5.4 %, 4/4**), while those workers' own per-pair median was −9.6, +6.6, +6.3, −15.7 % (no consistent penalty). In the first sitting the same reading was −13.7, −15.4, −7.3, −9.7 % for the renderer with the others +8.8, +7.6, +3.0, +4.4 % in every pair.

So an upload straight from shared memory cost the rest of the engine about 6 % in Predator (most likely Chrome copying shared-memory uploads on other threads; not traced), and the copy removes it while the kernel keeps the renderer's gain. `wasm.pixiPack` stays on. W11's wiring (mesh batches in a mesh memory) uploads from shared views too: it needs the same copy, or a sitting that shows it does not matter.

records.title: The sprite collect in C for scenes without physics, W4b kernel
records.text: **kernel win (W4b, scenes without physics).** `wasm/preRenderCollect.c` is `collectVisibleEntities`' per-entity loop for sprites with no body (straight camera with or without the cull, and E-51's turned copy), writing the main collector as the JS does; a sprite with a layer mask is handed back to `collectRenderable` at its place in the walk. Bit for bit in seven cases (`preRenderCollectWasm.test.js`; an `or0` mutant without the NaN case fails all seven). Wired (`a3ca6cc7`, `44d3ce66`): with physics off, Transform, its pose and Collider move into the render-queue memory (E-112's `componentDataByte` path), and the shipped collect takes the kernel when every column is there and no body or Y-sort needs the JS loop. Kernel, `preRenderCollectWasmMicrobench` (250 000 sprites, the shipped collect with and without the kernel bound, Node 22, 5 alternating rounds): BunnyMark (skipCull, the sprite query's list) **350.6 → 489.4 ops/s, +39.6 %**; a culled camera over a world five times the view 232.4 → 298.9, **+28.6 %**; turned 212.8 → 252.0, **+18.4 %**; each 25/25. BunnyMark's owner pair follows in the scene batch.

records.title: The decal tile premultiply in C, W21c kernel and wiring
records.text: **kernel win.** `wasm/decalPremultiply.c` is `copyPremultiplyRgba` bit for bit: each colour byte `(c·a·257 + 32896) >> 16`, which is c at a = 255 and 0 at a = 0, so the JS's two fast cases are the general one and the SIMD loop has no branch; in 16-bit lanes `(t + (t >> 8)) >> 8` with t = c·a + 128, equal for all 65 536 (c, a) pairs (checked exhaustively). Wired in Pixi (`a49710ac`): each dirty tile is premultiplied from the decal memory (W26) into a scratch tile and copied into the tile's own array, which is uploaded (E-123: no upload from shared memory). Kernel, `decalPremultiplyWasmMicrobench` (decalStampStressScene's 40 tiles of 128 px after eight frames of its stamps, Node 22, 5 alternating rounds, the copy-out included): `copyPremultiplyRgba` **463.5 → 1 873.3 ops/s, +304.2 %** (SIMD, the shipped path), scalar 1 477.7 (+218.8 %), each 25/25.

records.title: Decal stamping wired on a decal memory, W26 kernel on the shipped path
records.text: **kernel win confirmed on the shipped path.** E-120's kernel (`wasm/decalStamp.c`, exact) is wired (`72853643`): the decal tiles move into a WebAssembly.Memory of their own at byte 0 (every worker views them as before), with a copy of each decal texture, the stamp records and the kernel's scratch after them, made once the textures are loaded (`installDecalMemory`). `stampParticleToTile` writes each stamp as a 64-byte record and `flushDecalStamps` stamps the frame's records in one call, then sets the dirty flags of the tiles they touched. `decalStampWired.test.js`: tiles and flags byte for byte against the JS over three frames (one past a flush's capacity, a texture outside the memory). Kernel, `decalStampWasmMicrobench` now through the worker's shipped path (768 stamps a frame, Node 22, 5 rounds): `Decal.stampToTileBuffers` **307.2 → 1 454.4 ops/s, +373.5 %** (25/25; E-120 read +377.9 % on its own wrapper); the scalar loop −10.6 %. The owner pair follows.

records.title: The mesh corner kernel with the UV generation, wired, W11 and E-118 kernels
records.text: **kernel win.** W11's wiring (the mesh memory, the corner kernel in Pixi's MESH layers) and E-118's UV generation are finished and merged (`3937589c`..`63c5f3c8`); both mesh batches now upload arrays of their own, copied out of the mesh memory (E-123). `meshCornersWasmMicrobench` (Node 22, 5 rounds, 25/25 each): the shipped JS rewrite 706.7 ops/s; with E-118's UV generation **877.3 (+24.1 %)**; the kernel 937.1 (+32.6 %); the kernel with the UV generation, the product's call, **1 050.6 (+48.7 %)**, so W11 over E-118 alone is +19.8 %. At a 32-bit arena (E-130) the same call reads 992.5 (−5.5 % against 16-bit). E-130's arena past 65 535 vertices lets meshApiStressScene load the renderer past the 3 ms floor; its owner pair follows.

records.title: The compound-solid raster in C without atan2, W1 kernel
records.text: **kernel win; a pseudo-angle replaces atan2.** An agent's `wasm/test/solidSegments.c` (`bc58a3ac`) ports `collectSolidSegments` with its raster. The polar bins are uniform in angle, so an end's bin comes from its octant and a table of tan(kπ/256), with no `atan2`; the cutoff and the wrap are cross/dot tests. Every variant stamps with the JS's own double `raySegT`, so a bin is identical or flipped: 0 flips on 8 stress-scene frames (98 304 bins) and a 257-light corpus; 468 flips only on 1 040 ends constructed on bin edges, within 1e-16 rad. `solidSegmentsWasmMicrobench` (compoundVisPoly `ringSegments=64` frames, Node 22, 5 rounds, 25/25 each): JS 273.3 frames/s; `f64` (fdlibm atan2) 320.1 (+17.1 %); `pseudo` 415.4 (+52.0 %); `fast` 484.2 (+77.1 %); `f64x2` 501.1 (+83.3 %); **`f32x4` 516.2 (+88.9 %)**. Chrome chooses between them next; not wired.

records.title: The per-light visibility sweep in C, W2a kernel
records.text: **kernel win.** An agent's `wasm/test/visibilitySweep.c` (`0af5dd10`): one call per light covers `buildVisibilityPolygon`, `clipVisibilityToPolar`, `mergeSweep` and `markSeenPolarOwners`. Variants: `f64` (the JS's arithmetic, fdlibm trig), `pseudo` (events ordered by `pseudoAngle`, no atan2/asin per occluder), `pre` (ray-independent edge terms once per light), `simd` (a box's 4 edges as f64x2), `f32` (float32 edge terms, f32x4 box test, double kept for edges whose line passes next to the light). Gate: vertices within 1e-4 plus a float32 ulp (f32: 1e-4 of the distance from the light); 6 000 random scenes, double variants bit-identical except 5 seam ties (area within 1e-5); f32 worst move 6.2e-3 world units. `visibilitySweepWasmMicrobench` (visPolyStressScene's frame, 360 lights, Node 22, 4 rounds, 16/16 each): JS 391.7 frames/s; f64 588.2 (+50.2 %); pseudo 640.0 (+63.4 %); pre 599.6 (+53.1 %); simd 829.5 (+111.8 %); **f32 917.4 (+134.2 %)**. Chrome chooses next; not wired.

records.title: The painter sort in C, W10 kernel
records.text: **kernel win.** An agent's `wasm/test/painterRadix.c` (`9f2ba4ce`): `radixSortIndicesBySortKey`, `radixPainterOrder` and `reinsertChangedSlots`, every variant bit-exact (27 key families × 5 slot-list kinds, 8 mutants caught). `painterRadixWasmMicrobench` (Node 22, 5 rounds, 25/25 each), JS → best variant: predator-rebuild 2 826.8 → **11 426.6 ops/s (simd, +304.2 %)**; predator-reinsert 2 337.1 → 4 738.8 (inplace, +102.8 %; simd +100.0 %); stress-rebuild (300 000 rows) 130.9 → 404.8 (simd, +209.2 %); stress-static 2 672.1 → 3 768.3 (inplace, +41.0 %; simd +30.4 %); stress-move 270.3 → 392.9 (simd, +45.4 %). The scalar port alone: +31 to +181 %. The keys must live in WASM memory for the wiring (they are on the queue SAB today). Chrome chooses next.

records.title: The float32 pass over six shipped kernels
records.text: **the float32 pass on the shipped kernels (the owner's question: what do the kernels gain without the double conversions?).** Two agents wrote float32 and f32x4 variants of six shipped kernels as test modules, each held to a stated tolerance by a test (shipped binaries untouched). Node 22, 5 alternating rounds, against the shipped double kernel: **particle integrate** (W12) tween mix f32 +1.8 %, f32x4 +1.2 % (ties); spin mix f32 +5.7 %, **f32x4 +24.3 %** (25/25; a rotating particle's angle must stay double: `av·currentLife` reaches 3e4 rad); **particle lists** (W13) f32 scalar −22.9 to −26.6 % (0/25, worse), **f32x4 +49.1 % stress, +49.2 % zoomed, +59.9 % turned** (25/25), sparse +2.6 % (tie); **decoration sway** (W22) f32 −3.6 %, **f32x4 +12.9 %** (25/25); **shadow stamp** (W23) f32 +5.8 %, f32x4 +7.3 % (23/25; float reaches only the candidate test); **candidate gather** (W5) f32 −2.0 %, f32x4 −1.2 % (0/25: the gather waits on memory, as W8a found); **mesh corners** (W11) do no arithmetic, the variants only change stores: f32 stores +7.4 % over the shipped kernel, f32x4 −6.3 %. Float32 pays where four lanes replace two over contiguous data (lists, the spin integrate, sway), and not in gathers. These benches have no Chrome entry yet; each winner is decided by its scene pair in Chrome.

records.title: The movers-only grid on today's grid, E-126 kernel and its crossover
records.text: **kernel win under 20 % movers; restored and redesigned for exact bytes.** An agent restored the path of 57d30b14 onto today's grid (`028bc5c6`..`096295a3`): cells kept in id order and merged per touched cell, the per-cell cap handled exactly, the owned list in active-list order, spawns and despawns from the active list, physics' moved list read under a sequence (`e9255fb1`), created, destroyed and reshaped bodies added to it (`580dc881`; so `BODY_MOVED_COUNT` now counts those too). `spatialGridMovers.test.js`: three real spatial workers, 90 frames, the whole publish memory hashed every frame, identical to the full rebuild in four modes; seven one-line mutants caught. `spatialGridMoversMicrobench` (60 000 bodies, one worker, Node 22, 5 rounds, 25/25 or 0/25): the movers path against the full rebuild +778 911 % at 0 %, **+639.2 % at 5 %**, +188.6 % at 10 %, +72.4 % at 15 %, +17.5 % at 20 %, −10.1 % at 25 %, −34.9 % at 35 %, −51.5 % at 50 %, −72.8 % at 100 %. The old 0.35 threshold sat past the crossover (~23 %): `d8f41eb7` sets it to 0.2. Above it the shipped choice ties the full rebuild (50 % −0.5 %, 100 % +0.6 %). The owner pair follows.

records.title: Mesh vertices past 65 535 with 32-bit indices, E-130 built
records.text: **built (reach), untimed in a scene.** An agent's `89d93fcc`..`f20949e6`: `renderer.maxMeshVerts` past 65 535 gives the MeshGeometry arena Uint32 vertex counts and triangle indices (`meshIndexWidth`, chosen once from the config on every thread), up to 1 048 576 vertices; `maxMeshIndices` stays capped at 4 194 304 (the mesh memory must fit the kernel's 512 MB). A config of up to 65 535 vertices binds exactly the old layout (class, offset and length of all 21 columns, checked across 8 configs and through createSceneSharedBuffers). MeshRenderer, triangulation, saves and the corner kernel handle both widths (`rewrite_corners_u32`, the export chosen at bind; the 16-bit function body is byte-identical in the disassembly). The GPU never sees mesh indices: Pixi's MESH batches draw instanced triangles whose corners are resolved on the CPU. `meshIndexWidth.test.js` (9) and `meshCornersWide.test.js` (4), including Pixi's real MESH path on a 66 306-vertex plane. Kernel at 32-bit: −5.5 % against 16-bit on the same meshes (R-0567). meshApiStressScene's `maxVerts`/`maxIndices` knobs now load the renderer past the 3 ms floor (W11's owner pair).

records.title: The sprite collect in C, BunnyMark pair, W4b
records.text: **kept (product).** BunnyMark (250 000 sprites, physics off), one build (`d8f41eb7`), `--query-a wasmOff=preRenderCollect` (side A the JS collect, side B the kernel), exact windows, headed, source, detailed stats off, 4 pairs: pre-render **5.252 → 4.741 ms, −9.4 %, worse 0/4**, cv 1/1 %; renderer −0.4 % (2/4); presented 60.0 both; VISIBLE_ENTITIES and RENDER_QUEUE_SIZE 250 000 both sides. records.title: The mesh corner kernel in meshApi at four times the meshes, W11
records.text: **kept (product).** meshApiStressScene loaded past the floor with E-130's 32-bit arena (`count=4&maxVerts=262144&maxIndices=1310720`: four times the meshes, 5 280 entities), one build (`d8f41eb7`), `--query-a wasmOff=meshCorners` (side A the JS rewrite with E-118's UV generation, side B the kernel), exact windows, headed, source, 4 pairs: renderer **36.445 → 34.028 ms, −7.1 %, worse 1/4**, cv 1/9 %; logic +1.1 % (3/4); load equal (BODY_COUNT 800, ENTITIES_PROCESSED 5 280). Presented frames 51.3 → 50.1 (−1.8 %, fewer in 4/4): under the 3 % regression bar, and the scene is past what the GPU draws at 60 at this load; noted, as E-82 is the reason the guard exists. The kernel (R-0567) is +19.8 % over E-118's JS on the rewrite.

records.title: Decal stamping in C, decalStampStressScene pair, W26
records.text: **kept (product), with a load key that moved because of the change.** decalStampStressScene (768 seeded stamps a tick, 40 tiles of 128 px), one build (`d8f41eb7`), side A `wasmOff=decalStamp,decalPremultiply` (the JS stamp, no decal memory), side B `wasmOff=decalPremultiply` (the kernel), exact windows, headed, source, 4 pairs: particle **4.590 → 1.681 ms, −63.7 %, worse 0/4**, cv 12/3 %; renderer 2.821 → 2.159 ms (under the floor, not judged). The gate said FAIL (load) on DECAL_TILES_DIRTY 37.0 → 23.0 (−37.7 %). The stamping work is the same on both sides (the driver's seeded stamps; the sampled PARTICLES_STAMPED averages 579 and 577 a frame). What moved is what Pixi sees at its sweep: the JS path sets a tile's dirty flag after every stamp, so Pixi's claims raced the stamping and re-dirtied tiles came back the same frame; side A uploaded exactly its cap, 32 tiles, every frame. The kernel publishes each touched tile once, after the frame's batch: about 22 uploads from about 24 dirty. The tiles end in the same bytes (decalStampWired.test.js), so the batch also removes redundant uploads, which is the renderer's drop. Recorded as kept on the particle owner with this explanation rather than as a load failure.

records.title: Predator gate for the batch of 2026-10-24
records.text: **passed (NEUTRAL at 8 pairs).** The Predator gate for the batch of 2026-10-24: every engine change since the gate reading (`5b3b3633`: W9d's copy is in it) against `d8f41eb7` (W11 with E-118, W4b's memory and collect, W26, W21c, E-126, E-130, entityIdWidth auto), both sides in worktrees, exact windows, headed, source, 8 pairs (4, then `--append` 4: the first 4 flagged pre-render +6.6 %, 3/4, which "vs the others" read +4.4 %, inside the session's 4.8 % relative limit). At 8 pairs: logic +3.8 % paired (5/8 worse) / −0.5 % vs the others; spatial −0.9 % / −2.0 %; physics +0.8 % / −1.2 %; renderer −0.6 % / **−1.8 % (7/8 lower)**; pre-render +2.6 % (5/8) / +1.7 % (2/8 lower); presented 60.0 both; load within 0.2 %. No worker past its limit.

records.title: The decal premultiply in C at resolution 1, W21c pair
records.text: **kept (product), with a cost on the particle worker written down.** decalStampStressScene at `resolution=1` (tiles of 256 px, `360a2461`'s knob, which puts the renderer past the floor), one build, `--query-a wasmOff=decalPremultiply` (side A copyPremultiplyRgba, side B the kernel), exact windows, headed, source, 4 pairs: renderer **6.959 → 3.361 ms, −51.3 %, worse 0/4**, cv 1/4 %, while Pixi uploaded more tiles a frame (sampled 25.6 → 27.2, +7 %; DECAL_TILES_DIRTY 28.3 → 34.3, which failed the load band: a faster sweep sees more of the frame's dirty tiles, the same stamps on both sides). The particle worker read **+6.0 % (4/4, cv 2 %)**, about +0.25 ms, on code W21c does not touch: most likely the faster sweep now reads the tiles while the stamp kernel is still writing them, so the two cores pass the same cache lines (X5). The slowest worker of the frame goes from 6.96 ms (Pixi) to 5.84 ms (particle), −16 %. At the default resolution (0.5) the renderer read 2.282 → 1.153 ms under the floor. The Predator gate of the batch (decals on) passed with the renderer −1.8 % against the others.

records.title: The movers-only grid at 65 000 bodies, E-126 pair (under the floor)
records.text: **kept (kernel); the scene under the floor at the body cap.** movedBodiesStillScene at 65 000 bodies with every 20th moving (`moverEvery=20`, 5 %; the knob needed `61e95a07`, which lists MovedTicker for the workers), side A `097df89a` (the full rebuild), side B `d8f41eb7` (the movers path, threshold 0.2), both in worktrees, exact windows, headed, source, 4 pairs: spatial **2.514 → 1.048 ms (−58 %)**, under the 3 ms floor and so not judged; physics 5.522 → 5.578 ms (+1.8 %, 3/4: the moved list's sequence and the created/destroyed/reshaped bodies it now carries); load equal (BODY_COUNT 65 000). Box2D refuses more than 65 535 bodies, so no setting of this scene reaches 3 ms on the base: a protocol ceiling, and the claim is the kernel's (R-0572: +639.2 % at 5 % movers, +17.5 % at 20 %). Predator (47 % moved) takes the full rebuild; the batch's Predator gate passed.

records.title: copyTypeActiveListToBuffer with TypedArray.set, screened at the desk, E-124
records.text: **screened (ceiling), at the desk.** The copy is 2.4 % of logic (Q1's own share) and the `set` version won 20.9 % in its kernel, so the most it can save is about 0.5 % of logic, under every detection limit the session's A/A gave (logic 7.0 % against the others at 4 pairs). It also costs what E-104 removed: `buffer.set` needs a source view of the type list's live length, a `subarray` allocated per type per query per frame in every logic worker (logic garbage is 0.2 MB/s since E-104/E-105). Neither side of that trade can be seen in a scene, so no sitting is spent on it. Reopen if a profile shows the copy past 10 % of a worker (a scene with many large precomputed queries).

records.title: The sprite collect in C with bodies and the Y-sort foot line, W4b kernel (Phase 4)
records.text:
**Kernel win; Predator pair pending.** W4b's collect kernel now takes scenes with physics. Phase 4 put Transform's state block, RigidBody's, Collider's and both published pose buffers in Box2D's block, and workers bind Transform's heap pose on the block's buffer. So `collect_sprites` reads a body's latched pose and the one before it, and interpolates as `_displayPose` does.

The Y-sort foot line (`_storeEntitySortY`, `spriteSortFootY`, then `Math.round` with its halves and −0) is computed in C from the emit kernel's frame sizes. A sprite whose frame is not resolved yet goes to `collectRenderable`, as a masked one does. Each mode is a compiled copy of the walk, so the plain path carries no new test.

`preRenderCollectWasmMicrobench`, 250 000 sprites, 5 alternating rounds, every case won, checksums equal. Node; the machine was loaded by two agents' builds and tests.

| case | js ops/s | wasm ops/s | |
|---|---|---|---|

records.title: The bullet tick with its linecasts in C, W19 kernel (Node and Chrome)
records.text:
**Kernel win; wiring after E-129.** `wasm/bulletTick.c` puts `BulletPool.tick` and its `Ray.linecastDir` in one call per frame:
- the pool walk;
- the grid DDA of `_traverseGrid`;
- the filters of `_checkCellEntities`;
- the circle, box and single-polygon tests;
- the impact records;
- the active list;
- the slots that hit, which go back for the JS's `returnToPool` in walk order.

A cast that meets a compound polygon or a chain hands its bullet back before anything is written for it. `bulletTickWasm.test.js` checks the kernel bit for bit against the shipped tick: 4 000 bullets among 1 500 circles, boxes and rotated polygons, at three time steps and with every variant. A 0.02 % change to the box test fails it. The hand-back is tested too.

The pass covered:
- **flags:** two variants, both bit-identical: the box test's reciprocals once per ray (`hoist`), and no ray stamps (`nostamp`). A repeated test gives the same distance, which is never closer.
- **SIMD:** none. The walk is scalar per bullet, with a gather per candidate, so no lanes fill (the float32 pass's lesson).
- **float32:** not tried. Scalar f32 buys nothing over f64 on x86, and it would give up bit-identity.

`bulletTickWasmMicrobench`: bulletStressScene's world (4000 × 3000 px, cells of 128, 240 circles and boxes, four walls), a pool of 40 000 at 1500 px/s.

| | storm, 40 000 live | sparse, 4 000 live |
|---|---|---|
| Chrome 155, js | 262.7 ops/s | 2 074.6 ops/s |
| wasm | +61.0 % | +38.9 % |
| wasm_hoist | +62.1 % | +40.2 % |
| wasm_nostamp | +62.0 % | +40.2 % |
| **wasm_lean** (both) | **+63.5 %** | **+40.6 %** |
| Node, 5 alternating rounds | +73.7 to +80.2 % | +52.5 to +53.5 % |

Chrome ran every variant in one page over 7 alternating rounds, each 7/7 over the JS, checksums equal. The variants differ by about 2 %; `lean` was first in both cases and ships (9bc70782). The machine carried agents' builds and tests during both sittings.

An earlier smoke had inserted the walls into every cell their largest half extent covered; the bench now inserts each box by its own extents (81ae305d).

Next:
- E-129 widens the bullet pool.
- Then the wiring: the bullet columns in the bodies' part of Box2D's block, a dispatch in `BulletPool.tick` behind `wasm.bulletTick`, and a `bulletStressScene` pair on one build (owner particle).

records.title: The spawn sort by packed keys on the shipped method, E-125 kernel A/B
records.text:
**Kernel win; spawnStorm pair pending.** H-14 has been reapplied to the shipped `_processSpawnSoA`. Each spawn becomes a key, `entityIndex * span + position`, in a `Float64Array`. Its length is the batch capacity, a power of two from 256 that doubles, and it doubles as the span. The typed array's native numeric sort then gives the order the stable comparator sort over a permutation gave: by index, then by position. The position comes back exactly. `spawnSortParity.test.js` passes unchanged.

The 2026-10-14 kernel timed the sort strategies apart from the worker. The new `spawnSoAMicrobench` times the whole shipped method on a real logic worker: the sort, the duplicate drop, and the merges into the active list and the class lists. Each class owns a quarter of a 65 536-slot space, as an entity type owns its pool's range, and the batch draws 2 % repeats.

Writing the bench turned up two artifacts of a bare worker, both fixed before timing:
- **Merge scratch:** the merge allocated its scratch, because the worker's init sizes it and a bare worker never ran init.
- **Class layout:** random classes per index made one merge per spawn.

Old tree against new, alternating processes, 5 rounds, checksums equal. Node; agents' builds and tests were on the machine.

records.title: The split upload for plain sprites, BunnyMarkStressC and Predator pairs, E-82b
records.text:
**kept (product).** The split upload for sprites without pose interpolation (`wasm.gpuPackSplit`, default on), built as the 2026-10-24 design note asked: in the packer.

How it works:
- `gpuPack.wasm` gains `pack_sprites_split` and its scatter (b0ec6ca8). They write each plain sprite's pose (x, y, rotC, rotS: 16 bytes) and, when asked, its statics (44 bytes, E-82's static order). The values are bit for bit those of the 15-float row: `gpuPackSplit.test.js`, through the gather and the scatter.
- Pre-render writes the main sprites into its GPU queue as the two streams (`GPU_FLAG_SPLIT`, the statics' generation in the header). It writes the statics only into a GPU queue buffer that lacks the queue's `staticGen` for the same rows.
- The glow split's list (the rows that are not glows, in order) follows from the types and so from the generation. A painter-sorted frame always writes both streams.
- Pixi's entity batch is E-82's two-stream batch with a 16-byte pose, the previous xy read from the current one (the pose shader's mix at alpha 1). It copies and uploads the statics only when the generation or the row count moves (a37217a6).
- A frame whose statics change uploads the same 60 bytes a sprite as before. A nearest atlas, whose poses snap, keeps 15-float rows.

Measuring tool: `?bunnies=` on BunnyMarkStressCScene (f7d7ae5d). At 100 000 bunnies the split left Pixi under the floor (headless 1.93 → 0.80 ms).

**Owner pair.** BunnyMarkStressC at 250 000 bunnies (still camera, no Y-sort), one build (a37217a6 as f57b390f), side A `wasmOff=gpuPackSplit`, headed, source, detailed stats off, exact windows, 4 pairs, `--owner renderer`:
- renderer 4.953 → 1.701 ms, **−65.6 %**, worse 0/4, cv 2/2 %;
- pre-render 9.212 → 7.006 ms, **−23.8 %**, worse 0/4 (16 bytes written a sprite on a persist frame instead of 60);
- logic 2.501 → 2.533 (under the floor); 250 000 rows on both sides.

**Predator guard.** Its sprites take Pixi's SoA path into the split batch, painter-sorted, so their statics move every frame. Renderer, one build, 4 pairs: NEUTRAL. Renderer 3.517 → 3.480 ms (−3.1 % paired, 2/4 worse, +1.1 % against the others); no worker 3 % worse in 3 of 4; load within 0.6 %.

Tests:
- `instancedSpriteSplit.test.js` (the batch on every path, the static uploads);
- `gpuPackSplitWired.test.js` (pre-render's GPU queue on the real worker: the streams equal the rows of the switch-off run, which buffer rewrites its statics when, a painter-sorted frame every time);
- `gpuPackSplitPixi.test.js` (Pixi's commit of split and row frames, and a plain batch never reading a split frame as rows).

Screenshots of BunnyMark (on and off), Predator, and painterMove on WebGPU draw as before.

Left:

- 35 % on the generation check (`Atomics.load(gen, minE)` and `maxE`, two random entities per pair);
- 3 % and 2 % on the listen flags.

A C classification cannot take the dispatch: the callbacks are game code and stay JS, so a kernel would hand back a list the JS still walks and calls. What it could take is the generation check and the bookkeeping, at most about 40 % of the function: about a quarter of logic in the hunt scene, and 1 to 1.5 % of Predator's (Q1's 2.6 to 3.7 % ceiling). The generation check reads two scattered words per pair, which C would also wait on.

Next, before any port: a JS screen of that line on `contactsMicrobench` (a plain read of `gen`, or the generations copied beside the pair slots). It is cheaper, it tells whether the line is the load or the memory, and the port's ceiling follows from it.

records.title: The per-light occluder gather in C, visPoly and compoundVisPoly pairs, W2b
records.text:
**kept (product).** Each light's neighbour gather in C (`visibilityGather.wasm`, `wasm.visibilityGather`, default on), with physics and raycasted lighting.

**Q1 after W2a** (a headed CPU trace of visPolyStressScene, 261 ms/s busy in pre-render):
- `_buildVisibilityPolygonsSwept`'s JS gather: 35.6 %;
- the sweep, already in C: 29.7 %;
- `_displayPose`: 19.2 %;
- `clearPolarBins`: 4.6 %.

**Built** (87864b65, a7a2156f, 00f2825a, aa94a7db, reworded as 4a937081):
- `createVisibilityMemory` takes a place, so W2a's memory can be laid in Box2D's block. `visibilitySweep` and `solidSegments` import up to 32 768 pages.
- With physics and raycasted lighting, the render-queue spec lays in the block LightOccluder's block, the visibility memory's region (sized by `visibilityMemoryOpts`, which pre-render places it with) and the gather's table, results and 48-byte event records.
- The kernel walks one light's neighbour row. It takes the display pose (preRenderCollect.c's), the active and block checks, the reach cull, and packs circles, boxes and convex polygons as `writeOrientedBoxVerts` and `writePolygonVerts` do.
- Compound solids and self-lit candidates come back as events in neighbour order. JS rasters the solids (W1) and writes the self-lit items.
- The polar bins are cleared before a light's first solid, not for every light (`skipPolarBins`).
- Without physics, or with a column outside the memory, the JS gather runs.

`visibilityGatherWired.test.js`: on a real worker with every column in one memory, the kernel's polygons and self-lit lists are the JS gather's bit for bit. That holds over six frames of a mixed scene, a self-lit cap of 40, a scene with no compound solid, and W1 off.

**Pairs.** One build (4a937081 as aa94a7db), side A `wasmOff=visibilityGather`, headed, source, detailed stats off, exact windows, 4 pairs, `--owner preRender`:
- `visPolyStressScene`: pre-render 3.765 → 2.839 ms, **−24.3 %**, worse 0/4, cv 1/1 %. The other workers are under the floor and unchanged; 1 060 bodies.
- `compoundVisPolyStressScene?ringSegments=64`: pre-render 1.986 → 1.964 ms (−1.1 %), under the floor. The W1 raster dominates there; not worse.

The headless smoke had read 3.860 → 2.755 ms. Screenshots of visPoly look the same on and off. Predator does not run raycasted lighting, so no gate.

records.title: The contact stay loop without Atomics.load, contactsMicrobench, E-131
records.text:
**kept-kernel (the scene pairs follow).** From W18's Q1b (R-0601): in ContactDrainHuntScene, the stay loop's generation check (`Atomics.load(gen, minE)` and `maxE`) was 35 % of `_processBox2dCollisionCallbacks`. That record guessed the cost was the scattered reads; the screen says it was the atomic loads.

`contactsMicrobench` gained a `plainGen` variant (9eac8461): the shipped method with `gen[minE]` and `gen[maxE]` read plainly. Real LogicWorker, Predator fixture pairs, `runKernelVariants --variants base,plainGen`, 5 alternating rounds, checksums equal (341220998):

| case | base | plainGen | | won |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| contact (bodies touching) | 6 619.6 ops/s | 8 674.5 | **+31.0 %** | 5/5 |
| dense (+24 px reach) | 1 125.5 | 1 452.1 | **+29.0 %** | 4/5 |

The kernel's whole frame (ring drain, begins and ends, the stay walk and its callbacks) loses 22 to 24 % of its time.

Why a plain read is safe: physics bumps a generation when it recreates a body. A bump the walk misses is caught on the next frame's walk, exactly as one landing just after an `Atomics.load` would be. The value is an aligned 32-bit word, so it cannot tear.

Applied to the stay loop only (b25528f1). The foreign sweep (`_foreignValid`, every 30 frames) and the begin path's `_entityGen` keep `Atomics.load`.

records.title: Contact classification in C dropped: E-131 took the generation check in JS, W18
records.text: **dropped.** On its owner scene (R-0601) the classifier was 62.8 % of logic. 55 % of that function is the game's `onCollisionStay` dispatch, which stays JS whatever classifies; 35 % was the generation check, and that was `Atomics.load` itself: E-131 reads the generations plainly in JS (contactsMicrobench +29 to +31 %, ContactDrainHuntScene logic −12.9 %, R-0604). | logic (2 × ~400 ms/s) | GameObject's component getter (`gameObject.js:612`, 95 % on the `_componentCache[name]` load) **10.4 %**, game code (`findACivilianToShoot` 9.1 %, `Person.tick` 7.3 %), `neighborCount` 6.9 %, `_tickIntervalBucket` 6.3 %, `fsm.tick` 5.8 %, `getNeighbor` 5.4 %, ray `_circleRayDistance` 4.2 %, `_checkCellEntities` 3.2 %, `_processBox2dCollisionCallbacks` 3.2 % |

Leads it gives, in the order they can move Predator's frame:
1. The shadow stamp is nearly half of pre-render, in C already: its algorithm (casters a light walks, the sort) is what is left.
2. The component getter is a tenth of logic. Two engine fixes lost in Predator: L4's pre-filled caches (R-0284) and E-69's slot array (R-0400). The engine's own methods and the demo call the four core components most (`spriteRenderer`, `collider`, `rigidBody`). Explicit getters on fields the constructor declares are the one shape not tried.

4. Pixi's sprite pack and upload in Predator write statics every frame, because Pixi sorts there (`sortSprites: 'pixi'`), so E-82b cannot skip them.

records.title: The shadow stamp without the kept-slice sort under maxShadowsPerEntity, kernel and Predator, E-133
records.text:
**kept (product).** From Predator's profile (R-0607): the shadow stamp (`stamp_light_range`) is 46.7 % of pre-render, and `quicksort_order` showed apart at 3.1 %.

The argument (E-110's, for another sort): with `maxShadowsPerEntity` (Predator: 3), each light's kept casters go only into their own nearest-light slots (`note_nearest` / `noteNearest`). Those order by (distance, light index) whatever order the casters arrive in. So `takeClosest`'s quicksort of the kept slice, after the quickselect, changed nothing there. The quickselect still picks the same casters. The sort now runs only without a per-entity cap, where the kept order is the stamp's order. C and JS changed alike (c7b4e94b). `gpuShadowCasters.test.js` checks that the unordered take keeps the same casters, ties included, over 200 random rounds.

**Kernel.** `shadowStampWasmMicrobench` on the Predator fixture (48 lights, 512 per light, 3 per entity), the tree before (a5a646c9) against this one (`kernelAB2.sh`), 5 alternating rounds. Checksums were equal on every run (2692520044): the stamped rows are the same.

| variant | before | after | | won |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| wasm (shipped) | 1 816 ops/s | 2 233 | **+22.9 %** | 5/5 |
| js (fallback) | 915 | 1 021 | **+11.6 %** | 5/5 |

**Predator, the owner pair (pre-render).** Both sides from worktrees (`--vs a5a646c9 --hyp-rev 78795bfd`, the same code as c7b4e94b), headed, source, detailed stats off, exact windows, 4 pairs:
- pre-render 4.355 → 4.017 ms: **−12.0 %** paired, 3/4 better, cv 11/6 %; **−7.0 %** against the other workers, lower 4/4, past the session's 4.8 % relative limit;
- renderer −6.9 % (1/4 worse), spatial −3.8 %, physics −2.0 %, logic +0.0 %: none worse;

The −12 % paired is noisy; against the other workers, −7 % is what the kernel predicts: about a fifth of a stamp that is half of pre-render.

records.title: The cull's cost on bigWorldCullStressScene: the collect follows the world at a fixed visible count, E-127
records.text:
**note (Q1, the ceiling).** bigWorldCullStressScene (33241ca1: static sprites on a grid, `?sprites=`, `?view=` the share in view; physics off, no spatial worker), headless, source, detailed stats on, one run each:

| sprites | view | queue rows | pre-render STEP_MS | COLLECT_MS | EMIT_MS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 250 000 | 5 % | 18 643 | 2.333 | 2.033 | 0.148 |
| 500 000 | 2.5 % | 18 643 | 4.017 | 3.695 | 0.169 |

With the visible count fixed, doubling the world takes the collect from 2.03 to 3.70 ms (+82 %), while the emit holds (persist frames: the rows do not change). The collect is about 90 % of pre-render there, and it grows with every sprite in the world: about 7.4 ns a sprite at 500 000. The bench commit's message read the 250 000 / 500 000 pair at a fixed share, where the visible count doubled too; this pair is the clean one.

The ceiling is a cull that costs what the view holds. The 2026-09-27 grid (R-0241) lost sprites to the cell cap; spatial's grid includes sprites (`rebuildOwnedRows` bins every collider or SpriteRenderer) but caps cells too, and a scene like this one has no spatial worker. Next: the design (a grid of pre-render's own, kept for sprites that do not move, with the collect kernel walking only the cells in view).

records.title: WASM W8b, the 32-bit spatial publish and gather, E-76
records.text: **kept (product).** `wasm/spatialPublish.c` and `wasm/spatialGather.c` are written once over the id width (always_inline, a constant flag) and export `publish_batch_u32`, `gather_batch_u32` and `order_batch_by_cell_u32` beside the 16-bit ones (`5dcff194`). The memory map sizes the rows, lists, rebuild lists and order scratch by the id width; `createSpatialPublishMemory` accepts 4-byte ids and the modules' 2 GB import; the clients bind the `_u32` exports when `entityIdBytes()` is 4. Before this, a scene past 65 535 entities took the JS publish and gather silently. Owner pair, `stationarySpatialWideScene` (new, `79088100`: 70 000 stationary entities, 32-bit ids by 'auto', two spatial workers, physics off), Chrome, headed, source, 4 pairs, one build, `wasmOff=spatialPublish,spatialGather` on side A: spatial **18.648 → 12.234 ms, −33.0 % paired, worse 0/4**, cv 3/6 %; every other worker under the 3 ms floor; `ENTITIES_PROCESSED` 70 000 and `VISIBLE_ENTITIES` 21 318 on both sides. The JS side ran at 104–106 % load (FPS 57–58), so the gap is a floor. Parity: `spatialGatherWasm.test.js` runs 70 000 entities on three real spatial workers at 32-bit ids, and the WASM publish, the WASM gather and the gather in cell order publish what the plain buffers' JS path publishes, rows and counters, on every frame (detailed stats on, so the WASM publish's E-02 recount fills `neighborsFoundThisFrame`). The 16-bit kernels are unchanged (Node, `kernelAB2`, 5 alternating rounds against the parent): publish WASM 6 292 → 6 218 ops/s median, the gather frame 252 → 255 frames/s, both inside the rounds' spread. Found on the way and fixed first (`7b91a58b`): `box2dBlockPlan` returned null when the spatial part took Box2D's block past 2 GB, so the render-queue part lost the block too. The spatial part now stays out alone. A scene whose rows do not fit 2 GB (`count × (1 + maxNeighbors) × 4` bytes, twice: rows and candidates) still runs the JS path.

records.title: WASM W21a, ensureCompoundSolid's premise in the remesh scene, E-76
records.text: **screened (premise), no change.** One headed CPU trace (source, detailed stats off, 6 s warm-up, 8 s window) of `compoundVisPolyStressScene?remeshEvery=1&ringSegments=64`, the worst case on record: island 0 re-applies its polygons every tick, the pool-wide fixture revision moves, and every lit compound rebuilds its outline every frame. `ensureCompoundSolid` was **8.7 ms of pre-render's 1 490 ms busy (0.6 %)**, and it does not appear among Pixi's top functions (Pixi also rebuilds the fill there). Pre-render's time is W1's `collect_solid_f32x4` (74.1 %) and `sweep_light_f32` (9.6 %). A WASM rebuild cannot move a 0.6 % share. What the trace showed instead: Pixi's `_buildSelfLitBatch` was 43.8 % of Pixi's busy time (106 ms/s) and Pixi's `updateBuffer` 27.3 %. The fill loop (lines `data[o] = originX + …`, `fill[(v + k) * 2]`) is about 54 % of the batch: each fill triangle of each (light, compound) pair is written as three fresh 13-float vertices, though a ring's vertices are shared by about three triangles. Opened as E-135.

records.title: The self-lit fill as shared vertices, the compoundVisPoly pair, E-135
records.text: **kept (product).** `ensureCompoundSolid` builds, with the fill, its shared vertices (`fillPts`, `fillPtCount`) and per soup vertex its shared one (`fillIdx`). A soup vertex joins an earlier one only when both floats are the same bits, so the triangles keep the soup's order and every attribute Pixi computes from a vertex is the same. `_buildSelfLitBatch` writes a compound's shared vertices once per light and its triangles by index. Every shape now stops a light at either budget, vertices (`maxVerts`) or indices (`3 × maxVerts`), since an indexed fill can take more than three indices a vertex. Commits `e44b0dcf` (the golden, before the change) and `c3d6dd06` (the change). Golden, `selfLitFillTriangles.test.js`: a real Pixi worker with two lights over a ring, a jittered grid and an unshared pair of compounds, a circle, a box and a polygon, then a remesh. It draws the same 142 triangles with the same 13 floats a vertex, before and after the change, from **152 vertices instead of 352** (the fills 300 → 100). Owner pair, `compoundVisPolyStressScene?ringSegments=128`, Chrome, headed, source, detailed stats off, both sides from worktrees (`--vs e44b0dcf --hyp-rev c3d6dd06`), 4 pairs: Pixi **3.361 → 2.875 ms, −15.6 % paired** (better in 3/4), **−16.2 % against the other workers (4/4)**, cv 8/5 %. Pre-render +1.9 % (2/4) and physics −2.5 % (2/4), both unreachable from the change. `BODY_COUNT` 64 and `ENTITIES_PROCESSED` 65 on both sides. The vertex buffer Pixi uploads shrinks with the vertices (`vbuf.update(vtx × 52)`); the index upload is unchanged.

records.title: WASM W28, the physics glue's premise (one call per body), E-76
records.text: **screened (premise), no change.** `bodyForceCallMicrobench` (`f6c28028`): the shipped `box2dWasm.wasm` in Node, single-threaded, the Predator fixture's 16 551 bodies as dynamic circles, every one with an acceleration. Five alternating rounds of `applyForcesAndTorque`'s linear part, with the call and without it. With the call, **7.4 ns a body** (one `body_apply_force_center` per body); the same loads and tests with the force summed instead, **2.3 ns**. So the call costs **5.1 ns a body**, and that includes Box2D's own work (the slot's body lookup, the wake test, the force add), which a batched C export would still do. Q4 put the boundary itself at 3.4–4.8 ns for a call of this shape. The most one C call over the force ring can save is therefore about 3–4 ns a body: **about 60–70 µs a step** at Predator's body count with every body accelerating, **about 2 % of Predator's physics** (3.7 ms). That is under the 3 % keep bar, and under the 14.5 % that Predator's A/A can resolve for physics at 4 pairs. `publishMovedBodies` and `snapshotPrevPose` are plain JS loops with no boundary (2–5 % and less of the physics JS thread in Q1b); at the 1.5–2× that WASM gives such loops they add 1–2 %, each needing its own glue and a Box2D rebuild in both builds. Reopen if a scene has a much larger share of accelerating bodies in physics.

records.title: SpawnStorm's createBody warnings: a despawn during the create is not a failure (found screening W17)
records.text: **kept (hygiene, a bug fix).** Found while screening W17 (Q1b's SpawnStorm trace had 86 % of `syncBodySlot` on its `console.warn` line). The scene runner now prints the physics host's `[weedjs-box2d]` warnings (`55a83624`), and SpawnStorm warned `createBody failed; retry next step` about 470 times a second. A diagnostic in a scratch worktree showed every one with `entityActive`, `rbActive` and `colActive` at 0, a circle of radius 6. The entity was despawned while physics, beside the logic workers, created its body; `createBodyForEntity` found nothing active and returned false, and `syncBodySlot` warned and marked a retry that had nothing to do. Fix (`d11f9387`): a false create on an entity that no longer wants a body is left alone (the despawn marks the slot); a failure on a live entity still warns once and retries. `bodyCreateRace.test.js` runs the shipped block (`body-create-start/end`) and fails on the old one. Pair, `spawnStormScene?storm=4000`, Chrome, headed, source, worktrees (`--vs 76194d2a --hyp-rev d11f9387`), 4 pairs: warnings **112 083 → 0**; physics **3.600 → 3.460 ms (−6.9 %, worse 1/4)** while it holds **2.2× the bodies** (`BODY_COUNT` 529 → 1 184: physics now creates them before the storm despawns them, so the runner's load gate read FAIL on that key, an output of the fix, not its input); logic 10.896 → 10.361 ms (−7.6 %, worse 1/4). No worker worse.

records.title: Static scenery culled through pre-render's grid (static isStatic), the big-world pair, E-127
records.text: **kept (product).** The owner's choice (2026-10-24): an opt-in flag. A type that declares `static isStatic = true` does not move after onSpawned. Pre-render bins those types' entities by position in a grid of its own (`staticSceneryGrid.js`, about 8 entities a cell) when the scene's static counter moves (`staticScenery.js`: a static entity spawned or despawned, or moved, resized or given another sprite through the GameObject setters; writing its Transform columns directly is not seen). Each frame the collect walks the published sprite list's moving entities plus the static entities in the cells that meet the view, widened by the largest static half extent, in entity order. The static types' runs in the sorted list are skipped by binary search, and the static entities come out of a bitset in ascending order. Both collects, the JS and the kernel, still test every listed entity, so they draw the linear cull's set in its order. `staticSceneryCull.test.js` compares the collectors bit for bit at seven cameras (zooms 0.3 to 2.5, two turned, past the world's corner, far from everything), on both paths, and after a static entity moves; the walk is asserted to run and to leave entities out. Commits `65fb25f8` (the scene's `?static=1`) and `54e1b49f` (the change). Owner pair, `bigWorldCullStressScene?sprites=500000&view=0.025`, Chrome, headed, source, one build with `static=0` on side A and `static=1` on side B, 4 pairs: pre-render **4.230 → 1.346 ms, −68.0 % paired, worse 0/4**, cv 3/4 %; `VISIBLE_ENTITIES` 18 643 on both sides; every other worker under the 3 ms floor. What is left of the collect at 1.3 ms is its per-visible work (18 643 rows), not the world. One limit: the view box is widened by the largest static half extent, so one huge static sprite widens it for all of them; binning the large ones apart would remove that.

records.title: WASM W17, the command ring drain's premise, E-76
records.text: **screened (premise), no change.** Q1b's SpawnStorm trace (`spawnStormScene`, the one scene where the drain shows): `drainCommandRing` is 10.0 % of physics (138 ms over the window), and its hot lines are the ring protocol, not the export call: `Atomics.store(i32, base, read + cap)` 23 %, `Atomics.store(i32, HDR_READ, read + 1)` 23 %, `Atomics.load(i32, base)` 22 %, `Atomics.load(i32, HDR_READ)` 15 %, together 83 % of the function. Q4 put a JS → WASM call at about 4 ns, and `bodyForceCallMicrobench` (R-0614) put one call with Box2D's own work at 5.1 ns. A drain in C would turn those four atomics into plain wasm atomic instructions, but only if every handler moved into C with it (they call Box2D exports from JS and some keep JS-side state: joints, particles), which is a Box2D rebuild in both builds for a ceiling of a few percent of one stress scene's physics. In JS, only the `Atomics.load(HDR_READ)` per command is redundant (physics is the single consumer); the read index must still be published per command, since producers drop a command when they see the ring full. That is about 2 % of SpawnStorm physics, left as a note. The same trace's other lead, `syncBodySlot`'s warning, was a bug and is fixed (R-0615).

records.title: WASM Phase 6, all JS against all WASM on four multi-kernel scenes, E-76
records.text:
**passed: the kernels live together and their gains add up.** Phase 6, shortened at the owner's request (2026-10-24: "make it shorter"): all JS against all WASM, one build (`--vs HEAD`, side A `wasmOff=` every switch including `box2dBlock`, `pixiPack` and `gpuPackSplit`), Chrome, headed, source, detailed stats off, 4 pairs per scene, on four scenes where several kernels run at once. Leave-one-out was skipped: every winner has its own solo pair on record, and the all-JS pair shows no worker giving its gain back.

| Scene | Worker | All JS → all WASM | Paired | Worse |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Predator | pre-render | 5.397 → 3.715 ms | −31.0 % | 0/4 |
| | spatial | 6.041 → 4.935 ms | −17.8 % | 0/4 |

records.title: The sway whole in decorationSway.wasm (sway_free, sway_trig), close-out group B, E-76
records.text: **kept (coverage, close-out group B), a tie.** `12f47683`: decorationSway.wasm runs the whole sway. `sway_free` and `sway_free_u32` take updateDecorationSway's unbucketed loop, the engine's default (`particle.swayFrequencyBuckets` 0), which stayed JS. `sway_trig` finishes the bucketed kernel's trig list (impulses, angles of 0.08 rad or more), which `_finishSwayTrig` did in JS; that method is gone. Every sine and cosine is fdlibm's (`weed_sincos`), and an argument past its medium reduction (about 1.6e6 rad) is reduced modulo 2π. The sway regions are laid out without a grid too. Parity on the worker's own path (`decorationSwayWasm.test.js`): the trig list's 8 635 rotations over 60 frames and sway_free's 57 frames match the JS within 1e-6 of the base rotation's size, every other byte exact; only 32 of sway_free's rotations differ from the JS at all. A decoration outside fdlibm's domain is left out of the comparison. The bucketed exports are unchanged and still bit for bit. Pair, `decorationSwayStressScene?buckets=0&decorations=300000` (the `?buckets=` knob, `dee52a69`), Chrome, headed, source, worktrees, 4 pairs: particle **2.532 → 2.594 ms**, under the floor, a tie. At 40 000 decorations, 0.948 → 0.853 ms, also under the floor. A CPU trace of the 300 000 run: `sway_free_u32` 29.5 % of the particle worker, `updateDecorationScreenVisibility` 38.9 %, `resolveAttachedDecorations` 14.8 %, `copyActiveSnapshot` 12.3 %. The C sine costs what V8's Math.sin costs; what this buys is the JS path that can leave src/. The three JS loops over every decoration are the worker's cost at this scale, a lead.

records.title: The bullet tick at 32-bit ids and past 65 535 bullets, and the owner column's width, close-out group B, E-76
records.text:
**kept (coverage, close-out group B), with a bug fixed on the way.**

**The bug (`dfffe49b`):** `BulletComponent.ownerId` stayed a `Uint16Array` at 32-bit entity ids, so a shooter past index 65 535 was cut. The cast excludes the owner by index, so its own bullets could hit it, and impacts named another owner. It now takes `EntityIdArray()` in `getBufferSize` and `initializeArrays`, as `DecorationComponent.parentEntityIndex` does; `bulletOwnerWidth.test.js` checks that owner 70 000 is kept at 32-bit ids.

**The coverage (`25f118f1`):** the kernel read 16-bit grid ids and owners and wrote a 16-bit active list, so 32-bit ids or a pool past 65 535 bullets ran the JS tick. Two constant flags (`wideIds`, `wideSlots`) give `bullet_tick_lean` three more exports: `_ids32`, `_slots32` and `_u32`. The client binds the one the scene's widths need, the active list is laid at the pool's slot width, the 65 535-bullet gate in the scene spec is gone, and `BulletPool.tick` hands the kernel a list of its width.
- Parity, `bulletTickWasm.test.js`: the three forms leave what `BulletPool.tick` leaves, bit for bit, at 70 000 entities (with hits on entities past 65 535) and 70 000 bullets.
- The 16-bit variants: `bullet_tick` and `bullet_tick_hoist` compile byte for byte as before; the two stampless ones have one local read moved (13 bytes).
- Kernel A/B, `bulletTickWasmMicrobench --variant wasm_lean` against the parent, 5 alternating rounds: storm 385.5 → 369.9 ops/s median (paired −8.6, +1.8, +3.4, −0.3, −5.1 %), sparse 2 719 → 2 868 ops/s: a tie. A first sitting, before the owner reads went back where the 16-bit tick had them, read storm −9.2 %.

records.title: The engine block without physics (the bullet tick and the visibility gather in WASM there), and spawns of RigidBody types without physics, close-out group B, E-76
records.text:
**kept (product), close-out group B, with an engine bug fixed on the way.**

**The block (`d0b0528e`):** Phase 4's engine block (the render-queue regions, then the spatial ones) existed only in Box2D's memory. A scene without physics kept its render-queue and spatial memories apart, and the kernels that read both in one memory ran in JS: the bullet tick and the visibility gather. `standaloneBlock` lays the same two parts in a shared memory of its own after a null guard, `reserveBox2dBlock` takes it when there is no physics worker, and the spec lays the bullet and gather regions in it. In a block the collect now takes its own variant when it has no body variant; it took none before, which would have dropped the collect. `standaloneEngineBlock.test.js`: without physics the render-queue and spatial memories are the block's, with the bullet tick's regions, Transform and Collider in the first part and the grid in the second.

**The bug (`d054b48e`):** a scene with physics off could not spawn a type with a RigidBody. The spawn reset wrote `vx`, `vy`, `angularVelocity` and `sleeping`, which only Box2D's heap binds, and logic threw "Cannot set properties of undefined" on the first spawn; that happened before this work too. `spawnNoPhysics.test.js` fails on the old reset. Measuring it took `bulletStressScene ?physics=0` (`eaf323ea`; collider-only props tried in `22090890` kept their RigidBody, since components are inherited, and were dropped again in `dd0f2459`).

**The pair:** one build, side A `wasmOff=box2dBlock` (no block: separate memories and the JS tick, as before the change), 40 000 bullets, Chrome, headed, source, 4 pairs: particle **5.089 → 3.285 ms, −35.7 %, worse 0/4**, cv 4/1 %; pre-render −0.5 %; `VISIBLE_ENTITIES` and `ENTITIES_PROCESSED` equal; no page errors. A 4 s smoke had read the JS side at 31 ms while it warmed up.

records.title: gpuPack's slow path in the kernel (type filter, screen space, pixel snap), close-out group B, E-76
WASM close-out L7: Playwright's Firefox runs WASM 5-18x slow; in release Firefox 158 all WASM wins pre-render -36 % and spatial -10 % on Predator
records.text:
**Playwright's Firefox is not Firefox for WASM: its build ran the kernels 5–18× slower than release Firefox.** Close-out L7 (Firefox), 2026-10-24.

First pair, Playwright's Firefox 153 (`runPredatorAbab --browser firefox` as it was then, `--vs HEAD`, side A `wasmOff=` every switch, 4 pairs, headed, source): all WASM lost everywhere. Spatial 8.596 → 22.984 ms (+155 %, 4/4 worse), pre-render 9.504 → 19.449 (+106 %, 4/4), physics 20.078 → 24.866 (+21 %, 3/4), Pixi 7.023 → 8.151 (+8 %); casters and shadow lights −29 % on the WASM side (load keys off, so the pair failed on load as well). In Chrome the same pair is a gain on every worker (R-0618).

The cause is the browser build, not the engine or the automation. A two-loop probe (a hash-and-store loop and a float loop over shared WASM memory, the same loops in JS over views on that memory and on a plain SharedArrayBuffer, in a worker, best of 5 after 2.5 s of warm-up; ns per element):

| | Playwright FF 153 under Playwright | the same binary started by hand | release Firefox 158 | Chrome 155 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| WASM, integer loop | 5.78 | 5.42 / 5.46 headless | 1.08 / 1.09 headless | 1.07 |
| WASM, float loop | 20.71 | 20.32 / 21.25 headless | 1.31 / 1.18 headless | 1.32 |
| JS, integer loop (WASM memory / SAB) | 1.13 / 1.07 | 1.07 / 1.14 | 1.12 / 1.22 | 1.34 / 1.33 |
| JS, float loop (WASM memory / SAB) | 2.26 / 2.29 | 2.28 / 2.38 | 2.27 / 2.37 | 2.21 / 2.27 |

Juggler does attach a `Debugger` to every page and worker global (its Runtime.js and WorkerMain.js), but the build is as slow without it. JS views on WASM memory cost the same as views on a plain SharedArrayBuffer in both browsers.

Tooling (5714f54e): `--browser firefox` now starts the installed Firefox without Playwright (`tests/bench/stockFirefox.mjs`): a kept profile (a new one held the first page about 50 s), Playwright's quieting prefs, and the bench page loads `stockDriver.js`, which takes the runner's `page.evaluate` calls over HTTP. Playwright's build stays as `--browser playwright-firefox`, for boots and console lines only. Smoke, Predator all WASM in Firefox 158 (8 s warm-up, 5 s): spatial 7.0, physics 8.6, Pixi 6.1, pre-render 5.4, logic 6.8 ms, 60 fps on every worker, no page errors.

**The pair in release Firefox 158** (`runPredatorAbab --browser firefox --vs HEAD`, side A `wasmOff=` every switch, 4 pairs, headed, source, detailed stats off; load keys equal: casters +1.2 %, visible entities +0.7 %, 20 000 decorations):

| Worker | All JS → all WASM | Paired | Worse |
|---|---|---|---|
| pre-render | 8.413 → 5.206 ms | −36.2 % | 0/4 |
| spatial | 7.879 → 6.878 ms | −10.3 % | 1/4 |
| Pixi | 6.317 → 6.384 ms | −0.5 % | 2/4 |
| physics | 6.990 → 8.381 ms | +26.0 % | 3/4 (cv 12/18 %) |
| logic (no WASM) | 6.275 → 6.573 ms | +10.8 % | 4/4 (cv 10/9 %) |
| particle | 1.438 → 1.276 ms | under the floor | |

Physics is load: Predator's moved bodies were 7 312–8 260 on the WASM side in three pairs against 3 333–4 530 on the JS side. A line fitted to the four JS runs (STEP_MS against BODY_MOVED_COUNT, 0.475 µs a moved body) predicts the WASM runs at +4.5 %, −7.0 %, +2.6 % and one at +28.6 %: no regression shown. Logic runs no kernel but reads its columns in the engine block (`box2dBlock`); its +10.8 % is not decided (no Firefox A/A yet), and is the one lead from this sitting: `box2dBlock` alone in Firefox. No page errors in the 8 runs.

**L7, Firefox: passed for Predator** (the boot sweep of every scene follows). WebKit is out (the owner, 2026-10-24: Safari does not matter).

records.title: WASM close-out L7: all 61 scenes boot in release Firefox 158 with every kernel on
records.text:
**Every scene boots in release Firefox 158 with every kernel on.** Close-out L7, 2026-10-24: `profileSceneSweep.mjs --pass boot --browser firefox --set all` (61 scenes: the demos and the stress scenes, source, headed, a few seconds each; a run fails on a nonzero exit, a page error or "Fatal engine error").

61 of 61 ok. The first sweep stopped after four scenes: the bench's forced ends counted as crashes, and after three Firefox opened on a "Troubleshoot Mode?" prompt that held the profile (fixed in ed636c8a: a graceful close, the prompt off, a held profile refused at once). `sceneryCamStressScene` failed in Chrome too: it registered 12 custom layers over 4 built-in ones, and there are 5 built-in layers now (fixed in the scene: 11).
