records.title: WASM close-out step 2: eight kernels run only in WebAssembly, their JS is tests/reference; 61/61 scenes boot in Chrome and Firefox
records.text:
**Close-out step 2, group A: eight kernels run only in WebAssembly; their JavaScript is `tests/reference/`.** 2026-10-24/25, the owner's order ("delete covered JS now, then 7 and 6b").

One kernel per commit, each with the node suite green and its scenes booted in Chrome:

| Kernel | Commit | The JS, now | A case that ran the JS, now |
|---|---|---|---|
| decalStamp | 140f2729 | `Decal.stampToTileBuffers` → `tests/reference/decalStamp.mjs` | decal memory past its cap or refused: an error naming its size; a texture the memory lacks (malformed only): skipped, warned once |
| decalPremultiply | f8d4fd2f | `copyPremultiplyRgba` → `tests/reference/decalPremultiply.mjs` | (the decal memory is always made with decals) |
| navFlowfield | 42050b17 | the worker's flowfield search, bucket queue and its scratch arrays → `tests/reference/navFlowfield.mjs` | navigation memory past its cap: an error; NavScratch keeps what A* uses (its reset no longer refills five bucket arrays) |
| meshCorners | fbe56bcb | `rewriteExplicitMeshCorners` → `tests/reference/meshCorners.mjs` | a call the kernel cannot take, a MESH layer without its regions: errors; a MESH layer without MeshGeometry keeps arrays of its own (nothing to rewrite; a test holds it) |
| shadowStamp | da221e1f | `stampLightRange` and its machinery → `tests/reference/shadowStamp.mjs` | a call past the regions' caps: an error naming the count (unreachable: the caps come from the config that sizes the regions) |
| particleIntegrate, particleLists | a69bcfd3 | `src/util/particleIntegrate.js` → `tests/reference/particleIntegrate.mjs` (`particleWorkerJs.mjs` puts it on a worker) | particle memory past its cap or past MAX_POOL_SLOTS: an error. The F32 switches stay (they choose kernel forms) |
| spatialGather, spatialPublish | 1a0fa8db | `findNeighborsForOwnedEntities`, `_getNeighborCells`, the JS filter → `tests/reference/spatialGather.mjs` (`spatialJsClass`) | publish memory past its cap: an error that says to lower `spatial.maxNeighbors` |

Around them: a `wasm` key that is not a switch is warned once (b24b0362); a kernel that does not compile or link names itself (fe52d0ea); the engine catalog's rows time the kernels, not the references (40b26070, ddb2078e, ffb95c8d, 849866c3), and its test now checks each row's module exists (86addcc0); a dynamic import the stamp commit missed (8a9ae279).

Found by booting, not by the tests: the destructible-terrain scenes have a MESH layer without MeshGeometry (`renderer.maxMeshVerts` 0), which the first mesh-corner commit refused (fixed before it was committed, with a test); a turned-camera cull test ran on plain arrays (now on the reference list build). An import checker over src/, tests/ and demos/ (every named import exported where it points) found no other stale reference.

Parity, where the switch-off runs were the reference: every kernel test now compares against `tests/reference/`; the bench checksums of the js and wasm variants are equal (decal stamp 1246923899, flowfield 2328129863, mesh corners 3295885469, shadow stamp 2692520044); the spatial kernels equal the reference search with the kernel publish, and with the JS filter when detailed stats count both (E-02).

Hygiene, no speed claim: the shipped paths are the kernels', unchanged. Left with group B: gpuPack's entity batch and the painter sort's main queue (their JS still serves Pixi's pack-mode and interpolation batches and the custom layers' y-sort).

**Every scene boots after them: 61 of 61 in Chrome and 61 of 61 in release Firefox 158** (`profileSceneSweep.mjs --pass boot`, source, headed, a few seconds each; a run fails on a nonzero exit, a page error or "Fatal engine error").

records.title: W9e: a pose batch packs through gpuPack.wasm (pack_pose); bunnyMark Pixi -2.0 %, a tie, kept as coverage
records.text:
**W9e: a pose batch (renderer.interpolation) packs through gpuPack.wasm.** Close-out item 6b, its hot part. 2026-10-25.

Why this part of 6b first: a CPU profile of the scenes that run Pixi's own packers (pose interpolation or `packGpuSprites: 'pixi'`), 2026-10-25, found one hot JS packer: bunnyMarkScene's Pixi spent 71 % of its 192 ms/s busy time in `_packPoseOnly` (250 000 sprites, interpolation on). Pixi's glow, shadow, caster and custom-layer batches did not show; adobeAnimate's Pixi time is `commitSplit` (68 % of 376 ms/s), a copy of pre-render's two streams whose statics generation moves every frame (an animated scene), not JS arithmetic: a lead of its own.

The change: `pack_pose` in gpuPack.c (b0fa91de), the pose x, y, rotC, rotS and the previous x, y, and the 11 statics unless current, through pack_general's screen transform, pixel snap and type filter, with the JS's depth `1 - (out + 1) / depthDenom`; bit-identical to the batch's packers on 15 paths (both streams and the pose alone, full and short capacity). Wired in 418f50b9 (measured as 7f38f3fe, the same tree before its message took the numbers): with interpolation Pixi's pack region is 17 floats a row (pose then statics) and the pose batch packs there, then copies into its own arrays (E-123).

Kernel (`poseInterpPackMicrobench`, Node, 250 000 sprites, world space, pixel snap, the previous pose; 5 alternating rounds, the wasm side includes the copy): pose alone 90.9 → 405.6 ops/s (+346 %), both streams 68.5 → 169.1 ops/s (+147 %). One CPU profile of bunnyMark after: Pixi busy 161 ms/s, `pack_pose` 70 and the copy 45 where `_packPoseOnly` took 137.

**Scene: a tie.** bunnyMarkScene, Pixi owner, `--vs 0192f7c8 --hyp-rev 7f38f3fe`, 4 pairs, Chrome, headed, source, detailed stats off: Pixi **4.178 → 4.136 ms, −2.0 %, worse 1/4** (cv 2/1 %), pre-render 4.815 → 4.777 ms (−1.4 %, 1/4), logic and the rest under the 3 ms floor; load keys equal (250 000 visible). NEUTRAL by the speed rule; kept as coverage (decision 7: the JS pose packers can leave src/ once no batch needs them), as gpuPack's slow path was (R-0622).

Why the profile's −16 % did not hold: in Chrome the JS pose pack is about 2.3 ms a frame (the Node bench's 11 ms overstated it about five times), and the wired path adds the copy out of the shared region into the batch's own arrays (E-123), about 0.75 ms for 250 000 × 6 floats, which takes back most of what the kernel saves. Lead: in a scene whose other workers are idle (bunnyMark), uploading from the shared region (E-123's cost was other workers' time in Predator) or copying only what moved.

records.title: W4d: the bullet and trail rows in the emit kernel; bulletStressScene pre-render -14.1 %
records.text:
**W4d: pre-render's bullet and trail rows (types 4 and 5) in the emit kernel.** Close-out item 7 (group B, the emit's foreign rows), its largest part. 2026-10-25.

Why: the item-7 profile of bulletStressScene (2026-10-25) had pre-render at 203 ms/s, with `_emitForeignRows` 24.9 %, `clearQueueShadow` 5.7 % and `_resolveAnimFrameStart` 2.5 %: the bullet rows emit_rows listed for the JS.

The change: emit_rows writes emitSpriteQueue's bullet and trail branches when BulletComponent's columns are in the render-queue memory (df0c092f), which they are wherever the bullet tick runs (its block, W19); wired in pre-render in 33f8484a. The trail is computed in double as the JS computes it, hidden rows keep the columns the JS leaves, and a bullet without a first frame comes back as warning kind 3, which the JS replays. Where BulletComponent is elsewhere the rows stay listed for the JS. Parity: preRenderEmitWasm.test.js puts BulletComponent in the memory and holds the rows to the JS emit's bit for bit over 30 frames, with every slot class reached (inactive, zero and short trails, a −0 difference, no texture); a mutant (trail alpha × 0.8) fails it.

Kernel (`preRenderEmitBulletMicrobench`, 7c2e0b09, Node, bulletStressScene's frame of 32 700 bullets and 195 sprites, 5 alternating rounds, TurboFan, checksums equal): bullets 872.9 → 2092.5 ops/s (+139.7 %), with trails 744.2 → 1408.4 ops/s (+89.3 %).

Scene: at its default 40 000 bullets, bulletStressScene's pre-render is 2.97 ms, under the 3 ms floor: 2.972 → 2.507 ms (−15.6 %, better in 4/4), not judged. With the scene's new load knob (`?bullets=64000`, 671eda34), `--vs 7c2e0b09 --hyp-rev 33f8484a` (run as 411dc4ca, the same tree before its message was reworded), 4 pairs, Chrome, headed, source, detailed stats off: **pre-render 4.185 → 3.612 ms, −14.1 %, worse 0/4** (cv 1/2 %); particle 4.799 → 4.776 ms (−0.5 %, 1/4); the other workers under the floor; RENDER_QUEUE_SIZE 52 437 on both sides; presented 60 on both. **KEPT (product).**

Left in item 7: the bullet collect (E-137), the glow rows (type 3), the particle rows (type 1: ParticleComponent is not in the memory) and the frames with a LiquidFun row (declined).

records.title: E-137: the bullet collect writes its own rows; bulletStressScene pre-render -17.3 % after W4d
records.text:
**E-137: the bullet collect writes its own rows for bullets on the main collector.** Close-out item 7's other half in bulletStressScene (a JS change: E-98c and E-98e's pattern, for bullets). 2026-10-25.

Why: the same profile had `_writeRenderable` 13.5 %, `collectVisibleBullets` 9.5 % and `collectRenderable` 8.1 % of pre-render's 203 ms/s: collectRenderable's type dispatch, `Layer.entitiesMask()` and bit scan, then `_writeRenderable` re-reading the collector's columns from `this`, for each of 32 700 bullets a frame, which all end on the main collector.

The change: collectVisibleBullets writes the main collector's rows itself (y, type, index; the trail's after it at key − 1), the count in a local synced around the generic path, and leaves the last key in COLLECT_Y where the old loop left it (the sprite collect reads it). bulletCollectShortcut.test.js holds the collectors (main and a custom layer), the full-collector calls and that key to the old loop's, room for all and a full collector.

First version (59aceb37): the shortcut took mask 0 only, as E-98c does for sprites. But BulletPool.spawn gives every bullet `Layer.resolveSubscriptions(config)`, which is the entities layer's bit without a layer, so no default bullet took it: bulletStressScene?bullets=64000, `--vs 671eda34 --hyp-rev 59aceb37`, 4 pairs: pre-render 3.605 → 3.665 ms (+1.1 %, worse 2/4), a tie, as it had to be. Second version (ece24bf1): that bit alone routes to the main collector once, as 0 does, so it takes the shortcut too; the test's reference forces the generic path with the entities bit and bit 15 (no sprite-queue layer), and three mutants fail it (the trail's key, the COLLECT_Y write, the first version's condition).

Scene: `bulletStressScene?bullets=64000`, `--vs 671eda34 --hyp-rev ece24bf1`, 4 pairs, Chrome, headed, source, detailed stats off (the pairs ran as 70b485da, ad329ac0 and cbbbd59a, the same trees before the messages were reworded): **pre-render 3.623 → 3.016 ms, −17.3 %, worse 0/4** (cv 1/5 %); particle 4.874 → 4.847 ms (−0.8 %, 1/4); RENDER_QUEUE_SIZE 52 442 and 52 425; presented 60.0 and 59.9 (−0.3 %). The renderer went 1.429 → 1.625 ms, under the floor and not judged; the queue it reads is the same bit for bit, so it is noted, not explained. **KEPT (product).** With W4d before it (not measured as a total): bulletStress pre-render about 4.19 → 3.02 ms at 64 000 bullets.

Lesson: a shortcut on "no mask" has to check the mask the spawn path writes by default.

records.title: E-138: the collector sorted before the emit when it expands its rows; adobeAnimateScene (min zoom) pre-render -19.7 %
records.text:
**E-138: a frame whose emit expands its rows sorts the collector before the emit.** 2026-10-25.

Why: in adobeAnimateScene at the minimum zoom (20 000 characters, 261 744 queue rows), pre-render is saturated (818 ms/s) and spends 33.8 % in `pack_sprites_split_scatter`, 12.9 % in `painter_order_simd` and 2.5 % in `fillQueueIndices`. The painter sorts the queue's runs (E-103), and the pack then writes each row to its painter slot: a random write per root's run. A kernel screen of the shipped pack on that shape (Node, 261 744 rows): runs of 13 in random order 5.31 ms, the queue already in order 2.41 ms (the gather is worse, 7.07 ms).

The change (355ee06e, its gate fixed in 95e03c4c): when last frame's emit wrote at least twice the rows it was given, buildRenderQueue stably sorts the collector and its pose stash by the keys the emit will write (the painter's radix), so the queue comes out in painter order; _packGpuSprites packs it as it is, with no painter and no slot list, and sets GPU_FLAG_SORTED. Only with pre-render's painter, no sun casters (packed in queue order) and a queue that did not fill. Equal keys keep the collector's order, as the painter's full sort does (its reinsert of moved keys, which these frames skip, puts them after the unmoved ones). Tests: the queue emitted from the sorted collector is the emitted queue sorted by key, every column, frame after frame (two mutants fail it); the presorted queue packs to the rows the painter packs; real frames (resetFrameCounters, the collector, buildRenderQueue) sort from the second on.

First pair, a tie that measured nothing: the gate read _emitWriteCount, which resetFrameCounters clears at the start of every frame, so the presort never ran (adobeAnimateScene at the minimum zoom, `--vs a3300db3 --hyp-rev 355ee06e`, 4 pairs: pre-render 20.638 → 20.286 ms, −1.5 %, the painter and the scatter still in the profile). An earlier pair at the default zoom was under the floor (936 characters, 12 251 rows).

**Scene, with the gate fixed:** adobeAnimateScene, `--camera-zoom min`, `--vs a3300db3 --hyp-rev 95e03c4c`, 4 pairs, Chrome, headed, source, detailed stats off: **pre-render 20.516 → 15.818 ms, −19.7 %, worse 0/4** (cv 6/5 %), −21.5 % against the other workers; RENDER_QUEUE_SIZE 261 792 and 261 789; VISIBLE_ENTITIES 20 000 both. The tool called it REGRESSION for the renderer: 6.432 → 7.658 ms per step (+18.4 %, 4/4). The change does not reach Pixi (the GPU rows are the same), and its busy time per second did not move: CPU profiles of the scene before and after, 366 and 359 ms/s, pre-render 818 and 681 ms/s. Pre-render was saturated and delivered fewer frames (its FPS in the pairs 54.8 against 57.8), so more of Pixi's steps now commit a new frame (`commitSplit` +19 % per second) and fewer are empty: the consumer of a faster producer, read against its load as the rules ask. **KEPT (product).**

Lesson: a gate that reads per-frame state must be tested across real frames; every unit test passed with the presort never running in a scene.

records.title: W27b: the Adobe expansion in float32 and SIMD, kernel +55 %, a tie in adobeAnimateScene; reverted
records.text:
**W27b: the Adobe expansion in float32, four pieces at a time. Kernel +55 %, a tie in the scene; reverted.** 2026-10-25.

Why: after E-138, adobeAnimateScene at the minimum zoom spent 40.3 % of pre-render (681 ms/s) in `emit_rows`, nearly all of it expanding 20 000 characters into 261 788 pieces in double, piece by piece, as the JS does. The owner's rules allow float32 within a stated tolerance, and every kernel gets the SIMD/float32 pass.

The change (70e9490c, 7f5a961b, 49b40890): `adobe_root_f32x4`, the root's transform in double then rounded once, four pieces to an f32x4 with vector stores into each queue column, the rest with the same float32 arithmetic; behind EMIT_ADOBE_F32, on by default through wasm.preRenderEmitAdobeF32. preRenderEmitAdobe.test.js held it to the double expansion within 2e-3 px (positions), 1e-5 (scales, rotations) and 1e-6 (alpha), every other column exact, with Y-sort and without and a queue that fills inside a character (two mutants failed it).

Kernel (`preRenderEmitAdobeMicrobench`, Node, 10 000 characters of the demo's asset, 130 888 rows, 5 alternating rounds, TurboFan; the f32x4 variant's checksum frames in lock-step with the double emit, all 45 within the tolerance): emit 443.3 → 687.1 ops/s (+55.0 %).

Scene: adobeAnimateScene, `--camera-zoom min`, `--vs 7f5a961b --hyp-rev 49b40890`, 4 pairs, Chrome, headed, source: pre-render 14.608 → 15.625 ms (+2.1 %, worse 2/4, cv 8/5 %), −0.4 % against the other workers, which all moved up together (physics +7.5 %, renderer +6.3 %, spatial +3.1 %): no gain. A CPU profile of the scene with the switch on against the one before it (E-138 on): `emit_rows` 274 → 262 ms/s (40.3 % → 38.7 % of 681 → 676 ms/s). In the scene the expansion is bound by its stores (261 788 rows into 16 columns, while Pixi reads the other buffer), not by the arithmetic the bench's hot, half-size working set measured. Chrome decides: a tie, and a tolerance path that buys nothing is not kept. Reverted (65ccbc11, 950865f8, 91edeae2); the code is in 70e9490c if a scene where the expansion is compute-bound turns up.

Seen on the way: on E-138's presorted frames with lighting off, the main queue still takes the glow split (fillQueueIndices builds a list of every row, 3.5 % of pre-render) and packs through the scatter with that identity list (2.76 ms on the screen's shape) instead of with no list (2.41 ms). A follow-up.

records.title: E-138 follow-up: no slot list on presorted frames with no glow rows; adobeAnimateScene (min zoom) pre-render -10.6 %
records.text:
**E-138, follow-up: a presorted queue with no glow rows packs every row with no slot list; the unsplit pack names its glow type.** 2026-10-25.

Seen in W27b's profile (R-0630): on E-138's presorted frames with glows not drawn as sprites, the main queue still took the glow split. fillQueueIndices listed every row (3.5 % of adobeAnimateScene's pre-render at the minimum zoom) and the pack ran the scatter over that identity list, 2.76 ms against 2.41 ms with no list on its 261 744 rows (the kernel screen of E-138).

The change (8d67f225): the collector sort counts the glow rows; a presorted frame with none packs unsplit, every row in queue order with no list. The unsplit path read `spec.glowIncludeType` undefined, which `| 0` makes 0, so an unsplit frame (lighting.lightGlow 'sprite', or no slot lists) packed its sprite rows into the glow batch; pre-render now sets it as Pixi's layer does (3 when glows are not sprites, else −1). painterRadixWired.test.js packs makeFrames' frames without glow rows both ways: the same rows as the painter's, no glow rows, no slot list, sorted; two mutants fail it (the split kept, the glow type as before).

Scene: adobeAnimateScene, `--camera-zoom min`, `--vs fdaf6bb5 --hyp-rev 81619669` (the same tree as 8d67f225, whose message was amended with these numbers), 4 pairs, Chrome, headed, source: **pre-render 16.479 → 14.819 ms, −10.6 %, worse 0/4** (cv 3/3 %), −6.7 % against the other workers (which moved down 3.7 to 6.0 % together); RENDER_QUEUE_SIZE 261 790 and 261 786; presented 60 on both. **KEPT (product).**

records.title: WASM close-out L3: commit holds across 20 Predator loads (+77 MB); destroy leaves ~720 MB (N-75)
records.text:
**WASM close-out L3: the commit charge across 20 scene loads holds; after the engine is destroyed about 720 MB stay (N-75).** 2026-10-25.

L3 asks that loading and unloading a scene 20 times leave the commit where it started (on Windows every shared memory is committed whole when made). `sceneCycleSmoke.mjs --commit` (aadec9d1, 48205a08) loads a scene, runs it 2.5 s and collects, 20 times in one page, and sums the commit of the node process and the headless Chrome under it before the first scene, after each load and after `game.destroy()`.

Predator, 20 loads: 253 MB before, **1 639 MB after the first load, 1 717 MB after the twentieth** (+77 MB, about 4 MB a load, under the 128 MB the smoke allows): each scene's memories (Box2D's with the engine block, the particle, decal, navigation and spatial ones) go when the next scene replaces them. **After destroy: 1 105 MB**, about 850 MB over the start (974 MB in a one-load probe). The exported classes' static views still hold Box2D's memory (410 MB: `Transform.x` and `GameObject.neighborData` view it since Phase 4); letting those go by hand frees 154 MB, so the rest is held where the public classes do not show. A game switching scenes is fine; a page that unloads the engine is not. Recorded as N-75 in REVIEW_PLAN.md, with the smoke's `--commit` check as its test.

records.title: WASM close-out step 4 screened: engine.wasm saves 1.3 KB and <1 ms of compile per worker; not done
records.text:
**WASM close-out step 4 screened: one engine.wasm saves 1.3 KB and under a millisecond of compile per worker; not worth the posted-Module change it needs.** 2026-10-25.

The plan's step 4 links every kernel into one engine.wasm. A trial build (buildWasm.mjs with a module of several sources, the 18 product kernels linked by wasm-ld, the kernel rules passing; not committed): **231 270 B, 58 735 B gzipped**, against the 18 modules' 232 563 B and 61 055 B gzipped. The helpers repeated in several sources (js_fmod, js_toint32 and the like) are small, so a shared header would save little more. Compile time (Node, WebAssembly.compile, medians of 20): all 18 modules 1.71 ms, engine.wasm 0.48 ms; per worker, its own kernels take 0.14 ms (spatial), 0.62 ms (particle), 0.81 ms (pre-render) and 0.32 ms (Pixi). And one module embedded in each of the four workers that use kernels would add about 230 KB to the bundle (each worker carries 78 KB of base64 instead of its own kernels), unless the main thread compiles it once and posts the WebAssembly.Module, a change to every worker's init and to the --src path. The merge buys tidiness, not speed or size; it is not done. W7 (the whole spatial step in one call) does not need it: gather, publish and rebuild can share a module of their own if W6's +10.9 % ever justifies it.

records.title: W30: Pixi's copies by memory.copy into a private memory; adobeAnimateScene (min zoom) Pixi -17.8 %
records.text:
**W30: Pixi's copies out of the render-queue memory by WebAssembly memory.copy into a private memory.** 2026-10-25.

Why: E-123 has every batch upload from arrays of its own (uploading from the shared rows made the other workers slower), so every frame Pixi copies the rows pre-render or its own pack wrote. In adobeAnimateScene at the minimum zoom `commitSplit` was 65 % of Pixi's 359 ms/s (the copy of 261 788 rows, 15.7 MB a frame); in bulletStressScene 28 %; in Predator `_commitPackedBatch` 10 %. TypedArray.set from a view of a shared memory copies word by word (V8's relaxed memcpy for shared buffers); WebAssembly's memory.copy between two memories (multi-memory: Chrome 120, Firefox 125) is the engine's memmove. A screen in Chrome 155 (chromeKernel.mjs, 15 MB): TypedArray.set from shared into a plain array 1.985 ms, memory.copy from the shared memory into an unshared one 1.25 ms (−37 %), memory.copy inside the shared memory 1.31 ms; Node 12.4 runs the same module.

The change (da139ae4): `src/render/sharedCopy.js` holds the copy module, assembled by hand (C has no syntax for a second memory; its WAT is in the comment), and `createPrivateArena`: an unshared WebAssembly.Memory made at its full size and never grown, so its buffer is an ordinary ArrayBuffer the upload reads as before, with a bump allocator. Pixi makes one for the entity batch (its two streams at their widest, 17 floats a row); `InstancedSpriteBatch.copyIn` takes every copy into the arena by memory.copy (commitSplit, the W9d and W9e uploads, `_commitPackedBatch`) and anything else by TypedArray.set. Without multi-memory (no arena) the batch keeps its arrays. sharedCopy.test.js: the copy bit for bit (NaN and -0 patterns), the arena's arrays aligned and its end refused, a batch in the arena committing the bytes a batch without one commits, by memory.copy; a length mutant fails it.

Scene: adobeAnimateScene, `--camera-zoom min`, `--vs 987db5f5 --hyp-rev cbf074f8` (the same tree as da139ae4, whose message was amended with these numbers), Chrome, headed, source, Pixi the owner. The first 4 pairs: renderer 7.780 → 6.594 ms (−15.2 %, 0/4), but spatial, which the change does not reach, +4.0 % (worse 4/4, cv 1/3 %; +2.4 % against the others). An A/A in the same sitting (cbf074f8 on both sides, 4 pairs) moved physics +2.6 % (3/4) and spatial +1.0 %, so the sitting grew by 4 pairs (`--append`). **8 pairs: renderer 7.939 → 6.545 ms, −17.8 %, worse 0/8** (cv 2/3 %), −15.6 % against the other workers (8/8); spatial 5.356 → 5.348 ms (+0.6 %, 5/8), physics −0.7 %, pre-render −0.9 %; RENDER_QUEUE_SIZE 261 778 on both sides; presented 60. **KEPT (product).**

Next: the other batches Pixi commits from the render-queue memory (the glow batch, the shadow casters' sun, stamp and cookie batches: `_commitPackedBatch`, 10 % of Predator's Pixi) into arenas of their own.

records.title: W30 extended to the glow, cookie and caster batches; Predator Pixi -8.1 % (-3.6 % against the others)
records.text:
**W30, extended: the glow, cookie and shadow-caster batches keep their arrays in private memories too.** 2026-10-25.

The change (629e812a): every batch Pixi fills from the render-queue memory gets an arena of its own sized for its capacity (`_batchArena`): the entities' glow batch, the cookie shadow batch and the GPU caster batch, which `_commitPackedBatch` fills every frame with pre-render's packed rows (10 % of Predator's Pixi in the Q7 profile). Custom layers pack their own rows and copy nothing out of the shared memory.

Scene: Predator, `--vs caa49166 --hyp-rev 90c02b30` (the same tree as 629e812a, whose message was amended with these numbers), 4 pairs, Chrome, headed, source, Pixi the owner: **renderer 3.684 → 3.440 ms, −8.1 %, worse 1/4** (cv 5/2 %). Every worker moved down in this sitting (logic −3.6 %, physics −4.6 %, pre-render −3.1 %), so the figure that stands is against the others: **−3.6 % (lower 3/4)**. GPU_CASTERS 13 411 and 13 329, VISIBLE_ENTITIES 13 497 and 13 413, presented 60. **KEPT (product)**: a smaller gain than the entity batch's, as Predator's casters are about 1.2 MB a frame against Adobe's 15.7 MB.

records.title: E-138, fewer stores: presorted frames leave the sort keys and shadow terms; Adobe pre-render -14.5 %, Pixi +5.5 % (a trade, kept)
records.text:
**E-138, fewer stores: a presorted frame's emit leaves the sort keys and the shadow terms. Pre-render −14.5 %, Pixi +5.5 %: kept, with the trade written down.** 2026-10-25.

Why: after E-138 and W30, adobeAnimateScene at the minimum zoom spends 47.6 % of pre-render (744 ms/s) in `emit_rows`, and W27b showed that cost is the stores, not the arithmetic (float32 SIMD ran +55 % in Node and tied in the scene). On a presorted frame no painter reads the queue's sort keys and no sun-caster pass reads its shadow terms (E-138 presorts only without sun casters), so those four columns, 16 of about 61 bytes a piece, have no reader.

The change (3fa72bbd): emit_rows given EMIT_PRESORTED treats the sort key and the three shadow columns as absent for every row, which every row writer already handles (no branch added to the piece loop); only the main queue's emit sets it (_emitPresorted: custom layers emit after it and sort by their keys); rows the JS writes keep writing them. preRenderEmitAdobe.test.js: the kernel's rows leave the four columns and every other column is the one written without the flag (a mutant fails it); E-138's frame test now reads the order from the sorted collector.

Scene: adobeAnimateScene, `--camera-zoom min`, `--vs 0d436b43 --hyp-rev 3fa72bbd`, 4 pairs, Chrome, headed, source: **pre-render 13.125 → 11.369 ms, −14.5 %, worse 0/4** (cv 2/2 %), −15.9 % against the other workers; **renderer 6.565 → 6.916 ms, +5.5 %, worse 4/4** (cv 1/0 %), +5.8 % against the others; RENDER_QUEUE_SIZE 261 780 both, presented 60. Pre-render was not saturated on either side (its FPS 59.4 to 60.5, the same frame counts), so it is not E-138's consumer effect: CPU profiles before and after put Pixi at 364 and 403 ms/s busy, its copy (W30) and its upload (`updateBuffer`) each a little slower for the same bytes, likely pre-render's pack now moving memory while Pixi copies. The gate calls it a REGRESSION (another worker ≥ 3 % worse). **Kept as a trade**: −1.76 ms on the worker that sets the scene's limit (pre-render, 11 to 13 of 16.7 ms) against +0.35 ms on Pixi (6.9 ms); the owner may prefer the gate's letter (revert 3fa72bbd).

records.title: E-138, fewer stores kept: pre-render bounds adobeAnimateScene at the minimum zoom (11.4 ms against Pixi 6.9)
records.text:
**E-138, fewer stores (3fa72bbd): kept, a decision on R-0636's trade.** 2026-10-25.

R-0636's pair (adobeAnimateScene, `--camera-zoom min`, 4 pairs) moved pre-render 13.125 → 11.369 ms (−14.5 %, 0/4) and the renderer 6.565 → 6.916 ms (+5.5 %, 4/4), which the gate counts as a regression (another worker 3 % or more worse). The owner left the call to the session, with the scene's bottleneck as the criterion. At that zoom the worker that bounds the frame is pre-render: STEP_MS − WAIT_MS 11.4 ms on side B (load 65–69 %), against physics 7.7 ms (46 %), the renderer 6.9 ms (41 %), spatial 5.4 ms and logic 2.5 ms. The change takes 1.76 ms off that worker and puts 0.35 ms on one that stays 4.5 ms below it, so the headroom of the frame grows by the pre-render gain. **Kept.** Revisit if a scene where Pixi bounds the frame takes the presorted path (Adobe pieces at twice the collector's rows), since there the trade would go the other way.

WASM close-out step 3, group B's second batch: gpuPack, painter, collect and sway JS out of src, wasm.bulletTick gone; Predator and adobeAnimateScene neutral
records.text:
**WASM close-out step 3, group B's second batch: the JS copies of gpuPack, the painter sort, the sprite collect and the decoration sway left `src/`, and `wasm.bulletTick` went. Kept as hygiene: Predator and adobeAnimateScene at the minimum zoom show no worker 3 % worse.** 2026-10-26.

The commits:

- **gpuPack** (74b4e896). Its JS moved to `tests/reference/gpuPackJs.mjs`, and `wasm.gpuPack`, `wasm.pixiPack` and `wasm.gpuPackSplit` went.
  - The boot sweep found two bugs, fixed in the same commit. First, Pixi's frames outside the queue handshake read a buffer pre-render may be writing; they now keep the last good frame (N-76). Second, an empty split frame was refused; it now draws nothing.
- **The painter** (cdc3676c, then af66b3db). Pixi's y-sorted custom layers sort in the kernel first; then the JS painter moved to `tests/reference/painterJs.mjs`, and `wasm.painterRadix` went.
  - A queue the kernel refuses is drawn in queue order, with one error.
  - Pre-render told to sort on a memory without its painter state says so at init.
- **The sprite collect** (5c972848). Its two JS loops moved to `tests/reference/preRenderCollectJs.mjs`, and `wasm.preRenderCollect` went.
  - The memory always carries the collect's blocks when the spec has them.
  - A frame the kernel cannot take collects nothing, with one error.
  - Y-sort before the texture tables collects through the kernel.
- **The decoration sway** (ec15e7d8). Its JS loops moved to `tests/reference/decorationSwayJs.mjs`, and `wasm.decorationSway` went.
  - Parented decorations still sway in JS (`resolveAttachedDecorations`), which the kernel does not cover.
- **`wasm.bulletTick`** (6915ca31). The kernel runs wherever its regions are laid out.
  - BulletPool.tick's JS loop stays where the kernel cannot read the grid: no spatial workers, or the spatial memory outside the engine block.
- **Two re-init bugs** were found by the new tests and fixed in the commits above. `_gpuPainter` and `_swayWasm` kept the last init's binding.
- The node suite passed at each commit (1982 to 1985 tests). Every mutant was killed, except one: the sway's in-frame cache reset, which cannot run since `_swayBuckets` changes only at init. The scenes each change reaches booted clean (61, then 5, 11 and 8).

**Gates** (`runPredatorAbab --vs 587c5f60 --hyp-rev 6915ca31 --owner preRender`, 4 pairs each; A is R-0638's measured B; worktrees, headed, detailed stats off, AB BA order):

- **Predator.** The runner says KEPT (product), read here as neutral:
  - pre-render 4.040 → 3.796 ms, −6.2 % (worse 1/4, cv 8/2 %), but −1.6 % against the other workers;
  - logic −6.3 % and spatial −2.5 %, which this batch does not reach: the machine drifted down;
  - renderer −1.6 %; physics +2.2 % (worse 3/4, cv 11/4 %), not reached by the batch and under the line; particle below its floor;
  - presented 60.0 fps on both sides; load keys within 0.2 %.
- **adobeAnimateScene at the minimum zoom**, where pre-render is the bottleneck: NEUTRAL.
  - pre-render 11.101 → 11.081 ms, −0.2 % (worse 2/4, cv 1/1 %);
  - renderer +0.6 %, spatial +0.5 % (worse 2/4), physics −0.6 %;
  - presented 59.9 → 60.0 fps; load keys equal.

Verdict: **kept (hygiene)**. No primary worker is 3 % worse on either scene. Spatial's +3.65 % on adobeAnimateScene in R-0638 (N-74) does not reappear against that batch: +0.5 %, cv 1 %.

records.text:
**WASM close-out sitting: all WASM (4a82a562) against the last commit before E-76 (5477a582). The scoreboard has no row worse; L10 on four physical cores keeps the gains (pre-render −39 % on Predator, −76 % on adobeAnimateScene at the minimum zoom); the boot is the same or better.** 2026-10-26.

This is the migration's measured total (HOW_WE_MEASURE: a total is measured, not added). The kernels' own records are the parts. Phase 6's leave-one-out is R-0618.

**Scoreboard** (R-0641, `runScoreboard --vs 5477a582 --skip-kernels --skip-lockstep --skip-node`; stress rows headless 2 × 8/10 s, gameplay rows headed 5 × 10/10 s).
- Kernel rows skipped: the base has no kernels, so its side would time the reference or fail.
- Lockstep skipped: the float32 kernels are tolerance gates by the owner's decision (speed over exactness), not bit gates.

| Verdict | Rows |
| --- | --- |
| kept | ray: logic 4.345 → 2.735 ms, −37.1 % |
| | rayVsBox2d: logic −36.9 % |
| | liquidfunQuery: physics −9.8 % |
| | visPoly: pre-render −49.2 % |

| worse | none |
| fail | Protocol ceilings: the catalog's rows whose scene cannot reach 3 ms in the hot code (decals, emit, integrate, nav, tilemapGid, contactDrain, queryPublish, preRender, compute, sceneryCam, meshFillPan, meshFillLook). |
| | Step floors: queryAabb (logic −16.5 %, under 3 ms), meshFillMoving (Pixi 0.79 → 0.84 ms, under 3 ms). |
| | Loads not comparable: spatial (NEIGHBORS_REUSED −11.9 %), decalBlit (Pixi 20.9 → 8.7 ms with 12.7 % more tiles uploaded), audioStorm. |

**L4** (R-0640): the first 2 s are not worse; every bottleneck worker is faster from the first frames.

**L10, four physical cores** (`runPredatorAbab --vs 5477a582 --hyp-rev 4a82a562`, 4 pairs, headed). The runner and its Chrome ran under `start /affinity 55`, and the bench's Chrome processes were seen at 0x55.
- **Predator.** NEUTRAL:
  - pre-render 4.865 → 2.874 ms, −39.0 % (worse 0/4);
  - spatial −18.1 %, renderer −7.7 %;
  - physics +12.3 % (3/4) and logic +10.8 % (2/4), cv 12–15 %, too noisy to judge (N-74, L5);
  - presented 60.0 → 59.9 fps.
- **adobeAnimateScene at the minimum zoom.** NEUTRAL:
  - pre-render 45.698 → 11.135 ms, −76.4 % (0/4);
  - spatial −7.6 %, physics −6.8 %;
  - presented 59.2 → 59.9 fps.
- Process CPU per presented frame was not read: the runner has no tool for it yet (HOW_WE_MEASURE tool 9).

**Correctness and boot.**
- The node suite passes (1986).
- Every scene boots on the source tree in Chrome (61/61, after the last JS left).
- Every scene boots in release Firefox 158.0.1 too (61/61, `--browser firefox`): with no JS left to fall back to, every kernel loads there.
- The bundles build, and their embed and browser smokes pass (all 8; each about 9 KB smaller with the JS gone).
- N-75 is fixed: destroy gives Box2D's memory back.

**Verdict: the migration holds as a whole.**
- No catalog row is worse.
- On sixteen logical processors (R-0640, steady) and on four cores, Predator's pre-render is 39–42 % faster, and with 10,000 animated characters 70–76 % faster.
- The grouping (step 4) follows the merge.

records.title: WASM close-out step 4: every kernel ships in one engine.wasm (same code per function; Predator, adobeAnimateScene, visPoly, bullets neutral; 61/61 boot in Chrome and Firefox)
records.text:
**WASM close-out step 4: every kernel ships in one engine.wasm (branch wasm_group, 3e035db7). The kernels' code is the same as their own builds', and the owner scenes are neutral against the kernels apart. Kept as structure.** 2026-10-26.

**Built.**
- `scripts/buildWasm.mjs` links the 18 shipped kernels' sources into `src/wasm/engine.wasm` (`wasm/modules.json`'s "engine": one wasm-ld link over the objects, then wasm-opt; 78 exports).
  - Size: 240 471 B, 60 246 B gzipped, against 241 765 B and 62 963 B for the modules apart.
  - The kernels' own builds are now test fixtures (`tests/fixtures/wasm/`), byte for byte the binaries they replaced.
- **Same code, function by function.** Of the 88 named functions in the kernels' own builds, 65 are byte for byte the same in engine.wasm. The other 23 have the same size and differ only in their calls' function indices, which change with the module. None is missing, and none differs in size.
- **Loading.** `src/wasm/engine.js` is the only module that names the binary.
  - Each worker compiles it once and instantiates it once per memory (`util/wasmKernel.js`). The clients of one memory share the instance, each taking its own exports. That is safe because a kernel has no globals and no data of its own.
  - The bundle carries one copy, in the workers' common chunk: the prod compressed bundle is 1664 KB, against 1671 KB with the modules apart and 1680 KB on main.
- **Not done, on purpose:**
  - The main thread's compile and post of the module. Each worker's one compile costs no frame (L4, R-0640), and the bundle already holds one copy.
  - One `.c` per worker with a shared header. wasm-ld links the sources, and wasm-opt already merges identical helpers. W7's calls across kernels are a speed hypothesis of their own.

**Gate** (`runPredatorAbab --vs 0c94caff --hyp-rev 3e035db7`: the kernels apart, then engine.wasm; 4 pairs each, worktrees, headed, detailed stats off, AB BA order). Every scene NEUTRAL:
- **Predator:**
  - pre-render 3.829 → 3.799 ms, −0.7 % (worse 2/4);
  - renderer −4.6 %, logic −1.9 %, spatial −0.8 %;
  - physics −10.8 % (1/4, cv 7/8 %): drift, since the change does not reach physics;
  - presented 60.0 fps on both sides.
- **adobeAnimateScene at the minimum zoom:** pre-render 11.088 → 11.160 ms, +0.6 % (cv 1/0 %); every other worker within ±1.2 %; presented 59.9 → 60.0 fps.
- **visPolyStressScene:** pre-render 2.858 → 2.822 ms (−1.3 %, under the 3 ms floor).
- **bulletStressScene:** particle 3.166 → 3.169 ms, +0.1 % (cv 1/1 %).

**Correctness.**
- Suite 1986/1986.
- `buildWasm --check` passes.
- The bundles build, and their embed and browser smokes pass (all 8).
- Boot: 61/61 scenes in Chrome. 61/61 in release Firefox 158.0.1.

**Verdict: kept (structure).** The migration's plan is complete. The branch is wasm_hyp plus this step.

records.title: CPU profile of every scene after the WASM migration, Wave 7's source: Box2D's solver threads at 1000 ms/s even with no bodies, half of Predator's logic is engine code, spatial the largest engine sum
records.text:
**CPU profile of every scene after the WASM migration (v0.13.0 plus comment fixes, 7922d724), the source of EXECUTION_PLAN's Wave 7.** 2026-10-26, 16:47 to 17:11.

**Protocol.** `node tests/bench/profileSceneSweep.mjs --pass cpu --set all`:
- 65 scenes, one at a time, headed, from source, detailed stats off;
- 6 s of warm-up, then an 8 s window;
- the sweep's list now also has Q1's scenes (visPoly, compoundVisPoly at `ringSegments=64`, particleIntegrate with tweens) and stationarySpatialWideScene (7922d724).

64 scenes were profiled. particleEmitStressScene failed on a 404 for `src/core/debug/spawnParamsCheck.js`, an import another session was writing into `gameObject.js` at that moment. CPU samples say where a worker spends its busy time, not `STEP_MS`.

**Not a quiet sitting.** A visual-editor session worked in the same folder.
- **Contended scenes.** It ran headless scene loads (ED-39, R-0644) at least from 16:53 to 16:56, so scenes 16 to 23 may read high.
- **Half-edited code.** From about 17:08 its uncommitted spawn checks were in `gameObject.js`, `scene.js` and `logicWorker.js`, so scenes 58 to 65 ran on that code.

Profile both groups again before deciding anything on them.

**Findings** (ms/s busy, and % of that worker):
- **Box2D's solver threads read 1000 ms/s in every scene with physics, even with no bodies.** In bunnyMarkStressScene, physics steps in 0.13 ms with `BODY_COUNT 0`, and the threads are 99.6 % in `wasm-function[108]`. Either the sampler counts a blocked semaphore wait as busy, or the threads spin; an OS thread-time check decides it (E-144).
  - On a physics-bound scene, each solver thread spends 9 % in `_emscripten_get_now` (ballsHeavyStressScene, 90 ms/s per thread). Predator spends 3 %.
- **Logic: about half of Predator's logic is engine code around the game's.**
  - Each of its two workers (345 and 330 ms/s): the component getter 14 and 10 %, `neighborCount` 8, `_tickIntervalBucket` 8, the FSM tick 7, `getNeighbor` 7 and 7, the collision dispatch 5 and 7.
  - Game code is 27 %.
  - adobeAnimateScene: 44 % of its logic (226 ms/s) is the component getter.
  - painterSortStressScene: logic is 89 % `_tickIntervalBucket`; painterMoveStressScene: 37 % `_tickNonDecimatedOne` (720 ms/s).
  - tilemapStressScene: logic is 82 % `getTileId` (576 ms/s).
  - tweenStressScene: tween tick 49 %, `_apply` 35 %.
  - waterAndBoxesScene: `_processBox2dCollisionCallbacks` 58 % of logic.
  - spawnStormScene: `_spawnAt` 40 %, `despawn` 12 %.
- **Spatial is the largest engine sum.** `gather_batch` is 1 599 ms/s over 18 scenes and `publish_batch` 1 447.
  - Boids: spatial 583 ms/s on each of its two workers, gather 44 %, `rebuildOwnedRows` 26 %.
  - orientedBox: gather 76 % of 352.
  - movedBodiesMixed: publish 46 % of 553.
  - stationarySpatialWide: `publish_batch_u32` 61 % of 783.
  - Predator: gather 37 %, publish 31 %, rebuild 17 % of 412.
- **Pre-render and Pixi.**
  - painterMove and painterSort saturate pre-render (995 and 968 ms/s), 40–48 % in `pack_sprites_split_scatter`.
  - adobeAnimateScene at the minimum zoom: pre-render 696 ms/s, `emit_rows` 44 %, `pack_sprites_split` 28 %.
  - Predator: pre-render 368 ms/s, 39 % in `stamp_light_range`.
  - textureUpload: Pixi 900 ms/s, 96 % in `uploadSharedImage`.
  - meshApi: Pixi 351 ms/s, 32 % `rewrite_corners` and 32 % the UV upload.
- **Scenes that load nothing.** Several stress scenes load no worker past 50 ms/s at their default knobs: bunnyMarkStress, spritePack, painterAdobe, decorationSway, audioStorm.

**Outcome.** EXECUTION_PLAN's Wave 7 orders what is left:
- step 0's checks;
- nine hypotheses, ranked 1 to 9: E-144, E-139, E-140, E-141, E-142, E-146, E-147, E-143, E-145;
- the review items, among them a new one, N-78;
- a triage of the 39 older pending rows: 14 done, 22 stale and 3 small speed items, with the register moves listed and not applied yet.

records.title: The ground-row key alone costs pre-render 3.1 % against main’s key, where nothing y-sorts
records.text:
What the ground-row key costs, alone. ABAB from worktrees, Chrome headed, owner preRender,
particleIntegrateStressScene?tween=1 (65 000 particles in view, nothing y-sorts), 4 pairs: A = e5e8d4bd, B = the same
tree with collectVisibleParticles' key as on main ((y + z) * K, or y * K for a flat particle; b6bfa546, an

worse in 0/4 (pairs -3.0, -3.1, -4.9, -3.2 %), cv 3/3 %. The floor and the bias cost about 2 ns a particle; in that

records.title: Particles skip their sort key when no layer y-sorts: pre-render −4.3 %, the branch now 4.6 % under main there
records.text:
collectVisibleParticles computed every particle's sort key, every frame, though a key orders a particle only in a
layer that y-sorts: without one, orderSortKey keeps the zIndex alone and the emit writes no key. c08f3548 reads
Layer.anyYSorting() once a frame (a layer's flag can change at run time) and, with none y-sorting, gives the
particles one key in a loop of their own: no floor, no viewMode / flat / y / z loads. tests/node/particleSortKey.test.js
holds the drawn rows and their y to the keyed run's.

ABAB from worktrees, Chrome headed, owner preRender, particleIntegrateStressScene?tween=1, 4 pairs, e5e8d4bd (A)
against 388f0682 (B; amended into c08f3548, the same tree): pre-render 3.402 -> 3.232 ms, paired -4.3 %, worse in 0/4
(pairs -10.3, -2.5, -2.0, -6.2 %), cv 3/2 %. KEPT (product).

the same keys for every float32 y (tests/node/particleSortKey.test.js: parity, and an arithmetic sweep up to

records.title: PR #5: WebGL dropped the GPU particle records a frame drew none of
records.text:
Bug, fixed in cf88429f. Pixi's WebGL buffers upload the range of their last update() at the next draw that binds
them; a GPU particle ring that published records in a frame that drew none of them (a hidden layer, or a
sortWithEntities layer whose groups were all off screen) lost that range, and those particles drew stale records
later. The ring now flushes through renderer.buffer.updateBuffer when it publishes. tests/node/gpuParticleBatch.test.js
models the vendored GlBufferSystem.updateBuffer's lazy range and fails without the fix. Kept (hygiene).

records.title: PR #5: the y-sort proxies sort groups by merging runs, 2 048 groups 1.5 → 0.25 ms a frame
records.text:
The y-sort proxies sorted the frame's groups by insertion: n^2/4 compares, 1.5 ms a frame at 2 048 live groups.
1fe2d1c2 sorts runs of 32 by insertion and merges them bottom-up (pre-render's mergeSortPrefix, E-08, on the keys
themselves); runs already in order are not merged, so a frame mostly in order costs about n compares. Node, collect
and write per frame with 20 000 entities: 2 048 groups 1.48-1.58 -> 0.22-0.29 ms; 1 024 groups 0.43-0.58 -> 0.12-0.20
ms; 256 groups 42 -> 26 us. Stable, as before: tests/node/gpuParticleProxies.test.js. Kept.

records.title: PR #5: Pixi's WebGL shader sync without for…in: 7.4 MB/s of garbage gone in the GPU particle scene, 0.7 MB/s in Predator
records.text:
Pixi's WebGL shader sync (pixi.js/unsafe-eval's generateShaderSyncPolyfill, the bundle's G_) walked every shader's
groups and resources with for...in over integer keys on every draw: V8 builds a key array for each such loop, so
every WebGL draw made garbage, in every scene. f2d34f6a replaces the polyfill at build time
(scripts/pixi-stubs/shaderSyncPolyfill.mjs): a per-shader plan of (group, resource) pairs in a WeakMap, built once,
checked per draw by each group slot's BindGroup identity and its key count (BindGroup patched to count its keys,
_weedKeys), rebuilt when either changes; the per-resource body is upstream's. tests/node/pixiShaderSync.test.js
compares its GL calls with upstream's.

Chrome heap samples, Pixi worker: gpuParticlesStressScene sort 8 073.5 -> 663 KB/s (G_ 7 431 -> gone); Predator
1 214.5 -> 522.6 KB/s (G_ 695.6 -> gone). Engine-wide: every WebGL draw of every scene took that path.

records.title: PR #5: the GPU particle path’s garbage taken out (logic 1 838.6 → 106.5, Pixi 663 → 81.7, pre-render 174.7 → 16.4 KB/s)
records.text:
The garbage PR #5's GPU particle path made per frame, and the engine-wide Pixi site it exposed, taken out over one
sitting day. Chrome heap samples (tests/bench/heapSampleWorkers.mjs, 10 s warm-up, 8 s sample unless noted),
gpuParticlesStressScene (webgl) unless noted, KB/s per worker. "Before" is the branch as it came, with the bug
fixes of that morning (cf88429f's WebGL flush, the pre-render key) and before any allocation work.

| worker, mode | before | after | what took it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pixi, default (sort) | 8 073.5 | 79.1 | f2d34f6a (Pixi's WebGL shader sync, 7 431 of it), 92fdd105 (render path), 545a0e5c |
| Pixi, interp=1 | 8 306 | 84.1 | the same, and collect's 138.6 in 545a0e5c |
| Pixi, Predator | 1 214.5 | 522.6 | f2d34f6a alone (G_ 695.6 -> gone): every WebGL scene |
| pre-render, default | 174.7 | 20 | 545a0e5c (collect 135.8 -> gone) |
| logic, default | 1 838.6 | 106.5 | 18c99ee5 (emitGpu: _emit, resolveParticleOp, randomRange, travelExtent), a2398952 |
| particle, default | 88.7 | 33.9 | a2398952 (syncParticleFeed 50.4 -> gone) |

Sites left on those workers are the engine's own per-frame ones that every scene has (_runFrame, camera latch,
Pixi's bind / startRenderPass / instruction GC tick) and once-a-frame functions still in Sparkplug during warm-up
(proxyView, _writeCameraRtTransform: every double they make is boxed until they tier up; gone from the 20 s runs).

records.title: ProxyCollector._grow’s closure allocated a context per listed group, every frame (Chrome only)
records.text:
ProxyCollector._grow built its arrays through an arrow function that captured `cap`, so every call allocated a
context (the calls that grew nothing too), and collect called it for every listed group, every frame. Fixed in
545a0e5c: a module function copies, and collect calls _grow only when n reaches the capacity.

Chrome heap sample (heapSampleWorkers.mjs), gpuParticlesStressScene, 20 s warm-up, 8 s sample:
- default (pre-render lists the groups): pre-render 176.5 -> 20 KB/s, collect 131.3 KB/s -> not sampled.
- interp=1 (Pixi lists them): Pixi 220 -> 84.1 KB/s, collect 138.6 KB/s -> not sampled.

Node never showed it: under heapSampleNode.mjs the collect probe allocated only during warm-up, before and after
(Node 22's TurboFan inlined _grow and dropped the context). A Node micro-test of the same shape (a method whose
closure captures a local, returning early) made 784 scavenges over 20 M calls against 3 without the closure, and
ran 2.7x slower: the pattern allocates wherever the method is not inlined.

records.title: Chunk twins: no stage rebuild per frame while the batch flips; NEUTRAL in time
records.text:
EntityChunks kept its chunk meshes per ring geometry of the entities batch, and the batch draws from its two
geometries in turn: every frame the last frame's chunks were hidden, this frame's shown and swapped into place, and
each set structureDidChange (Pixi's swapChildren and the visible setter both do), so the stage's instructions were
rebuilt every frame while GPU particles sorted among the entities. 6292504b keeps chunk j as a pair of meshes, one
per geometry, both children (slot 0 first), the idle one at alpha 0, which MeshPipe.execute skips (isRenderable
needs groupAlpha > 0) without a rebuild. tests/node/gpuParticleProxies.test.js checks structureDidChange stays false
over frames that flip the geometry (fails on the old code).

ABAB, Chrome headed, owner renderer, worktrees ea9b1983 (A, with the new ?hold knob) against 6292504b (B):
- gpuParticlesStressScene?hold=500&count=20 (1 000 groups held still: the layout this helps most), 4 pairs:
  renderer 5.210 -> 5.190 ms, paired -1.4 %, worse in 2/4, cv 9/3 % (A's own sides 4.98-5.97 ms). NEUTRAL.
- columns=30&count=300 (a group every few frames, so both sides rebuild most frames), 4 pairs: every worker under
  the 3 ms floor (renderer 1.447 -> 1.548 ms, pairs +23 / +22 / -7 / -10 %), not judged.
Garbage at 30 columns (heapSampleWorkers): Pixi 99.6 -> 81.7 KB/s, its instruction-building sites as they were
(next 6.9 -> 7.3, Ua 7.0 -> 6.1 KB/s).

Verdict: a hygiene keep. A stage rebuild of about 1 100 renderables is under this scene's detection limit; the change
removes a per-frame rebuild that grows with the stage (text, graphics, other layers), not a measured cost here.

records.title: Region UVs from a uniform: pixel-identical, two uploads per region per frame saved, garbage unchanged
records.text:
A look layer's region quads carried their UVs as vertex data that the CPU recomputed from the camera every frame, so
every region uploaded both its buffers every frame (two Buffer.update emits each, through Pixi's emitter). The
world-to-UV map is now a static UniformGroup of the layer's region shader (uUvX, uUvY: RegionQuads.setView, once a
frame, update() only when it changed), the vertex shaders apply it (gpuRegion.vert.glsl, gpuRegion.wgsl: a uniform
at @group(2) @binding(2)), and a quad's positions go up only when its rectangle changes.

Lockstep frames (150 injected steps) against the commit before, gpuParticlesStressScene: pixel-identical on
webgl look=1, webgpu look=1, webgl look=1 interp=1 and webgl sort=1 (0 differing pixels each).
What it saves is work, not garbage: two uploads and a UV loop per region per frame (regions are few: overlapping
groups merge). Pixi, look=1 at 30 columns (heapSampleWorkers, 20 s warm-up): 163.5 -> 167 KB/s, noise; the update
emits were not among the steady-state sites before either. Kept as hygiene (0c51068b).

records.title: Pixi's WebGPU draw path without garbage: 6 000.7 → 131.2 KB/s, renderer −35.6 %
records.text:
Pixi's WebGPU draw path made garbage on every draw, in every WebGPU scene: the encoder walked its bind groups, a
group's resources and the vertex buffers with for…in over integer keys (a key array per loop, and a parseInt per
buffer), BindGroup._touch did the same on every bind group switch and _key when dirty, the bind group cache built
`${key}:${layout}` per call, the mesh adapter passed a new options object to encoder.draw, and the pipeline cache was
looked up by a double key (boxed for Map.get). 477dfb39 patches them at build time (scripts/buildPixi.mjs,
patchPixiDrawGarbage), as f2d34f6a did WebGL's shader sync: BindGroup keeps its keys in for…in order (_weedKeyList),
the encoder walks indices, a BindGroup keeps its GPU bind groups per layout for its key and owning system, the mesh
adapter draws through one options object it empties after (firstInstance declared for instanceRangeDraw's hook), and
a Geometry keeps its last pipeline for its cache and key. tests/node/pixiDrawGarbage.test.js holds each patched
method to Pixi's own on the same input; the bundle rebuild is byte-reproducible.

Chrome heap sample, Pixi worker, gpuParticlesStressScene?backend=webgpu at 30 columns a second, 20 s warm-up, 8 s
sample: 6 000.7 -> 131.2 KB/s (_syncBindGroup 1 781.8, _touch 1 365.2, getBindGroup 699.9, _setShaderBindGroups
688.3, setGeometry 591, the adapter's execute 341.6, setBindGroup 229.8, getPipeline 91.9: all gone).
Lockstep frames against the commit before: byte-identical PNGs on webgpu sort=1, sort=0, look=1, interp=1 and
webgl sort=1.
ABAB from worktrees, Chrome headed, owner renderer, 0c51068b (A) against 477dfb39 (B, the same tree as 55c6ba0f),
gpuParticlesStressScene?hold=500&count=20&backend=webgpu, 4 pairs: renderer 5.216 -> 3.625 ms, paired -35.6 %,
worse in 0/4 (pairs -37.2, -22.9, -36.3, -34.9 %), cv 8/8 %. KEPT (product). The loops cost time as well as garbage.

records.title: N-83 fixed: a resize keeps a sorted look layer's regions on its look target
records.text:
Found while adding a run-time `Layer.resolution` for Blastforge's Pixel size (PR #5's branch). `_resizeCustomLayerRTs` releases the bind groups on a look layer's old render textures before destroying them; a `sortWithEntities` layer's `RegionQuads` samples `rtOut` through its own bind group, so the release destroyed it and the next frame's `setTexture` threw in `BindGroup.setResource`. From then on the layer drew nothing.

Reproduced in Chrome on the plain canvas-resize path: Blastforge, `scene.resize(1100, 700)`, then a Fireball: no fire and no smoke, only its ground light, and the Pixi worker logged "frame threw … Cannot read properties of null (reading '0')". With the fix (the regions go to `Texture.EMPTY` before the release and onto the new `rtOut` after it) the Fireball draws after the resize, sorted behind the tree, and nothing throws; Pixel size at 6×, 1× and 3× likewise.

Test: `gpuParticleProxiesPixi.test.js` runs the real resize path on a `RegionQuads` and fails without the fix (4 of 5 pass, the new one fails), passes with it. A resize is not per frame: a hygiene keep, no sitting. `main` is not affected (the regions came with the branch).

records.title: E-142 rejected: getTileId's divisions are not its cost; N-78 fixed with the world bounds
records.text:
tileMapMicrobench (44bdf560), Node, one loop per case after warmNormalCompile, three to four runs: shipped `map.getTileId(x, y, name)` 2.44 ns a call, the layer method alone the same (the name lookup is free), `Math.floor(x / w)` 3.6 ns, a guard then `(x / w) | 0` 2.3 ns, the stored reciprocal 2.6 ns, the world-pixel bounds then truncation 2.5 to 2.8 ns (machine noise about ±10 %). Parity against `Math.floor(x / w)` on quarter pixels: the reciprocal reads one tile low 203 times with 49 px tiles; `Math.floor` alone reads `data[NaN]` for NaN.

So the reciprocal is out and the speed claim with it. N-78 is fixed with the bounds form (9c6739dc), the only one that answers 0 for (−w, 0), NaN, the infinities and past the far side; `worldToTile` floors. Hygiene keep, tilemapStressScene, 4 pairs from worktrees: logic 8.240 → 8.229 ms (−0.1 %, worse 1/4, cv 0/0 %).

records.title: N-77 answered: headless Chrome's GPU process keeps a cache the dispose does not free
records.text:
`sceneCycleSmoke --commit` now splits the commit by process (ab033c25). Predator, 3 cycles, headless, the commit after destroy over the start: GPU process +90 MB, renderer +76 MB; the GPU process holds about 215 MB after the first cycle and after the third, so nothing grows with loads.

The fix N-77 proposed was built: the Pixi worker, asked to dispose, destroys its `GPUDevice` (WebGPU) or loses its WebGL context and answers, and `Scene.destroy` waits for the answer (at most 1 s) before the terminate. Against the same tree without it, the GPU process after destroy: Predator (WebGL) +82 MB with it, +90 without; balls (WebGL) +79 and +85; GPU Galaxy (WebGPU, headed Chrome, since the headless shell has no WebGPU) 81 and 80 MB against 100 at the start, everything given back either way. It freed nothing, so it was not committed.

The smoke judges the commit after destroy outside the GPU process, which it prints apart (cf090ed1): Predator +68.8 MB there, under the 128 MB limit.

records.title: N-76 fixed: no commit from a queue Pixi did not take
records.text: updateSpritesFromRenderQueue returns before reading the queue on a frame with no new queue when a sync exists (before the first frame, or a resume): the entity and glow batches keep what they committed, nothing before the first frame. _refusePackedFrame had kept the batch only when the header read incomplete; a complete-looking frame pre-render was writing was committed with two frames' rows. gpuPackSplitPixi.test.js commits nothing of such a frame (fails without the change). Predator (pre-render packs) draws 13 666 entities and BunnyMark (Pixi packs) 250 000, as before. One compare a frame: no sitting.

records.title: E-144 step 0: idle solver threads burn no CPU; the sampler counted their wait
records.text:
Step 0 of E-144: each thread's CPU time read from Windows (`threadCpuProbe.mjs`, 91434298: every thread of Chrome's renderer process, `TotalProcessorTime` twice over a 5 s window, after 8 s of warm-up), headless, from source.

- **bunnyMarkStressScene** (physics on, no bodies): the whole renderer process uses 73 ms/s over its 36 threads; the busiest thread 34 ms/s; none over 800 ms/s. The sweep's 1000 ms/s for each of Box2D's three solver threads (99.6 % in one function) was the sampling profiler counting threads blocked in their wait as busy. Idle solver threads burn nothing: there are no cores to win back.
- **ballsHeavyStressScene** (physics-bound): 2 665 ms/s in all; four threads at 643, 538, 538 and 513 ms/s (the physics thread and the three solver threads doing work), one at 301 ms/s; none spins at 1000.

What is left of E-144 is the clock reads while the solver threads wait for work (`_emscripten_get_now`, 9 % of each thread in ballsHeavy's profile, which also counted blocked time, so the real share is unknown). A thread spinning for work is off the critical path, so the gain would be cores for the other workers, not physics' step. It needs the names build of Box2D to see who reads the clock (the scheduler spin, the step profiler) before any change. Lowered behind the logic items.

records.title: E-139 kept: component getters read numbered slots (Predator logic −8.0 %)
records.text:
The getter (gameObject.js `_ensureComponentAccessors`) read `this._componentCache[name]`: the getters were closures of one function, so the keyed load saw every component name, from objects filled in the order each entity first touched its components. The variant numbers each class's components; an instance keeps them in `_components`, an array made in `bindToEntitySlot`, and each getter reads its slot by the integer it captured (9fa90154).

**Kernel** (`componentGetterMicrobench`, 02d5b0c3: five classes, each tick reading its components in its own order): 23 ns a getter read shipped, 7.3 ns with the slots copy; after the change the shipped getter reads in 6.7 ns.

**Owner, adobeAnimateScene at the minimum zoom** (4 pairs from worktrees, 02d5b0c3 against the change): logic 2.418 → 1.775 ms (−26.6 %), below the 3 ms floor, so not judged; the scene has no load knob. Physics +1.7 % (4/4, cv 2/2 %), a worker the change does not reach.

**Predator** (owner logic and the gate, 4 pairs): logic 3.979 → 3.620 ms (−8.0 %, worse 0/4, cv 2/4 %, −4.9 % against the other workers, lower 4/4); spatial −0.8 %, physics −3.4 % (cv 9/6 %), renderer −2.4 %, pre-render +0.1 %; presented 60.0 both. **Kept.** No A/A this session for these scenes.
