| Predator (step 6.46 ms, 60 drawn) | 456.7 | 170.8 | 67.3 | 130.7 | 56.8 | 28.9 |
| Adobe (pre-render 14.7 ms limits) | 386.8 | 174.2 | 149.7 | 23.9 | 17.4 | 19.3 |
| BunnyMark (GPU-bound, 283 frames in 8 s) | 172.2 | 112.7 | 30.2 | 9.2 | 8.9 | 10.5 |
| painterMove (pre-render saturated, 28 fps) | 254.5 | 88.7 | 124.0 | 13.0 | 8.3 | 20.2 |

Outside Predator, what Pixi does besides uploading is 0.15–0.4 ms a frame. **Predator's 130.7 ms/s (≈2.2 ms of its
6.46 ms step)** is, inclusive: the render groups' transform walk (`_updateRenderGroups` → `Fa`/`zd`, the recursive
updateTransform under a container that is not a render group) 35.7, the sprite batcher (`execute` of the batch pipe,
`packQuadAttributes`, `updateElement`) about 21, shader and uniform sync (`bind` :188, our E-148 plan `N_`) 23.4,
texture binds (`bindSource`) 14.6, the rest render targets, clears and draw issue. The only plain sprites Predator has
in number are the decal tiles: 40 × 20 `PIXI.Sprite`s of 256 world units (10 000 × 5 000 world), each with a texture of
its own, made visible at their first splat and never culled, under `decalTileContainer`, which `_placeWorldCamera`
moves every frame. A moved plain container makes Pixi recompute every visible child's group transform and re-pack
its quads; one texture per tile breaks the batch at each texture-unit limit. Opened as E-175 (the attribution is from
the call tree, not yet a sitting).

For the question this answered (does Pixi limit the engine): in none of the four scenes is the renderer the worker
that sets the frame (physics in Predator, pre-render in Adobe and painterMove, the GPU in BunnyMark); the bytes moved
(pack, W30 copy, upload) are the renderer's cost and stay with any renderer; E-162 is the lever for them.

records.title: E-178 rewritten: speed stays derived in the particle worker
records.text: The owner, 2026-10-29: computing RigidBody.speed on read would move the work to the logic workers, which the particle worker's derive pass exists to spare. The first premise was also wrong twice: the derive is already opt-in per class (`static deriveSpeed = true`; Predator's Person and Boid), and game code reads `RigidBody.speed[i]` from the array (boid.js, person.js, personAnimationFsm.js), which a getter cannot serve. E-178 now makes the pass cheaper where it runs: a dense f32x4 kernel over RigidBody's block in Box2D's memory, or the JS loop with the square root in place. No stress scene opts its bodies in, so a knob comes first.

records.title: N-94 fixed: the Pixi worker's raw texture uploads put back the unit's binding
records.text:
**N-94 fixed: the Pixi worker's raw texture uploads could leave a texture unit holding another texture than Pixi
tracks.** 2026-10-29, found by E-175's culling check, fixed in 2f96ab60.

- **Found:** decalStampStressScene in lockstep, then the camera panned and zoomed over six views. With the decal tiles
  outside the view hidden, one view (zoom 1.5) drew tile (3, 4) with another tile's texture: 10 746 pixels, the same
  every run; the same code twice was exact. A plain container with the culling did the same, so it was not the
  render group.
- **Cause:** `_uploadDecalRgba8`, `_gpuRecordRowsGl` and `_uploadRgba32FloatGl` call `texSys.bind(source, 0)`, then
  `gl.bindTexture`. When unit 0 already holds the source, Pixi's bind does nothing, not even select unit 0, so the raw
  bind lands on the active unit; Pixi still takes that unit to hold the texture it last bound there and skips binding
  it for the next batch. The culling changed the batches enough to show it.
- **Fix:** the three put back the active unit's binding after the upload (`sharedTextureUpload.js` already did). With
  it on both sides, the six views are the same pixels with and without the culling.
- test:node 2129/2129, test:demos 100/100.

records.title: N-95 fixed: Pixi's WebGL integer texture formats take *_INTEGER, no invalid texImage2D
records.text:
**N-95 fixed: Pixi allocated the WebGL integer textures with an invalid texImage2D.** 2026-10-29, found by the owner
opening carScene (two GL_INVALID_OPERATION warnings in the console), fixed in f3d3d33f.

- **Cause:** Pixi 8.20.1's `mapFormatToGlFormat` gives the integer formats (`r8uint` … `rgba32sint`) `RED`, `RG` or
  `RGBA`; WebGL 2 wants `RED_INTEGER`, `RG_INTEGER` or `RGBA_INTEGER` beside an integer internal format. A source
  with the upload method `unknown` gets an empty texture from Pixi first: E-162's indexed-sprite statics texture
  (`rgba32uint`, 3072×37 in carScene) logged "Invalid combination of format, type and internalFormat" once, shown
  twice (worker and page), before the engine's upload reallocated it right. No wrong pixels, only the noise.
- **Fix:** `scripts/buildPixi.mjs` patches the map at build. The rebuilt vendor differs from HEAD's only there (the
  unpatched build is HEAD's byte for byte).
- **Check:** carScene in Chrome with a `texImage2D` spy in the Pixi worker: one invalid call before (RGBA32UI
  3072x37 RGBA UNSIGNED_INT), none after; 23 calls both sides.
- test:node 2129/2129, test:demos 100/100.

records.title: Three engine bugs found building the GitHub Pages site: bundle export default, mask 0, read-only spawn keys
records.text:
**Three engine bugs found building the GitHub Pages site (`pages-site`).** 2026-10-29, a local server that
imitates Pages (the repo under `/Web-Engine-for-Enhanced-Dynamics/`, no isolation headers), Chrome through
Playwright; times from the result files.

- **Sweep:** all 32 scenes of `demos/menu.js` on the debug bundle through the root `weed-sw.js`: 30 started
  clean, destructibleTerrainScene and planetPhysicsScene each had one entity error, `simplify2 is not defined`

  worker loader leaves as it is. Fixed on the demo side in `1e8e93a0`; both clean on bundle and source after it.

  20 px from home and under 20 px/s after 7 s, their `ax` equal to the spring's; an 800 px/s kick died in two

random grass and loses where the order is predictable.** 2026-10-31, 20:16 to 20:30.

- **Kernel** (decorationVisibilityMicrobench, bbd5cd74: the shipped method on Predator's 20 000 blades, Node, 4
  alternations, same checksum): with 51 % on screen in random order, **4 084-6 420 -> 12 826-13 149 calls/s**

records.title: Four open engine bugs fixed: getJointCount() hang, read-only spawn keys, collision mask 0, bundle default exports
records.text:
**Four open engine bugs fixed, each with a test that failed before (wave11).** 2026-11-01, 02:40 to 03:04 (the
commits' times); `npm run test:node` 2145/2145 and `npm run test:demos` 100/100 after the last one. Hygiene: none
runs on a hot path a scene times except N-98's line in the spawn loop (one null test per spawn until a class needs it),
so no sitting.

- **N-100, `8feba1d3`:** `Joint.getJointCount()` with no argument never returned (`undefined < 0` is false and
  `head[undefined]` is not INVALID_INDEX). `getJointCount`, `getJoint` and `forEachOnEntity` now test
  `entityIdx >>> 0 !== entityIdx`; the test runs them under a vm timeout, so a regression fails instead of hanging.
- **N-98, `04d59ca3`:** `X.spawn({ speed: 2 })` threw "which has only a getter" inside `_spawnAt` and stopped the
  logic worker. The first write's throw checks the property's descriptor: a read-only key is warned about once per
  class and skipped from then on (a WeakMap, null until needed); any other setter error still throws.
- **N-97, Box2D `95dd9eb` and `cb11f523`:** `collider.collisionMask = 0` collided with every layer
  (`normalize_mask_bits` read 0 as the default for bodies). Bodies take their mask as given; queries keep 0 as the
  default. Rebuilt with `build_for_weed.bat` (SIMD copied, no-SIMD checked SIMD-free); the guide already said 0
  collides with nothing and now adds that Box2D's queries skip such a body. `collisionMaskZero.wasm.test.js`.
- **N-96, `99c6e660`:** a bundle's workers could not load a module with `export default`. The transform turns it
  into `exports.default` (a named class or function stays a declaration); a default import reads the module's
  default export by its resolved URL (`__blobDefault`, retried like named imports until that module ran); a module
  that does not compile is reported with its URL.

  decorationSwayStressScene at 320 000 (679), ballsHeavyStressScene (139), spawnStormScene (56).

  manager's dependency changes, the bench page's own). Nothing deopts every frame.

records.title: E-177 step 0b: Predator's changed statics are spread over the keys; a scatter, not dirty runs
records.text:
**E-177 step 0b: Predator's changed statics are spread over the keys, so they go up as a list the GPU scatters, not
as dirty runs.** 2026-11-01, 06:04 to 06:05 (the result files' times), Chrome, headed, source, detailed stats off;
pre-render instrumented in an overlay worktree (HEAD 69432150, with the key column; not committed): after each emit,
every sprite row's statics against its key's row of a table, and the dirty keys counted in chunks of 1 to 1 024 keys,
logged every 120 frames.

- About 13 800 sprite rows and 120 to 250 rows without a key a frame; 670 to 765 changed (4.9 to 5.5 %), their keys
  spread over 42 634 entities (the largest drawn, 42 632).
- An upload by chunk sends: chunks of 16 keys, 8 000 rows in 310 runs; of 64 keys, 19 000 rows (more than the frame)
  in 70 runs; texture rows of 1 024 keys, 26 of the 42. Single rows, 650 runs a frame. None pays.
- So the changed rows go up as a list, 64 bytes each (about 45 KB a frame against 590 KB of statics today), that the
  GPU scatters into its copy of the table: a draw into the statics texture on WebGL (Predator's backend, so the first
  one built), a compute pass on WebGPU.

The kernel (f185a8c4, gpuPackKeyedMicrobench in Chrome, Predator's shape): split 0.195 ms, keyed 0.270 ms a pack,
painter's order random; 0.135 against 0.22 to 0.31 ms with the queue's order nearly kept. A variant that builds and
compares the statics without the table's reads ties the split pack, so the extra is those reads (900 KB a frame).
Predator's trace (step 0's) runs the Pixi worker's memory-bound work at about 5 times its kernel time (pack_sprites_split
1.0 ms a frame against 0.195 ms; the arena copy at 1.2 GB/s), so the table's reads may cost much of what the smaller
copy and upload save (60 to 24 bytes a sprite): the sitting decides. If they do, the next lever is a generation per
row written by the emit, which compares in entity order; pre-render runs 4.07 ms in Predator against the renderer's 3.5
(R-0782), so that is not free either.

records.title: E-177 keyed frames as built: Predator's renderer 30-44 % slower; the compare must leave Pixi (v4: the emit lists the changes)
records.text:
**E-177, keyed frames as built (Pixi compares the statics by key): Predator's renderer 30 to 44 % slower; the
compare must leave Pixi.** 2026-11-01, 06:45 to 06:59 (the result files' times), Chrome, headed, source, detailed stats
off, Predator (WebGL, Pixi packs and sorts); single runs and CPU traces of the Pixi worker (8 s warm-up, 6 s window),
not a sitting: the build is a regression, so no pairs were spent on it.

- It draws right: screenshots of wave12 (0d72905b) and main side by side show the same scene.
- First look, one run each: renderer STEP - WAIT 4.164 ms on main, 5.987 ms keyed (+44 %).
- The trace (keyed, 0d72905b) against main's, ms of the Pixi worker a second: pack_sprites_keyed 181 against
  pack_sprites_split 62; the arena copy 30 against 39 and updateBuffer 28 against 43 (the bytes went from 60 to 24 a
  sprite, but the copy and upload fell 23 %, not 60 %); scatterStaticsGl 66, of which 92 % on
  gl.getParameter(COLOR_WRITEMASK): a query the GPU process answers, the first of a frame waiting there for every
  command before it. Fixed by reading Pixi's caches (1b230b05): 5.5.
- A fingerprint a key instead of the statics (8c378075, 8 bytes a key instead of 64): 164. With `--no-liftoff`: 162,
  so not the WASM tier.
- Variants of the kernel, traced the same way (built into engine.wasm, never committed): pose, key and slot alone (no
  stamp, no compare; the statics loads then dead) 23; with the stamps 62. A per-key array read at the address of a key
  read from the queue is a chain of two misses (idx -> key -> stamp), about 40 ms/s each in Predator, where the split
  pack's fifteen column reads depend on one load and run in parallel. The statics loads, the fingerprint and its
  per-key read make the rest (about 100).

So the per-row compare cannot be in Pixi. Next (v4): pre-render's emit, whose per-entity reads are one level deep
(the collector gives the entity), compares each sprite's statics with an entity-indexed store it keeps in the
render-queue memory and, when they changed, writes the store's row and appends the entity to a ring; Pixi packs the
pose and the key only (23 ms/s measured) and scatters the store rows of the entities the ring lists since its last
frame (skipped frames are covered; a ring overrun re-sends the store). On a persist frame only the repaired textures
change, through the same path. The keyed frames stay on in wave12 (WebGL, Pixi pack mode) until v4 replaces the
compare; the branch is not merged as it is.

records.text:
**E-177, the keyed emit split in the kernel: v6's store costs the emit 12.3 %, of which 6.5 the store's writes, 4.9
the per-row flag and texture checks, 0.9 the ring; without a store (v8) it costs 2.7 to 5.1 %.** 2026-11-01, 08:16 to
08:25 and 08:54 (the result files' times), Node, preRenderEmitWasmMicrobench (13 532 sprites, 10 120 decorations) with
a keyed variant that binds the keyed regions (6dcf3d46 committed its v8 form), runKernelVariants alternating the
variants in separate processes.

- v6 (5eb1c011), 5 rounds, 08:16: plain emit 1 851 ops/s; the key column alone 1 875 (+1.3 %, a tie: writing the key
  is free); the keyed emit with the store and ring 1 623 (-12.3 %). Variants built into engine.wasm and never
  committed split it: without the store's writes 6.5 points come back, without the ring 0.9; the flag and texture
  checks, each a read at the sprite's entity, keep 4.9. A rerun of v6 gave -18.3 %: kernel runs of this emit move
  several points.
- So the store is the cost, in the kernel and in situ (each write a random line of a 2 MB array that Pixi reads back
  from the ring): v8 drops it. The emit marks a changed sprite in its key (its flag, a moved frame or texture, a
  repeating sprite), Pixi takes the marked rows' statics from the queue it packs anyway, and a header resyncs Pixi's
  texture when it misses a frame.
- v8 as prototyped, 5 rounds, 08:25: plain 2 029, keyed 1 925 ops/s (-5.1 %). v8 as committed (ce8ad4b9, with the
  texture compare and the persist marks), 3 rounds, 08:54: plain 1 966, keyed 1 914 (-2.7 %, a tie).

records.title: E-191 step 2 kept: keyed caster rows, Predator crowd 1.5 pre-render -16.8 % (0/4)
records.text:
**E-191 step 2 kept (de71ce66; sat as 1c4db31c, the same tree): keyed caster rows, Predator crowd 1.5 pre-render -16.8 % (0/4), renderer +1.2 %
(-4.4 % against the others).** 2026-11-01, 13:48 to 14:08 (the result files' times; the first probe's file was overwritten), Chrome, headed, source, detailed
stats off, Predator `?crowd=1.5`.

- **What it does.** Pixi's entity batch stores each keyed upload's queue frame in the keyed header's LIVE word once Pixi
  has the keyed caster passes; while the word is within two frames of the one being written, pre-render packs the sun
  casters as keyed rows (pack_casters_keyed: x, y, the key and a zero, the shadow terms; 7 floats instead of 22) and the
  stamps copy them with their light (11 floats), with GPU_FLAG_KEYED_CASTERS in the GPU queue's header. Pixi draws the
  sun from the entity batch's instances (step 1) or from those rows, and the stamps from theirs, with the shadow program
  reading the statics by key (spriteIndexedVertex's casterRows form: no rotation; a stamp row's light). A caster without
  an entity key, a stale word or a scene not keyed packs the full rows; a skipped shadow frame republishes keyed rows
  only while the word holds.
- **The first build never ran.** The first probe counted keyed rows on 0 frames, and a diagnosis (13:48) found why: the GPU pack's view of the main queue
  (`_gpuSoAFromViews`) dropped the key column, so every caster read as keyless (22 860 of 22 860) and each frame packed
  the full rows. Fixed in the same commit, with a test. Then (13:50): keyed rows on 595 and 600 frames of 600, the
  stamps drawn from them (595, 600), the sun from the instances (597, 600) and from keyed rows once. Zoomed in (0.6, 1.2)
  the keyed frames pause after about 80 frames (E-188's grass) and the full rows come back, as built. Screenshots against
  cd6183bb's at the default zoom (13:49 and 13:50, 13:55 and 13:56) show the same shadows, no stray quad.
- **Correctness tests.** shadowStampKeyed: on 60 random stamp frames, the keyed rows stamp the full rows' (light, caster)
  pairs in the same order, each row the caster's keyed row and the same light bit for bit. spriteIndexed: the casterRows
  forms. instancedSpriteKeyed: LIVE stored on keyed frames only, the caster rows' geometries. shadowIntervalRepublish:
  the LIVE window, the keyed republish, a stale word packing again.

- **What it does.** A scene whose sprites go keyed keys its decorations too, where the statics texture also holds a row
  for every decoration slot (keyedDecorationsFit): a decoration row's key is its slot past the entities, so Pixi's
  texture keeps its statics there and a frame sends its pose alone. The emit marks the key changed when the statics the
  row got (scale, alpha with the zoom's fade, tint, texture, anchor) differ from the ones its slot last emitted, kept in
  a record a slot (32 bytes), or when the record is from an earlier epoch, which pre-render moves when Pixi asks for every
  statics again. Before it, Predator zoomed in past 0.5 drew its 20 000 grass decorations as rows without a key, which
  went up every frame (64 bytes each) and paused the keyed frames after ten losing frames, and E-191's keyed caster rows

  animated sprites' marks and the rows that still have no key).

  its later rows that frame do not; held statics mark none; a texture, an alpha and a tint mark their slot alone; the
  zoom's fade and a new epoch mark every one. renderQueueMemory: the keys past the entities, the texture's rows, the
  records' region (zero, so stale from the start).

records.title: N-109 fixed: integer textures bind on the top texture units, Pixi's batcher no longer drops the lighting draw
records.text:
**N-109 fixed: an integer texture left in a low texture unit made WebGL drop Pixi's batched draws, the lighting
sprite among them.** 2026-11-03, found in Conurbano-weed (a game on the 0.13.0 bundle: at night, zoomed out past 0.5,
the lighting went off), reproduced in Predator, fixed in ffa862bd.

- **Cause:** WebGL 2 checks every active sampler of a program against the texture its unit holds, read or not, and
  drops the draw on a mismatch (`GL_INVALID_OPERATION: Mismatch between texture format and sampler type`). Pixi's
  batcher declares sixteen float samplers (`uTextures`) and binds only the units its batch uses. The shader sync
  (`scripts/pixi-stubs/shaderSyncPolyfill.mjs`) gave the integer textures (`rgba32uint`: E-162's and E-177's
  statics, E-157's GPU particle rings) the next unit up, so after an indexed or keyed entity batch unit 2 held the
  statics, and the next batched draw, `lightingDisplaySprite`'s multiply, was dropped: night looked like day.
  Predator's entities go keyed at any zoom, so Predator lost that draw every frame, by day too (where it shows less).
  A batched draw costs the Pixi worker the same CPU whether the GPU drops it or not.
- **Fix:** integer textures take the top units, counting down from `MAX_COMBINED_TEXTURE_IMAGE_UNITS - 1` (at least
  31 in WebGL 2; the batcher reads 0 to 15); float textures keep units 0 up, numbered as before. The record-texture
  uploads (`_gpuRecordRowsGl`) bind there too, not on unit 0. The rebuilt vendor differs from HEAD's only there (an
  unchanged rebuild is HEAD's byte for byte). WebGPU binds by layout, not by unit: not affected.
- **Check:** headless Chrome (SwiftShader), a GL spy prepended to the Pixi worker (each draw's GL error and, on the
  first ones, the sampler that mismatched; the draws made while units 0 to 15 held an integer texture), counted
  from the start of each load to its end (about 45 s: a 25 s warm-up, two 10 s windows; headless draws a few frames a
  second, so before the fix one draw a frame was dropped: 30 in the last 10 s at zoom 1, 14 at zoom 0.3):

  | load | before: dropped draws, draws with an int texture in 0-15 | after |
  |---|---|---|
  | Predator `?hour=23&zoom=1` | 177, 1943 (every one `batch-vertex`, `uTextures[2]` on RGBA32UI) | 0, 0 |
  | Predator `?hour=23&zoom=0.3` | 51, 735 | 0, 0 |
  | Predator `?hour=23&zoom=0.3&indexedSprites=0` | 0, 0 | 0, 0 |
  | gpuParticlesStressScene (no batched draw after the rings) | 0, 10165 | 0, 0 |

records.title: N-111 fixed: the texture LUT folds past 2048 frames; the seven exact scenes match pixel for pixel, folded too; WebGPU draws
records.text:
**N-111 fixed (f47a2e86): the texture LUT folds into rows of several frames past 2 048, so an atlas of any practical size draws.**
2026-11-03, at the owner's ask, the bug reported the same morning from Conurbano-weed (9 020 frames drew nothing on SwiftShader's 8 192-texel limit; 7 938 drew). The WebGPU runs 04:12 to 04:14 (their screenshots' times); the lockstep runs just before them (a passing run deletes its files).

- The fix: `textureLutLayout(count)` keeps one frame a row up to `TEX_LUT_MAX_ROWS` (2 048, WebGL 2's promised `MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE`) and past it puts K = ceil(N / 2 048) frames a row: 3·K texels wide, ceil(N / K) rows, neither side past 2 048 up to 1 396 736 frames (past that an error names the frame count and the limit). `packTextureLutRgba` writes the layout, the Pixi worker sizes and uploads the texture by it (`_texLutWidth`, `_texLutHeight`), and the 12 shaders that read `uTexLut` take K from the texture's width and fetch frame t at (3·(t % K), t / K). Up to 2 048 frames the texture is the one it was, bit for bit.
- **WebGL, pixel for pixel** (the lockstep visual suite, headed, its seven `exact` scenes: balls, liquidfun, particles, oriented, lfstress, vispoly, compoundvis; baseline saved on the code before the fix): the new shaders draw 0 of 921 600 pixels differently in every scene; with every LUT forced to fold (3 frames a row, a temporary edit) again 0 of 921 600.
- **WebGPU, folded** (forced fold, headed runs with screenshots): BunnyMark `?backend=webgpu` (250 000 sprites), GpuGalaxy (GPU particles), MeshGallery (mesh UV fills), BadPiggies, and Predator switched to WebGPU for one run (sun shadows, 13 452 casters) all draw, with no shader, page or uncaptured GPU error.
- Cost: an integer division and remainder per vertex beside the three texel fetches, on the GPU; the CPU packs once per atlas load. No sitting: no worker's step changes, and the extra vertex arithmetic is far from what a frame's presented rate could show.

Hygiene keep. `textureLutFold.test.js` (layout, bit-identity below the limit, every frame at the texel the shaders compute, every reader folded).

Loads matched (ACTIVE_DECORATIONS 64 000, RENDER_QUEUE_SIZE 20 000 both sides). Both primaries are under the 3 ms floor, so the gate does not judge them; neither reads 3 % worse in 3 of 4 pairs.

In the game with `?debug`: houses' wall pieces, trees' branches, people, the ground, 0 console errors. Same bundle with a CPU mask of 2 cores and the game's two-core config (HC = 2: 2 logic workers, 2 physics, 1 spatial, against 3, 4 and 2 at 16 threads), 3 runs of 3: the same. The page still reports hardwareConcurrency 16, so the game's own HC constant was edited in the scratch clone.
- **The tracked lock's toolchain:** `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in a scratch worktree gives webpack 5.109.2, terser 5.49.0, terser-webpack-plugin 5.6.1 (dist on this machine comes from an untracked package-lock.json: 5.105.0, 5.46.0, 5.3.16). Its debug bundle in the game draws everything, and against the sources in 8 still scenes of attached pieces (decoration slots and entity ids 16 and 32 bits, parents with and without a sprite, pieces behind and in front, sheared and plain) the canvas captures are identical bytes, 8 of 8.
- **So this note withdraws what e62ac27d and 1348c4e8 said** (the tracked lock pins a failing toolchain, the toolchain is the likely cause). No bundle has been shown broken. What drew nothing in the container is not known: its Linux, its 2 vCPUs for real, or the game at that day's commit, none of which can be run here. The row's other readings (prod, unminified debug and the committed dist drawing in the same runs) stand as that session's.
- **What the builds do differ in:** a method-by-method comparison of the debug bundles, mangled names normalised, changes 44 methods on the main thread, 41 in Pixi, 22 in pre-render, 3 in the particle worker. Read in the attached path (`resolveAttachedDecorations`, `updateDecorationSway`, the pool's `spawn`) each change is a literal where an imported constant was read: webpack 5.109.2 inlines exported constants across modules, strings too (a GLSL source moved into `_scatterStaticsGl`). Elsewhere `??` survives where the older build wrote `null == x ?`, from a newer browser list. `entityIdNone`, an `export let`, is still read live. Filed as a lead.
- **The gap N-115 did show:** nothing tested that a bundle draws an attached decoration. `smokeBundleBrowser.mjs` now runs `attachedDecorationSmokeScene.js` (864d585f), whose only sprites are attached decorations on a black canvas, through the 4 ESM bundles: 32 768 pixels on each (8 squares of 64 × 64); with the pieces at alpha 0 all 4 read 0 and the smoke fails. `scripts/bundle-test` is a build input, so the page was left alone: dist's hash is unchanged (1c2a369c8e28452e), no rebuild, and no new sitting.

**PR #8's review, not merged: the default path draws main's pixels, and Predator's gate moves every worker alike, the unreachable ones too.**
2026-11-04, PR #8 (`lighting-ground-projection`, head 7febf1c0, branched from 1348c4e8): `config.lighting.groundScaleY` and `LightEmitter.sourceHeight`. Reviewed at the owner's ask ("chequeá"); no commit of mine on that branch. The owner's Chrome read 0 cores just before the sittings.

- **Suites here:** node 2230 of 2230, demos 100 of 100 (its note names failures of its container; none here).
- **Default path against main, canvas captures byte for byte:** the raycast scene (visPolyStressScene) and a still scene of 6 point lights over sprites, each on WebGL and on WebGPU (NVIDIA Turing, headed): 4 of 4 identical. That scene drew no cast shadow of its sprites, so the shadow shader's default is not covered by it: there it stands on reading (`floorD = d` at scale 1, and `invScreenDist` equals `invDist` past `distSq >= 1`).
- **groundScaleY 0.5:** ellipses, turning with a rotated camera; WebGL against WebGPU differ by at most 1 of 255 over every pixel. The raycast scene draws squashed pools with its occluders' shadows. Predator with the whole PR draws without artefacts. Not drawn here: particle and LiquidFun lights at scale under 1; `_drawLightSplat`'s axes were read against the camera matrix (a = z cos, b = z sin, c = -z sin, d = z cos) and agree.
- **Read:** the five uniform groups list their new uniform where the WGSL structs do (Pixi lays the buffer out in that order), one writer of the light texture, `_groundInvScaleY` set (line 7002) before the shaders are made (7039), new fields declared as doubles.
- **Predator's gate, engine only (the same demo on both sides), 8 pairs (20:09 to 20:17, 20:29 to 20:34): the runner's REGRESSION, on a worker the change cannot reach.** spatial 4.559 → 4.671 ms (paired +3.6 %, 7/8 worse, +0.7 % against the others), physics 5.269 → 5.610 (+3.8 %, 6/8, +2.8 %), logic 3.272 → 3.380 (+2.8 %, 6/8, 0.0 %), preRender 3.070 → 3.138 (+2.7 %, 6/8, −1.7 %); renderer, the owner, under the floor 2.479 → 2.382; 60.0 fps; loads within 0.2 %. The first 4 pairs alone read spatial +6.7 % (4/4).
- **A/A, the PR against itself, 4 pairs (20:23 to 20:29), this session's noise:** physics −9.3 %, logic −3.9 %, preRender −2.4 %, spatial −0.9 % (renderer 2.574 → 2.548); NEUTRAL.
- **The whole PR (Predator at 0.7, lamp posts at sourceHeight 110), 4 pairs (20:17 to 20:22):** spatial −0.0 % (2/4), physics −5.2 %, preRender −0.2 %, logic +3.3 % (4/4), renderer under the floor 2.580 → 2.481; loads within 0.3 %. The runner's REGRESSION is logic, also unreachable.

Reading: every worker moves about +3 % in one sitting and not in the other, the unreachable alike, so it is read as drift, with a detection limit of about 4 % on the workers that matter here and 9 % on physics. A common +3 % is not ruled out by 8 pairs; no code the PR changed runs on spatial or logic. No cost on the owner. Open when it merges: an entry here and a review row (the PR adds neither), and the bundles, which it leaves as they are. Predator's default look changes (the gate scene), with `?groundScaleY=1` for round pools; its lamp posts keep sourceHeight 110.

records.title: N-118: a rotation reaches the body of a Collider with no RigidBody
records.text:
Reported by the owner as Sun Street's cars vibrating between two rotations through a bend; the same cause as N-118. `set x` and `set y` send every body the rotation they read, physics exports it back over the channels, and `set rotation` told only RigidBody bodies, so on a Collider alone an old rotation went round and the true one showed for a frame now and then. Sampled on the page every frame: the channels held 1.7180 for a dozen frames while x and y moved, with one frame of the true value. `set rotation` and `setRotationCS` now tell any body; a rotated static collider also rotates in Box2D, which it did not. The RigidBody path of `setRotationCS` stays as it was.

`colliderRotationScene`, an angle advancing 0.02 rad a tick: 59 of 600 reads backwards, worst step 0.28 rad, box posed at 1 read 0.000; after, 12 of 600, worst 0.06, posed 1.000. The rest is a tick writing x and y before rotation when physics drains between them; Sun Street writes rotation first: 0 of 139 reads in the bends.

records.title: lighting.faces on Conurbano: correct to 2.1 of 255, neutral off, and Pixi's pass without garbage
records.text:
**DX-FACES: a decoration lights as a flat surface in 3D, on `dx/face-normals` (`3733cab3`, `63c8914c`), not merged.** Asked
2026-11-05 by the owner with Conurbano as its tester; written and measured 2026-11-05 and 06, on AC, Chrome quiet.

`lighting.faces`: a decoration says where its face looks and how high it is (`faceNormalX/Y/Z`, `faceHeight`), the entities
batch draws again into a face map at the light pass's size, and the light pass lights a face's pixel with `N · L` and its
real 3D distance, the sun by its angle. `DX_NORMALS_DESIGN.md` says what was built and what was left out.

**Correctness.** `faceLightCheck.mjs`, white faces against a formula written apart from the shader: worst sample 1.4 of 255
at five hours and settings, on WebGL and WebGPU; 2.1 of 255 over every sprite path (ySort off, indexed off, interpolation,
nearest, keyed). A 45-degree normal fell between two bytes and read 3.7 until the code moved to 1..253 with ±1/2 on a byte.
Default captures against main: 0 of 921 600 pixels on WebGL, WebGPU and raycast, day and night (one run of `night=1` read
3 pixels at 1 of 255; five reruns, two of them against itself, read 0).

**Kernel, faces off, against main (`preRenderWorker`).** 1959 → 1870 (−4.5 %, TIE) with a test in `deco_row`; with the
faces moved to a loop of their own, 1907 → 1868 (−2.0 %, 7 rounds, TIE). Moving two struct fields changed no byte of
engine.wasm and then read 1803 → 1899 (+5.3 %, TIE): on one binary the row moves ±5 %, so that is this kernel's limit.

**In the game, Parque Chas, zoom 2.2, 12 000 people, 22 h, prod bundle, `?caras=0` against faces, 4 pairs.** Renderer
3.88 → 3.70 ms (−4.6 %, faster in 4 of 4), pre-render 1.41 → 1.45 ms, logic 7.79 → 7.61 ms, 60 fps both. The game's
main-thread tint pass is gone with it.

**Load, faces off against on, `faceLightScene` with 20 000 faces and 48 lamps.** Light pass at ¼: renderer 0.717 → 0.761 ms
(below the floor), the same frames. At full size with 56 lamps: renderer 0.687 → 0.737 ms, pre-render 1.985 → 2.099 ms
(the faces' own loop), frames 565 against 565: no frame lost, so the GPU is not what limits it here.

**Garbage (the owner's point 3).** `heapSampleWorkers`, Pixi worker, `faceLightScene` town 8000, lamps 24, ¼. The feature's
code allocates nothing a frame. The pass is one more `renderer.render`, and Pixi made garbage in each: 138.4 KB/s without
faces, 209.7 with. Pixi's pass patched (`1eabb76a`): 88.0 and 145.8. A mesh per ring geometry and the camera's transform
worked out only when it moves (`63c8914c`): 140.2 with faces, no site of the feature in the list. Faces on now make what the
same scene made on main with them off, and every scene without them makes 36 % less.

**Predator, the branch against main (b6f0997d, 8 pairs, AC, Chrome quiet).** NEUTRAL: renderer 2.084 → 2.035 ms, spatial
−1.5 %, physics +3.4 % (5 of 8, not blocking). The first 4 pairs printed REGRESSION on spatial, +5.4 %: Predator has two
regimes, 2 200 and 7 700 bodies moved a frame, and side B drew the high one 3 times of 4 against 1. Over the 8, fitted against
BODY_MOVED_COUNT, every worker reads −0.2 to −2.1 % at equal load. A sitting before that shared the machine with a second
Predator, a run TaskStop had not killed, and was thrown away.

**Found on the game.** The sun's default `shadowAngleOffset` is π: every wall a camera sees is against the light all day, and
the day cycle's 90 degrees leave no sun on any wall at noon. Scene settings, not bugs: `shadowAngleOffset: 0` and the new
`maxElevation` (`e5453d2f`). Roofs above a lamp stay dark: right, and darker at night than the floor's pool made them.

Not done: one wall shadowing another; faces on layers other than the entities'; `raycasted` turns faces off.

records.title: A sprite in a face's row read as that face: people and cars dark for a frame on a zoom
records.text:
**A sprite that sorted into a face's row read as that face.** The owner, on the game, 2026-11-06: people and cars went dark and came back, frame by frame, when zooming. None of the sittings before saw it: they were still pictures, and at a still camera no row changes hands.

A decoration's face travels in the row's tile offsets. An untiled sprite's row cleared its repeat and multipliers but not the offsets, which nothing read until DX-FACES, so a person or a car in a row a face held was drawn into the face map with that wall's normal and height. Next to a lamp it went nearly black for that frame. The parity test could not see it: the JS reference left the same offsets alone, and its rows never change hands. The new test swaps faces and sprites between two frames, and failed with a sprite holding code 9034.

**Measured on the game in motion**, Parque Chas at 22 h, 23 000 people, Chrome on the GPU, filmed through the compositor at 55 fps, each walker tracked from the published queue and its body's brightness followed. A person has no reason to change brightness from one frame to the next, so a step is flicker.

Slow zoom (2.4 to 3.8 and back, 7 s, about 55 000 person-frames, one spot):

| | step ≥ 6 | ≥ 10 | ≥ 16 | people with 3 steps ≥ 10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 0.400 % | 0.263 % | 0.163 % | 19 |
| fixed, sources | 0.107 % | 0.025 % | 0.013 % | 1 |
| fixed, prod bundle | 0.116 % | 0.029 % | 0.011 % | 2 |
| faces off | 0.111 % | 0.020 % | 0.005 % | 0 |

Fast zoom (1.8 to 4 and back, 1.8 s, about 16 600 person-frames): sprite rows carrying a face 41.7 a frame, up to 170, to 0 in every run; step ≥ 10 5.07 % → 1.30 % (1.42 % on the bundle), people blinking 99 → 35 (40); faces off 1.05 % and 29. What is left there is the camera's own motion against the rectangle followed: the worst strip, at the screen's edge, shows no change of light. At 17 h on the bundle, 1.01 % and 19.

Kernel `preRenderWorker`, faces off: 1945 → 1967 (+1.1 %, TIE). Only a row that takes the `tilesDirty` branch does more. Node suite 2306 pass, demos 100, bundles 271 and smoke OK.

Two false trails on the way, worth keeping: a whole-screen flicker count was ruled by the asphalt's speckles and by how bright the walls are, and read no change; people planted still read none either, even before the fix, and nothing here says why. Follow the ones that walk.

Seen once in 177 walkers, not a matter of light: one person drawn in front of a car and behind it in turn over six frames. A still camera in the same spot, 10 s, reads no flip against a still car with faces on or off; a car that moves falls outside that count.

records.title: VolumeShadowCaster, phases 0 and 1: pictures equal, the renderer 5 % under meshes by hand, the game faster
records.text:
**VolumeShadowCaster, phases 0 and 1: kept.** The owner took the plan's five recommendations on 2026-11-06: the name, no `castsLights` by default (not built yet), a per-volume `floorScaleY`, a mesh of its own refused with a warning, phases 0 and 1 first. `DX_VOLUME_DESIGN.md` says what was built and where it left the plan.

**Pictures.** The town of `volumeStressScene`, cars at 60 headings, written by hand against the component: 0 of 921 600 pixels on WebGL and WebGPU, floors of 0.7 and 0.6 on the cars, 1 and 0.5 on the houses. The hand-written side is the game's `cajaAuto` on the CPU, so the shader equals it. Default captures against main: 0 pixels on both backends, with and without a sunProjected layer. `sunMeshParity --bar volume`: a volume's shadow ends within 1.35 px of a ShadowCaster's, five hours, both backends. In the game, moved to the component: the houses' shadows do not appear in a difference of captures at gain 4, and `sombras.html`, every model at every heading, reads 0 pixels past 8 of 255 at 9 and 15 h, against the code before.

**Speed, `volumeStressScene`, 20 000 houses, 200 cars, the sun moving, 4 pairs, Chrome and Code under 0.25 core.** The first sitting printed REGRESSION: 238 frames drawn in 5 s by hand against 223 as volumes, in all 4 pairs. GPU-bound, and real: the shader normalized a heading for 1.5 million vertices a frame. With the heading worked out only for what turns on a flattened floor (`c32dbc59`), 22:34 to 22:40: frames 48.0 → 48.0 fps (238 to 241 on both sides), renderer 3.537 → 3.340 ms (-5.0 %, better in 4 of 4, cv 3/1 %): KEPT.

**The game, Parque Chas, 12 000 people, prod bundle, 4 pairs, before the move (`c8343af`) against after, both at the committed `lighting.resolution` 0.25.** By day, zoom 2.2, 22:40 to 22:46: renderer 4.11 → 3.50 ms (-14.7 %, 4 of 4), logic 8.41 → 7.80 (-7.3 %, 4 of 4), pre-render 1.36 → 1.33 (-2.2 %). At dusk, zoom 1.6, 22:46 to 22:52: renderer 3.89 → 3.58 (-8.1 %, 4 of 4), pre-render 1.83 → 1.68 (-7.9 %, 4 of 4), logic 7.79 → 7.60 (-2.6 %, 2 of 4). The move takes 4 092 entities out of the scene and a car's `setVertices` out of every turn.

**In motion.** A car followed by day through its turns: its shadow stays under it. A walker's frame-to-frame brightness through a zoom at 10 h: steps of 10 of 255 or more, 0.427 % → 0.273 %, and no sprite row carries a face. The biggest step on the new side is a person crossing a table.

**Found on the way, each with its test.** `addLevel` left a hole per level, and the last entities lost their volumes with room to spare: only the mesh-against-volume capture showed it, as cars missing. An entity on the layer with no mesh would fill its collider in black, so `clear`, a refused mesh and `setLayer` keep it off. `GameObject.tint` reaches a volume's row, so the layer paints black.

Open: lamps and headlights ignore a volume (phase 3), and the sun's mask (phase 2). The person seen drawn in front of a moving car and behind it in turn (R-0843) was not looked at.

records.title: VolumeShadowCaster's review closed: four edge cases fixed, pictures unchanged
records.text:
**A review of `dx/volume-shadow-caster` at `a448ebea`, closed: four fixes, kept as hygiene.** The review was a reading and probes in Node, by another session, with nothing timed. Each fix has a test that fails on `a448ebea`, written and seen failing before the fix.

- `541d5667`: a point, size or offset that is not finite is refused, with a warning that says so. A box with one x of NaN drew 4 vertices and 4 triangles, the first tetrahedron, since a NaN made `convexHull3D`'s tolerances NaN. A NaN corner in `addLevel` warned about the corner count. Not in the review: a size, an offset or a topScale that is not finite in `setBox` reached the arena, and its warning said the arena was full.
- `33ab1e18`: `setHull` refuses more than 4 096 points instead of hulling the first 4 096. On the code before, 5 000 points on a sphere took 21 s and drew 4 096 vertices; the hull test of 4 097 points took 134 s.
- `4fde4d5c`: a top that closes on a point or a line is a pyramid or a gabled roof, with no row of zero area: `topScale: 0` gives 4 triangles, a gable over 4 corners 6. The review's recipe, "the doubled signed area under an epsilon", would have let a top that crosses itself evenly through: its signed area is 0 too. Flat means all corners on one line within a millionth of the base's size, and a test keeps the crossed top refused. A topScale below 0 is refused.
- `64395cf1`: each kind of mistake warns once. At `a448ebea` one flag covered six call sites with five texts (the review said six messages).

Checks at the end, 2026-11-10: node 2342 of 2342, `check:types` and `check:dist` pass, bundles `1897910a` (embed and browser smokes on all 8, `test:node:bundle` 271 of 271). `sunMeshParity --bar volume`: 0.24 to 1.35 px at six hours on WebGL and WebGPU, as before. `volumeStressScene` by hand against volumes, cars on floors of 0.7 and 0.6, houses on 1 and 0.5: 0 of 921 600 pixels on both. Sun Street and the game use neither `topScale: 0` nor more than 16 points.

**Not built, on record (section 4 of the review).** A hull of boxes that share planes keeps a point on an edge or face of the final hull when it was outside the partial hull at its turn: the review's synthetic cases, two boxes side by side at one height 11 vertices for 8, three in a row 14 for 8, four in 2×2 14 for 8. Keeping only true corners and hulling again would fix it, and saves nothing here. The branch's hull over every house of the game's three barrios, re-counted for this record: Parque Chas 3 484 houses, 36 997 vertices; Carabobo 4 698, 50 351; Barrio 1 119, 11 862; at most 16 a house, none over the 16 the arena keeps for each. The review's "corners only" column (the same totals, no house smaller) was not re-run: the exports already hold corners.

For the owner, not touched: an `addLevel` that does not fit takes the whole volume off the layer (it could publish the mesh it had), and an `addBox`.

records.title: The Buenos Aires demo, and N-123: a VolumeShadowCaster with no volume yet warned
records.text:
**The Buenos Aires demo, built for DX-VOLUME and DX-FACES, and the bug it found (N-123), kept as hygiene.** Nothing timed.

The owner asked for buenos-aires as a demo in the engine repo: a small barrio made by the game's editor, with its people and cars, to try faces, volume shadows and lamps under control. The barrio is a new export (200 × 160 m, seed 385919651, no plaza; 191 houses, 1 234 props, 91 trees, 25 cars; 15 MB, `e8e5d2e9`). The demo (`a2848ced`) ports the game's houses, props, trees, people and cars without its traffic rules, with Sun Street's panel: clock, jump to an hour, night light, volume and sprite shadows hidden, lamps and headlights off, cars and people stopped, and reloads for faces, `lighting.resolution` and raycasted lighting. The floor is the game's shader, and `floor.wgsl` the same lines for WebGPU.

Checked in Chrome on this machine's GPU: no page errors on WebGL and WebGPU; WebGPU's floor equals WebGL's (the diff is the swaying plants); hiding the volume layer takes the houses' and cars' shadows; 312 of 400 people and 11 of 12 driving cars moved in 4 s, and with both switches off 4 people (0.2 px mean) and 4 cars (2 px, pushed). Read from the panel, not a sitting: renderer about 1.1 ms, pre-render 1.1 ms, logic 0.3 to 0.5 ms with 400 people. Eleven people sheets keep the packed atlas within 4 096 px (fourteen made 4 392 × 4 094).

**N-123** (`83ef3072`): every load printed "MeshRenderer requires setLayer on a LAYER_KIND.MESH layer". The game's wooden posts are houses with no shadow points (21 of 191 here), so their MeshRenderer, which VolumeShadowCaster brings, never joins the volume layer, and the collider-fill packer took them for a forgotten `setLayer`. It now skips entities with `VolumeShadowCaster.floorScaleY` above 0; the test (one such entity: no warning; a plain MeshRenderer next to it: one) failed before the fix. Node 2343 of 2343, demos 100 of 100, bundles `77284c15` (embed and browser smokes on all 8), `check:dist` fresh.

records.title: The Buenos Aires demo's load: 28.5 s to its first frame, 6.1 s after the packer, the floor and a loading screen
records.text:
**Why the Buenos Aires demo took 28 s to draw its first frame, and three fixes, kept.** Measured from `game.loadScene` in Chrome (WebGL, GTX 1650, ANGLE D3D11), with load-step times from `onProgress`, a main-thread CPU profile and a trace of every thread; the first drawn frame is the first screenshot that is not black.

On main (40f5d2f3): the atlas step finished at 21 058 ms, the world at 21 802, the first frame at 28 501. The main thread spent 19.2 s in `MaxRectsPacker.insert`: `isContainedIn` 12.1 s and `pruneFreeList` 7.0 s (N-124). After that fix the atlas came at 2 180 ms and the first frame at 10 358, the main thread idle: the renderer worker spent 8.0 s in Pixi's program link (`rh`) inside the first `_presentStage`. A trivial floor shader took that to 0.18 s and the first frame to 4 927 ms, so it was the floor: linked alone it took 6.1 s, 1.3 s with grass and dirt emptied, 2.1 s without the tree pits' loop.

- `53f789c9` (tool): `atlasPackMicrobench` on the 4 386 sizes the demo's load gives the packer, checksum 3981242099 (equal to the browser's placements); 17 873 ms a pack on main, free list peaking at 2 307.
- `6dcef423` (N-124): the prune tests only the parts a placement cuts, in the old order. 177 ms a pack, the same checksum; random packs equal to the old packer, with all four heuristics.
- `14022ad0` (demo): the floor decides what a pixel is, then draws it once; the tree-pit loop decides after it. Linked alone 6 177 -> 1 740 ms. The barrio's data in 8 views against the old shader: 7 identical, the whole-map view 10 of 589 824 pixels on a threshold. WebGL and WebGPU floors equal in the demo.
- `e6cd4905` (demo): a loading screen from `Scene.onLoadProgress`, kept until the renderer's STEP_MS is above 0.
- `4e3b772a` (N-125): the menu hides its list for any load.

Result, from loadScene: WebGL first frame 28 501 -> 6 081 ms, WebGPU 4 636 ms; opened as a user does, the screen comes up 3.3 s after navigation (the dev page's modules) and goes 5.5 s later with the barrio drawn. Node 2345 of 2345, demos 100 of 100. Not done: the game's own `shaders/piso.frag` still links in about 6 s on Windows; trimming stays on the main thread (0.6 s); Box2D's three task threads spin at a full core each during the load (9.9 s busy each in the trace), which this did not look into.

records.title: D1 and B1 of the volume review: a level that does not fit keeps the volume; WebGL float pictures filed
records.text:
**N-126, kept as hygiene; N-127 filed; 0.14.0 released.** Nothing timed.

The owner said yes to two items of the `dx/volume-shadow-caster` review: D1 (a level that does not fit keeps the volume) and B1 (file the WebGL float upload bug).

**N-126** (`3874fe59` on `dx/volume-keeps-mesh`): `addLevel` frees the entity's spans before it asks for the bigger mesh, so a refused level left the entity with no mesh and off the layer. The old mesh is still at the start of the scratch and fits the spans just freed, so it now goes back, on the layer, with the same warning about `lighting.maxVolumeVerts`. The test that held the old behaviour (`a volume that no longer fits leaves the layer with its mesh`) holds the new one, fails before the fix, and checks that the six free vertices still hold a three-cornered volume; a new test keeps a first volume's refusal. Guide, types and `DX_VOLUME_DESIGN.md` say so. Node 2346 of 2346, demos 100 of 100, check:types.

**N-127**, filed open: `uploadSharedImage` gives `texSubImage2D` a `Uint8Array` with type `FLOAT` and sends `r32float` as `RGBA`, so a worldRect layer's float pictures never reach the GPU in WebGL. Read in the code, not yet seen in a browser.

**0.14.0** is on npm (`7f7b5f00`, tag `v0.14.0`, pushed with main). The release script's own `npm publish` timed out on the browser approval (five minutes, nobody approved); two authenticator codes were refused within seconds with the clock right; a visible console ran `npm publish` with a TTY and the owner approved in the browser.

records.title: The atlas trim and N-126 merged with bundles; Box2D's threads do not spin during the load
records.text:
**The atlas trim (N-124's follow-up) and N-126 merged to main, with bundles; no bundle sitting, by chunk identity.** Two items left open by R-0849 are closed here.

**The trim** (`487e9a8a`, merged in `e6e1d8eb`): `SpriteSheetRegistry` trimmed each frame of a spritesheet from its own `getImageData`; it now reads the bounding box of the frames it needs once per sheet (`_readImagePixels`) and finds each frame's bounds in that one array (`_getTrimBoundsInPixels`), and a trimmed frame is drawn from the sheet with an offset source rect instead of a canvas of its own. In the Buenos Aires demo's load, `createBigAtlas` went from 1.53 to 1.69 s (runs before) to about 1.25 s, with the same packed atlas: the same hash of its pixels and of its JSON in both. `tests/node/atlasTrim.test.js` checks the bounds against the old canvas code (kept as `tests/reference/atlasTrim.mjs`) on random sheets, frames and thresholds, and the edges.

**Box2D's threads do not spin during the load.** A Chrome trace showed its three task threads busy for the whole load. Windows' per-thread counters (`TotalProcessorTime`, two snapshots) showed none of them near a core: the V8 sampler counts a wasm thread blocked in `Atomics.wait` (Box2D's scheduler spins 0.05 ms, then sleeps on a semaphore) as running. Nothing to fix.

**The merge** (`40ddb8b4`, with N-126's `3874fe59`) and bundles `b7699e54`: make_bundle, check:dist fresh, test:bundle (embed and browser smokes on all 8), test:node:bundle 275 of 275, Node 2348 of 2348, demos 100 of 100. No bundle-vs-src sitting: in the prod ESM bundle, six of the seven worker chunks are byte-identical to `7f7b5f00`'s, and the seventh differs only in `addLevel`'s refusal path and the atlas trim, which run at setup and load, not per frame; a sitting could not change a verdict.

records.title: The volume review's plan closed: D1's replacement test, D2, B2 and B3 filed, pictures unchanged
records.text:
**The plan that closed the review of `dx/volume-shadow-caster` is done; the last of it filed.** Nothing timed.

The owner handed back the review's plan ("dale"). Where each part stands:

The plan asks for a second test, the replacement: `33971553` sets a box, then a hull of 16 corners in an arena of 14, and the entity ends with no mesh and off the layer (the old box would be a wrong shadow). - **WASM:** A* in C (E-207; the flowfield gained 16× there, E-122).
- **GC:** listUpdates through a SAB ring (E-208), entity instances made at spawn (E-209), eslint-plugin-weed in create-weed-game (DX-LINT).
- **DX:** config validation and a size advisor (DX-CONFIGCHECK), workers 'auto' and a quality governor (DX-AUTOQUALITY).

records.title: Static flowfields in a binary file (DX-FFBIN), merged with their bundles; the last partial column and row they lost (N-133)
records.text:
**Static flowfields in a binary file (DX-FFBIN), and the last partial column and row they lost (N-133).** Asked by the owner on 2026-11-11 after reading the Buenos Aires demo's `ff_peaton0.json`: the barrio editor exports binary flowfields, WeedJS reads them with nothing to convert, JSON still loads, and the compression is ours (gzip that the browser opens), not the server's.

- **The format, WEFF version 1:** a 24-byte little-endian header, never compressed ("WEFF", version, compression 0 none or 1 gzip, a reserved u16, width and height in cells as u32, cell size as f64), then the cells as NavGrid holds them, x and y as Int8 per cell, row by row. The loader reads the format from the first bytes; a raw file is a view of the fetched bytes and a gzipped one inflates through `DecompressionStream` into the Int8Array itself. `src/core/staticFlowfieldFile.js`; `NavGrid.loadStaticFlowfields` (the old `loadStaticFlowfieldsFromJSON` is a deprecated alias); the guide's "Static flowfields" has the table.
- **Equal cells:** the editor's export of the demo barrio and `scripts/flowfieldToBinary.mjs` write the same bytes, and all 10 fields decode to exactly the JSON loader's cells (all 122 400 cell bytes each). Conurbano's 30 fields too (0 differ).
- **Sizes:** the demo's barrio 3 709 849 → 116 092 bytes (3.1 %); Conurbano's barrio 19.97 → 0.76 MB, Carabobo 58.65 → 1.90 MB, Parque Chas 84.99 → 3.39 MB.
- **Main-thread time** to turn the fetched bytes into cells, the demo barrio's 10 fields, headless Chromium, three fresh pages of seven rounds: JSON (decode, parse, quantize) 17.9 to 20.9 ms the first time, median 13.5 to 15.8; binary gunzipped one by one 8 to 10 ms; all at once 5.0 to 6.1 ms the first time, median 4.9 to 7.3. Node's web streams are slow and not representative (binary 52 ms the first time there).
- **All at once:** the loader awaited each fetch before the next; now the fetches go out together and the fields keep the order of the URLs (a test holds the answers and releases them in reverse; it fails on the old loader).
- **N-133:** the JSON loader clipped to `Math.floor(world / cell)`; `Math.ceil` keeps every cell the world touches. Conurbano had lost a column and a row in its barrio (958 x 322 of 959 x 323), a column in Carabobo, a row in Parque Chas. The demo's barrio, 408 x 150 whole cells, was not touched.
- **Checked in the demo** (headless Chromium, `/src`): the ten `.bin` files requested, each field 408 x 150, no errors, 390 of 400 walkers moved in 8 s.
- **Not measured:** STEP_MS. Nothing per frame changed (the sampler, `requestVectorFromStaticFlowfield`, is the same code), so no scene pair, and no bundle-vs-src sitting for this merge: the bundles were rebuilt and passed their smokes and the node suite.

records.title: DX-VOLLIGHTS planned (lamps cast a volume's shadow, basic and raycasted lighting) and N-134 filed (raycasted lighting hides every sprite shadow)
records.text:
**DX-VOLLIGHTS planned and N-134 filed: lamps do not see a volume in either lighting mode, and raycasted lighting hides every sprite shadow.** Nothing timed. Read from the code at 99e39b8b.

The owner asked whether Sun Street's raycasted lamps interact with its volumes. They do not:
- `VolumeShadowCaster`'s rows sit in the `volumeShadows` MESH layer, which only the sun moves.
- Raycasted lighting stops a lamp with pre-render's 2D sweep over `LightOccluder` shapes.
- Basic lighting stops it only with `ShadowCaster` stamps.

Sun Street puts a `LightOccluder` on every house and car. In its oblique view, that wedge darkens the wall that faces the lamp and runs to the reach whatever the object's height.

The owner then asked for a plan that pins down the API, the developer experience and the picture. It is `DX_VOLLIGHTS_DESIGN.md`, which works out DX-VOLUME's phase 3:
- **The shadow:** `p + (p − l) · h / (H − h)`, with `H` the bulb's `sourceHeight`. It runs to the reach where the object is taller than the bulb, fades with the lamp's falloff, and never falls on the object's own picture.
- **The cases:** each one with Sun Street's sizes. A car 100 px from a 40 px bulb throws 48 and 208 px (body and cabin); under a 150 px bulb, 9 and 22 px. A house 100 px from a 150 px bulb throws 226 px.
- **The API:** `castsLights`, as decided for DX-VOLUME, and the existing shadow-casting lights. A light skips its own entity's volume and any footprint it stands in. A class with both `LightOccluder` and a volume that casts lights warns at load.
- **Two ways to draw it:**
  - Basic lighting: into `shadowRT`, one draw per light, MAX within a light.
  - Raycasted lighting: a mask of four lights per pass that cuts each fan, with the volumes' own pictures cleared, because `visPolyRT` multiplies over the whole frame.
- **Phases 0 to 4** and **eight decisions**, recommended: basic lighting first; Sun Street on basic lighting with volumes, `R` comparing.

N-134 came out of that reading. `initVisibilityPolygonSystem` (pixiWorker.js) runs after `createCastedShadowsSystem` and hides `castedShadows`, because the cookies crushed the fans' umbra. The sun's sprite shadows and the lamps' stamps go with it. Conurbano's notes saw it ("turns off the projected shadows of people and trees"), and Sun Street runs raycasted by default. Confirmed in the code, not yet seen on screen.

Ranked 32 (N-134) and 33 (DX-VOLLIGHTS), after the queue's 31.

records.title: E-200 kept: lists two logic frames before each tick; Boids at a fixed load spatial -15.0 % (0/4), Predator NEUTRAL
records.text:
**E-200 kept (79065acc, sat as 7d19810e, the same tree): a class that ticks every few frames gets its neighbour lists two logic frames before its ticks. Boids at a fixed load, spatial -15.0 % (0/4).** 2026-11-11, 01:59 to 02:26 (the result files' times), Chrome, headed, source, detailed stats off, AC power, no other bench Chromium. Every sitting ran `runPredatorAbab.mjs --full-rev` from the main folder, so each side served its own revision's src and scenes.

**The change.** Spatial's stagger refreshed every list every `neighborTickInterval` frames (15 in Boids and Predator), whatever its entity's logic interval. Boid ticks every 30, so half its lists were never read. A soldier ticks every 6 and a civilian every 4; they read lists up to 14 frames old.

The spatial worker now reads logic 0's frame number. Logic publishes it in frameRateData as its frame starts, and `sceneWorkerBootstrap` passes its row as `logicFrameRateIndex`, with each class's `tickInterval` and whether it ticks. A class that ticks every T frames (`logic.staggeredUpdates`, a `tick`) gets its list on the logic frames f with f % P equal to the slot's offset:
- P is the smallest multiple of T not under the interval.
- The offset is (tickBucketPhase − 2) mod P: two frames ahead lands before the tick whether logic started this vsync before or after spatial.

The test is stateless: logic's frame modulo P once per class a frame, and one compare per slot. A first, countdown version missed phases when a row changed spatial worker, because the new owner's countdown was stale. Lights and classes that tick every frame keep the old countdown.

**Tests.** `spatialTypedStagger.test.js` checks lists against logic's tick phases: boids every 30, then a mixed scene (civilians every 16, soldiers every 18, boids every 30, props on the plain 15). It fails on main and passes here. Node 2355 of 2357 in the branch's worktree; the two failures are pixi tests that need node_modules, which that worktree does not have.

**Kernel.** `spatialWorkerMicrobench --types`, a tool commit of its own (eae26c6b), A B A B in Node, 4 pairs, n = 16 500, 3 workers:
- `boids`: 299.4 → 388.8 frames/s, +30.5 %, 4/4. Lists gathered 936 → 504 a frame, published 981 → 535.
- `predator` (civilians, soldiers, boids, props): 266.2 → 312.9, +17.1 %, 4/4. Gathered 936 → 850.
- No typed class: +5.1 %, 2/4. The same checksum and rates as main, so this is the kernel's noise.

**Boids, flocking (the demo as it is), 4 pairs: FAIL (load).** Spatial 8.403 → 7.322 ms (-17.4 %, worse 1/4, cv 12/9 %), physics -8.1 %, VISIBLE_ENTITIES -29.1 % (cv 9/1 %). Fresher lists changed the flock. A list up to 14 frames old still holds boids that have left, and pulls the flock together; a fresh one does not, and the flock spreads. B gathered 1 511 to 2 007 lists a frame against an expected 1 333: the 0.5 to 2 % of boids with no neighbour are searched every frame.

**Boids `?steer=0`, 4 pairs: KEPT (product).** A demo knob, its own commit before the change (ecaa2051): every neighbour is read and weighed, and their pull is scaled by 1e-9, so the flock's path does not depend on a list's age. Spatial 7.186 → 5.828 ms, -15.0 %, worse 0/4, cv 10/10 %. Physics -1.9 % (1/4). VISIBLE_ENTITIES +0.2 %, ENTITIES_PROCESSED +0.1 %.

**The session's A/A, Boids `?steer=0`, ecaa2051 against itself, 4 pairs: NEUTRAL.** Spatial +0.5 % (worse 2/4, cv 3/5 %), physics -1.1 %. The detection limit is about 3 to 5 %.

**Predator's gate, 4 pairs: NEUTRAL.**
- Spatial 4.905 → 4.511 ms (-4.8 %, worse 0/4; -6.4 % against the others, 4/4).
- Logic +1.1 %, pre-render +1.6 %, presented 60.0 both.
- Physics +10.2 % (worse 3/4, cv 15/4 %, not blocking) is load. B moved 27 % more bodies a frame (6 664 against 5 244 on average): fresher lists make the AI react. Per thousand moved bodies, B is 17 % cheaper (0.873 against 1.057 ms).
- Load keys within 0.5 %.

**The look, judged by the owner on 2026-11-11.** Side by side, 20 s after load with the whole world in view, main's flock draws thin streams and the branch's gathers into thick clouds: a list read when it is 0 to 14 frames old against one read at 2. Logic's four workers were on the same frame (frameRateData: 269, 592, 951, 1440 on all four), so the phase is as designed. The owner: the branch's looks better. Spreading the lists' ages like main's (an offset per slot) would have kept main's look with the same saving; not done.

records.title: N-79 fixed: a layer drawn in one pass takes its blendMode; one demo's beam retuned
records.text:

records.text:

- **N-131** (`5b860316`): `collider.isTrigger` changed on a live entity makes its body again. Marking LIFECYCLE was not enough: `syncBodySlot` makes an existing body again only for a new generation, so `box2dBodySync.remakeBody` gives a live slot one (and marks LIFECYCLE before the entity is live). In Chromium, with Box2D: a ball dropped on a platform and turned into a trigger 20 frames after its spawn rested on it at y 480 before, and falls through after. Predator's money, turned into a trigger a second after it drops, now is one.
- **N-135** (`77c81f77`), found while fixing N-131: `collider.enableHitEvents` had the same hole. Its setter marked LIFECYCLE and PHYSICS.md said the body was made again; it was not, and R-0857's "enableHitEvents already reaches the body" was wrong. Same fix.

- Bundles `d438e90f`: check:dist fresh, test:node:bundle 279 of 279 on each of the 8, test:bundle 8 of 8; the production bundle still holds none of the run-time texts.

**Checks.** Each engine fix has a test that fails without it. Suites at `7a0d2226`: test:node 2410 of 2410, test:demos 101 of 101. records.title: E-193 step 1 dropped: the keyed pack read in order costs the same in Pixi's worker; Predator crowd 1.5 renderer +2.6 %
records.text:
**E-193 step 1 dropped: the keyed pack read in the queue's own order (an inverse in C) costs the same in Pixi's worker, and Predator crowd 1.5's renderer reads +2.6 %.** 2026-11-11, from 04:17 (the sitting's first result file) to 04:23 (the second trace). Chrome, headed, source, detailed stats off, AC power. Nothing else ran on the machine: b3's sittings had ended.

**What was tried.** `pack_sprites_keyed_scatter` (b442ba45) is `pack_sprites_keyed` through W9b's inverse: `inv[queue row] = draw slot`, then the queue read in order, each drawn row's pose, slot pair and shadow terms written at its draw slot. The updates list in queue order; keys are unique a row. A repeated or out-of-range row declines it and the gather packs the frame. Pixi got an inverse for the keyed pack alone (`pixiKeyInverse`). `gpuPackKeyedScatter.test.js` checks the same frame as the gather (random and near order, with and without shadow terms, a repeated row).

**Kernels** (ef08b5d4, kept; Node, n = 14 000 rows, entities 42 600, run while b3 built bundles, so these are a screen):
- `gpuPackKeyedMicrobench`, warm, one thread: keyed 0.085 ms, keyedScatter 0.093 ms.
- `gpuPackKeyedCrossCoreMicrobench`, every queue column rewritten before each pack, three reps:
  - on the pack's own thread: gather 0.08 to 0.10 ms, scatter 0.10 to 0.12;
  - on a worker thread: gather 0.12 to 0.23 ms, scatter 0.12 to 0.23.
- Another core's writes cost +50 to +150 %, not ten times, and reading in order does not take that cost away.

**Predator `?crowd=1.5`, 4 pairs** (`--vs ef08b5d4 --hyp-rev b442ba45 --full-rev --owner renderer`): NEUTRAL by the runner, a loss by the rule.
- Renderer 3.290 → 3.389 ms (+2.6 %, worse 3/4, cv 3/3 %; +4.1 % against the others, lower 0/4).
- Pre-render -2.5 % (2/4), logic +2.4 %, spatial -2.1 %, physics -0.6 %.
- Load keys within 0.7 %.

**One CPU trace a side** (8 s warm-up, a 6 s window, the same tree as each side):
- A: `pack_sprites_keyed` 94 ms/s, 31 % of Pixi's 300 ms/s busy; `updateBuffer` 20 ms/s.
- B: `pack_sprites_keyed_scatter` 102 ms/s, 32 % of 316.
- At crowd 1.5 (23 500 rows) the pack takes about 1.5 ms a frame in the worker against about 0.15 ms for its kernel at that size. The read order is not why.

**Reverted** in 3167b9ee. What is left of E-193:
- Whether that time is the Pixi thread's CPU at all. A sampled profile counts a preempted thread's stack, as it counts Atomics.wait; check the thread's CPU time on Windows.
- Then the pose and slot streams written by pre-render, or E-201 (poses read by key on the GPU, no gather).

records.title: N-128 fixed (fixedFps by deadline) and N-129's pins fixed; its lost impacts open
records.text:
**N-128 fixed and N-129's first half fixed, on `fix/n128-n129`.** Nothing timed: bug fixes, each with a test that fails before it.

- **N-128 (01842774).** fixedFps scheduled `setInterval(loop, 1000 / fps)`, and timers take whole milliseconds (WebIDL `long`). 60 asked for 16 ms and ran at 62.5 frames a second, with dt fixed at 1/60: the simulation ran about 4 % fast.
  - A worker's `scheduleNextFrame` and the physics host's loop now set a timer to a deadline one period after the last frame's (`src/util/fixedRate.js` `nextFixedDeadline`; the classic host script has its own copy).
  - A timer that fires late is caught up. The first frame, a resume, or a loop more than a frame behind start one period from now, with no burst.
  - Only one frame is pending at a time, as with the interval. `setPresenting` may ask twice.
  - `fixedRate.test.js`: 600 frames under fake timers that take whole ms and fire 0 to 3 ms late run at 60 a second. It fails before the change (setInterval).
  - Not counted in a browser: the rounding is the spec's.
- **N-129, the pins (7ddc9590).** `processImpacts` sent each impact to logic worker `targetId % workers`, while ticks and collision callbacks honour `GameObject.forceProcessOnLogicWorker`. A pinned entity is now shot on its pin's worker; the rest go by the modulo. `impactPins.test.js` runs on the real logic worker and fails before the change.
- **N-129's other half stays open.** The particle worker writes each frame's impacts over the last, and when logic misses a frame those impacts are lost. They need a ring in `wasm/bulletTick.c`, which writes them.

Node 2421 of 2423 in the branch's worktree; the two failures are pixi tests that need node_modules.

records.title: E-193 step 0: the keyed pack's time is Pixi's CPU (284 of 317 ms/s), and it pays for bytes (about 28 000 lines a frame), not their order
records.text:
**E-193 step 0 answered: Pixi's keyed pack time is the thread's own CPU, and what it pays for is bytes, not their order.** 2026-11-11, 04:55 (the trace file's time). Predator `?crowd=1.5` on main (58c61264), headed, source, detailed stats off, a timeline trace (`--trace`): an 8 s warm-up, then a 5 s window.

**CPU against wall.** For each worker thread, the top-level tasks' `tdur` (the thread's CPU) against their `dur` (wall), over the last 5 s:
- Pixi's thread (2 388 tasks): 284 of 317 ms/s.
- Every other worker: 90 to 94 %. For example, 545 of 587 ms/s, 414 of 437, 338 of 366.

So a sampled CPU profile's busy time here is CPU, and the keyed pack's 94 ms/s (R-0864) is CPU too.

**Why then ten times its kernel.** The machine is a Ryzen 7 4800H: 8 cores in two complexes of 4, each with 4 MB of L3. Per frame, at 23 500 rows, `pack_sprites_keyed`:
- reads about 21 bytes a row that pre-render has just written: x, y, rotC, rotS, key, type, about 0.5 MB;
- writes 36: the pose 16, the slot pair 8 and E-191's shadow terms 12, about 0.85 MB, over lines that other work has evicted since the frame before.

That is about 28 000 lines from outside Pixi's caches. At about 50 ns each, that is about 1.4 ms, whatever the order: the scatter (R-0864) changed the order and not the time. The kernel repeats one frame with everything in its own cache.

**What would pay is fewer bytes:**
- the slot pair without its depth (E-186);
- the shadow terms only for the rows that cast, and none on a frame whose sun pass does not run;
- a pose only for a row that moved.

Pre-render cannot write these streams in Predator: Pixi sorts the painter's order there (`sortSprites: 'pixi'`, `packGpuSprites: 'pixi'`).

records.title: E-211 kept: the sun pass draws pre-render's keyed rows, Pixi's keyed pack writes no shadow terms for it; Predator crowd 1.5 renderer -4.5 % (1/4)
records.text:
**E-211 kept: the sun pass draws pre-render's keyed rows, and Pixi's keyed pack writes the shadow terms only for a sun pass that will draw its instances. Predator `?crowd=1.5` renderer -4.5 % (worse 1/4).** 2026-11-11, from 13:57 (the sitting's first result file) to 14:02. Chrome, headed, source, detailed stats off, AC power. The owner's Chrome used about 0.4 of a core throughout. No other session was benching.

**Why.** R-0867 found that the keyed pack pays for bytes. E-191's step 1 had the sun pass draw the entity batch's keyed instances. So every frame the pack:
- gathered each sprite's shadowH, offX and offY in the painter's order;
- wrote 12 bytes a slot, which were then copied and uploaded.

Pre-render meanwhile packs keyed sun rows every frame anyway (E-191 step 2, E-192), because the stamps are cut from them: 28 bytes a caster, read in the queue's order. In Predator Pixi left those rows unused.

**The change** (`f508c2ed`; sat as 9d507cc6, the same tree):
- The sun pass draws pre-render's keyed rows when the frame has them.
- It draws the instances only on frames without them.
- The pack writes their shadow terms only when the next frame's sun pass will draw the instances: no keyed rows, the pass not skipped by `shadowUpdateInterval`, the layer shown.

**Probe first** (f3b22400: the instances never drawn).
- 4 pairs, 13:28 to 13:35: two pairs ran every worker 10 to 15 % high on the B side (drift). In the other two the renderer read -1.7 and -5.6 % while the other workers rose.
- One CPU trace a side, twice (8 s warm-up, 6 s):
  - `pack_sprites_keyed` 79 and 119 → 59 and 57 ms/s;
  - `updateBuffer` 20 and 25 → 27 and 26 ms/s (the rows go up at 28 bytes a caster).

**The change, Predator `?crowd=1.5`, 4 pairs** (`--vs e75004cb --hyp-rev 9d507cc6 --full-rev --owner renderer`): **KEPT (product).**
- Renderer 3.390 → 3.275 ms (-4.5 %, worse 1/4, cv 5/2 %; -3.9 % against the others, lower 4/4). Pairs: -11.4, -3.5, -5.5, +0.8 %; in pair 1 every worker ran lower on B.
- Logic -3.7 %, spatial +0.1 %, physics -1.0 %, pre-render -0.3 %.
- Load keys within 0.2 %.

**Checks.**
- The sun shadows look the same on both sides (`?hour=10&zoom=1`, the post-warm-up frame).
- `keyedSunStream.test.js`: the stream is on only before a pass that will draw the instances, including with `shadowUpdateInterval` 2 and the layer hidden.
- `instancedSpriteKeyed.test.js`: the keyed batch's stream turned off writes nothing; turned back on, it writes the slots' terms.

Left in E-193: the slot pair's depth (E-186), and a pose only for a row that moved.

records.title: N-113 fixed: the visible particle list published in three copies; 24 048 of 24 055 collects torn before, 0 after; particleIntegrateStressScene NEUTRAL
records.text:
**N-113 fixed (`e9d9aa08`): the visible particle list is published in three copies, so pre-render never reads one the particle worker is writing. Hygiene keep.** 2026-11-11, from 14:22 (the sitting's first result file) to 14:27. Chrome, headed, source, detailed stats off, AC power.

**The bug.** The list kernel rewrote `visibleParticlesData` in the particle memory every frame, while pre-render's `collectVisibleParticles` walked it on its own loop. A read that overlapped a write mixed the two lists: an index twice, another missing. A missing particle is not drawn that frame, and an additive one drawn twice flashes.

**The fix.** N-112's published list (`publishedList.js`), as a region of the particle memory:
- a header and three copies, each with room for the kernel's slot past the count (`bindPublishedList` takes a byte and the extra room);
- the particle worker gives the kernel the byte of a copy pre-render does not hold, and publishes that copy once the kernel returns;
- pre-render takes the published copy each frame;
- the debug panel peeks at its count.

**Correctness.** `visibleListTear.test.js` gains a particle case. A real particle worker in its own thread writes the list as fast as it goes, with the camera alternating between two views. A real pre-render, bound by its own init path, collects it as fast as it goes. Every collect must be one view's list whole.
- Before (the same test on main's `src`): 24 048 of 24 055 collects torn (374 936 lists written).
- After: 0 of 486 torn (8 518 lists written, 300 changes of view seen).

The tests that handed pre-render one list now hand it a published one: `particleSortKey`, `renderOnlyQueueRows`, the lists parity and the wide pool layout.

**Cost.** particleIntegrateStressScene `?maxParticles=200000`, 4 pairs (`--vs b5859a00 --hyp-rev e9d9aa08 --full-rev --owner particle`): NEUTRAL.
- Particle 3.242 → 3.204 ms (-1.6 %, worse 1/4, cv 1/1 %). Pairs: -3.0, -0.6, -2.5, +2.9 %.
- Pre-render 6.969 → 6.982 ms (+0.7 %, worse 3/4, cv 2/3 %). Pairs: -7.6, +1.3, +0.4, +1.0 %.
- 198 000 particles live on both sides; render queue within 0.1 %.

No primary is 3 % worse: a hygiene keep.

records.title: N-136 fixed: the active particle list published in three copies; 1 420 of 3 324 takes torn before, 0 after; particleIntegrateStressScene NEUTRAL
records.text:

records.title: E-186 kept as hygiene: a slot is its statics row alone, the depth no batch read gone; Predator crowd 1.5 renderer -2.3 % (NEUTRAL)
records.text:
**E-186 kept as hygiene: a keyed or indexed frame's slot is its statics row alone, without the depth no batch read.** 2026-11-11, from 14:59 (the sitting's first result file) to 15:03. Chrome, headed, source, detailed stats off, AC power.

**The premise.** Every InstancedSpriteBatch Pixi makes draws with `depthTest: false`: the entities, their glow, the cookie and caster batches, and the custom layers'. So the depth in the slot pair only reached `gl_Position.z`, inside the clip volume. Every frame:
- Pixi's keyed pack wrote it (4 of its 24 bytes a sprite), and so did pre-render's indexed pack;
- it was copied and uploaded.

**The change** (`29a6cf35`):
- `SLOT_FLOATS` 1 in gpuPack.c, with the depth stores gone (`invDepthDenom` stays in the exports' signatures, unused).
- `GPU_INDEXED_SLOT_FLOATS` 1.
- `in float aInstSlot`, with `aInstDepth` a constant 0 (GLSL and WGSL).
- The slot attributes as `float32`, the keyed caster rows' too (their key at offset 8).
- The kernels' and batches' tests now check the row alone.

**Kernel**, in Chrome 157 (`chromeKernel.mjs --module /tests/bench/gpuPackKeyedMicrobench.mjs`, 23 500 rows, 42 633 entities, 121 frames, main and the branch alternating, 3 runs each): keyed 0.14 / 0.15 / 0.14 ms → 0.14 / 0.14 / 0.14 ms. With everything in cache the bytes do not show, as E-193 found.

**E-189 kept: a sprite whose texture alone changed sends its row and texture, 8 bytes instead of 64. Predator `?crowd=1.5` renderer -10.7 % (worse 0/4).** 2026-11-11, from 15:33 (the sitting's first result file) to 15:36. Chrome, headed, source, detailed stats off, AC power.

**The premise** (R-0813). Every keyed mark of a steady Predator frame is an animation's step, which changes the texture alone. Each sent a 64-byte update, and to write it the pack gathered the row's eleven statics columns. At crowd 1.5 that is about 1 100 rows a frame.

**The change** (`16fe185c`).
- **The emit** marks such a sprite with KEY_TEX_ONLY beside KEY_CHANGED. Causes: the clock's step, a wrapped frame, a texture that moved since the emit before.
- **keyedDirty** carries two bits: 1 (what the setters write: every static), and 2 (the persist path's clock and repairs: the texture alone, an atomic or beside the setters' stores).
- **A repeating sprite** still sends its row whole, since its tile multiplier follows the frame's size.
- **The keyed pack** writes a texture-only row as a texture update (its row, its texture's float bits) into a region of its own (`pixiKeyTexUpdates`). Without that region, the row goes up whole as before.
- **Pixi's statics scatter** draws each texture update as one texel, the second of its row, with the blue channel alone written. The indexed program is untouched.
- **Every key reader** masks both bits.

**Kernel** (`5aae5fe6`: `gpuPackKeyedMicrobench`'s `marked: 'texture'`). 23 500 rows, 42 633 entities, a twentieth of the rows changed a frame. Chrome 157, main with the tool against the change, 3 runs each:
- keyed 0.170 / 0.165 / 0.180 → 0.145 / 0.155 / 0.155 ms;
- 1 336 whole updates a frame → 199 whole and 1 137 texture updates.

**The scatter on WebGL2** (a one-off probe through `chromeKernel.mjs`, not committed). A statics texture of known words takes full and texture updates, then is read back: 0 of 49 152 words wrong, the color mask back to all four channels, no GL error.

**Correctness in Node.** `preRenderEmitWasm.test.js` replays Pixi's texture from the keys, writing a texture-only mark's word alone, and finds every row's statics there. In its animated case, 143 to 234 of a frame's 196 to 287 marks are the texture alone. `gpuPackKeyed`, `instancedSpriteKeyed` and `gpuPackKeyedPixi` cover the pack, the batch and Pixi's path.

**Predator `?crowd=1.5`, 4 pairs** (`--vs 5aae5fe6 --hyp-rev 16fe185c --full-rev --owner renderer`): **KEPT (product).**
- Renderer 3.315 → 2.969 ms (-10.7 %, worse 0/4, cv 4/3 %; -8.2 % against the others, lower 4/4). Pairs: -12.7, -4.6, -8.8, -16.3 %.
- Pre-render 4.906 → 4.952 ms (-0.9 %, worse 2/4).
- Logic -4.0 %, spatial -2.8 %, physics -2.4 %.
- Load within 0.5 %.

**Not the plan's form.** The plan named a per-key texture-id texture that the indexed program would read. The masked texel write keeps the program as it was and adds no texture fetch.
